雅思口语 6.5 分 学习路线

从零开始到 6.5 分，按以下顺序学习。总时间约 80 分钟通读一遍，之后每天挑 1-2 个主题练习说。

1

看规律框架 10 分钟

  • 理解 Part1/Part2/Part3 各自的答题结构
  • 不需要背，只需理解"总论点 - 举例 - 递进"这个模式
2

读五篇故事 40 分钟

  • 故事一"成都四年"：覆盖 14 个主题
  • 故事二"身边的人与事"：覆盖 18 个主题
  • 故事三"从家到城市"：覆盖 23 个主题
  • 故事四"数字时代"：覆盖 23 个主题
  • 故事五"成长之路"：覆盖 27 个主题
  • 五篇故事共覆盖约 100 个雅思口语主题，重点是熟悉故事脉络，不是逐字背诵
3

掌握语料 15 分钟

  • 句型框架里的句型和连接词模板
  • 标蓝的短语是在故事中出现过的，重点记这些
4

对照提升路径 5 分钟

  • 6 分到 6.5 分的 5 个关键动作
  • 8 组词汇升级对照表
  • 4 组 6 分 vs 7 分范文详细对比
5

记语块 持续

  • 语块库里有 348 个按主题分类的完整语块，整块记忆
  • 优先背你考试可能遇到的：Headphone、Clothing、Art、Films
  • 标蓝的短语是在故事中出现的，结合故事记更高效
总时间：约 80 分钟通读一遍。之后：每天挑 1-2 个主题练习说。

规律框架

📝阅读建议：10分钟浏览，理解即可，不需要背。重点掌握"总论点-举例-递进"模式。

Part1/Part2/Part3 通用回答结构与思路展开模式。理解即可，不需要背诵。

本框架基于 16个雅思口语话题、111个问题、331组思路角度 的 6 分与 7 分范文数据分析， 提取出 Part 1 和 Part 2&3 的通用回答框架、句子逻辑模式和思路展开策略。

Part 1 通用回答框架

Part 1 四步回答结构 Part 1

Part 1 问题通常较短（如 "Do you like art?"），回答应控制在 4-6 句、30-50 词。 数据显示 7 分范文的平均句长约 19 词，核心结构为 "立场 → 原因 → 举例 → 让步/补充"。

1
立场声明 — 明确回答 Yes / No / Depends
用态度副词 + 核心动词直接给出立场，不绕弯子
7分范例：Absolutely, I'm quite passionate about art... / To be honest, I'm not really into... / It really depends on...
2
核心原因 — Because / Since + 具体理由
紧跟一个 because 从句，给出最直接的理由
7分范例：...because it allows people to express complex emotions and thoughts in ways that words sometimes can't.
3
举例扩展 — For instance / On weekends / Such as
用个人经历或具体场景支撑观点，增加细节
7分范例：On weekends, I often visit local galleries—it's become my go-to activity for unwinding...
4
让步或补充 — Although / Even though / On top of that
先退一步再转折，或追加一个递进观点，展示思维深度
7分范例：Although I'm not skilled at drawing or painting myself, I deeply admire the imagination and hard work artists put into their creations.
Part 1 核心原则：每句话都有明确功能——第1句给立场，第2句给原因，第3句给例子，第4句做让步或补充。 不要只堆砌 "I like... because... and... so..." 的扁平结构。
Part 1 句子逻辑模式分析
逻辑层功能7分常用连接词示例
立场层 直接回答问题 Absolutely / To be honest / Personally / Well "Absolutely, I'm quite passionate about..."
因果层 解释为什么 because / since / — (直接接从句) "...because it allows people to express complex emotions"
举例层 用具体场景支撑 For instance / On weekends / Such as / Especially "On weekends, I often visit local galleries"
让步层 展示多角度思考 Although / Even though / While / That said "Although I'm not skilled at drawing myself, I deeply admire..."
递进层 追加补充观点 On top of that / Plus / Also / Not only...but also "On top of that, I often watch films in their original English version"

Part 2&3 通用回答框架

Part 2 描述题五步结构 Part 2

Part 2 要求 1-2 分钟独白，7 分范文平均句长约 20 词。核心结构为 "引入 → 主体描述(What/When/Where) → 细节扩展 → 感受/意义 → 收束"。

1
引入话题 — I'd like to talk about...
用固定句式引入，直接点题
7分范例：I'd like to talk about my cousin, who's a software engineer at a leading global tech firm.
2
主体描述 — 回答 You should say 提示点
按提示卡逐一展开，每个点 1-2 句，用 When / Where / What 连接
7分范例：It was a thoughtful surprise from my best friend—she'd secretly ordered it online and arranged for it to be delivered right to my doorstep.
3
细节扩展 — 具体化、画面化
加入感官细节、情感反应、转折点
7分范例：The moment she walked in and saw all her closest friends waiting for her, her eyes lit up and she started tearing up from happiness.
4
感受/意义 — And explain how/why
回答最后一个提示点，升华感受或意义
7分范例：What made it truly special wasn't just the taste—it was the fact that I'd been away at university for months, and this cake was her quiet, heartfelt way of saying she missed me.
5
收束 — 自然结尾
用一句话总结，避免突然结束
7分范例：Everyone stayed well past the scheduled end time, chatting and laughing—it was clear the event had truly brought joy, which made me feel incredibly proud.
Part 3 讨论题三层论证结构 Part 3

Part 3 问题偏抽象（如 "How can we solve traffic jams?"），需要展示分析和论证能力。 核心结构为 "观点 → 论证(因果+举例) → 让步或对比"，比 Part 1 更强调逻辑完整性。

1
观点层 — In my opinion / I believe that
给出核心观点或方案，比 Part 1 更正式
7分范例：In my opinion, enhancing public transportation is the most effective long-term solution to traffic congestion.
2
论证层 — 因果链 + 条件句 + 举例
用 If...then 因果链 + For instance / Take...as an example 举例
7分范例：When public transit is convenient, affordable, and reliable, people are far more likely to leave their cars at home. Take Tokyo or Singapore as examples: despite being densely populated, their well-well-connected networks keep road traffic surprisingly manageable.
3
让步/对比层 — While / That said / On the other hand
承认对立面或补充条件，展示辩证思维
7分范例：While such measures may face initial public resistance, they've proven over time to significantly ease traffic flow and even improve air quality.

Part 1 vs Part 2&3 结构差异

维度Part 1Part 2&3
回答长度4-6句，30-50词Part2: 8-12句，100-150词；Part3: 5-8句，60-100词
平均句长~19词~20词（略长，含更多从句嵌套）
核心结构立场→原因→举例→让步Part2: 引入→描述→细节→感受→收束；Part3: 观点→论证→让步
立场表达Absolutely / To be honest（口语化）In my opinion / I believe that（更正式）
举例方式On weekends / For instance（个人经历）Take...as an example / Such as（可引用城市/案例）
逻辑深度单层因果即可需要因果链 + 条件句 + 让步对比
连接词偏好Also / Plus / Because（口语化）Moreover / Since / While / That said（更正式）
思路角度Yes / No / Depends 三选一多方案并列（方案A + 方案B + 方案C）

思路展开模式

数据统计显示，331 个思路角度的标题分布如下：

模式数量占比适用场景
Yes 开头4915%Part1 偏好题，直接肯定
No 开头309%Part1 不偏好题，直接否定
Depends / 中性309%视情况而定的题，展示辩证思维
方案/角度型22267%Part2&3 多角度展开，如 "Public Transport Solution" / "Urban Planning"
三角度模式（Part 1 核心）：几乎所有 Part 1 问题都提供三个思路角度—— 肯定（Yes）、否定（No）、中性（Depends/Sometimes）。 考生应选择最接近自己真实体验的角度，而非背诵"标准答案"。 例如 "Do you like art?" 提供：Yes-Passionate / No-Not Interested / Sometimes-Selective。
多方案并列模式（Part 3 核心）：Part 3 问题通常提供 3 个不同角度的解决方案或观点， 考生可以选择其中一个深入展开，也可以综合多个角度。 例如 "How can we solve traffic jams?" 提供：Public Transport / Remote Work / Smart Policies。

框架记忆卡片

从真实题目中提炼的可复用回答框架，直接调用即可。

🎧
When should people not wear headphones?
Three-dimension structure
回答公式
场景定义 → 原因 → 举例
⚠ 人身安全 Safety-Critical
crossing street / cycling / traffic / announcements
切断预警 = 听不到喇叭声
👥 社交职场 Social/Professional
meetings / dinners / customer service
耳机 = 社交隔离信号
🎯 全神贯注 Full Attention
lectures / machinery / emergencies
耳机 = 注意力分流
核心逻辑：耳机功能是隔绝声音 → 找隔绝声音会产生负面后果的场景 → 从生理安全到社会关系再到任务效能，层层递进
三段展开公式：场景 → 为什么不行 → 具体例子

语块与句型

📝阅读建议：按需查阅，优先看你考试可能遇到的主题。不要从头背到尾——整块记忆，整块调用。

按主题分类的完整语块，每个都是能直接拿出来说的预制件。下方"句型框架"给你搭骨架的句型。

语块 = 内容性表达
描述具体事物的完整短语，让你的回答有"料"
如 noise-cancelling headphones, an immersive art installation
句型框架 = 框架性表达 →
组织语言结构的句型，让你的回答有"型"
如 What surprised me was..., On top of that...

一、核心短语（按功能分类）

表达态度与喜好

be really into—很喜欢
be quite passionate about—对...充满热情
aren't really my thing—不是我的菜
appreciate both—两者都欣赏
care deeply about—深切关心

描述体验与感受

go-to place—首选去处
inner world—内心世界
a sense of being surrounded by life—被生活环绕的感觉
at peace—平静
caught us off guard—出乎意料
a small revelation—小小的顿悟

展开与连接

What makes it special is...—让它特别的是...
What surprised me was...—令我惊讶的是...
What I love most is...—我最喜欢的是...
it's not just about X—it's about Y—不仅仅是X——而是Y
Looking back,...—回想起来...

因果与反思

carry the weight of—承载...的重量
represent the payoff of—代表...的回报
make a real difference—产生真正的改变
sink in without you even noticing—在不知不觉中沉淀
gradually fades into—逐渐淡成

二、句子结构模板

结构1：立场 + 原因 + 举例
I'm really into X because [reason]. I often [example]—it's become my [expression].
结构2：让步 + 转折
While I deeply admire X, I don't see myself [doing Y]. My strengths lie more in Z.
结构3：What 强调句
What surprised me was that... / What made it special wasn't X, but Y.
结构4：Not... but... 对比
It's not about X, but rather Y. / Not rote memorization, but natural exploration.
结构5：条件 + 自然结果
When you encounter the same patterns over and over, they sink in without you even noticing.

三、连接词使用模式

逻辑层连接词示例
立场Honestly / Absolutely / I'd sayHonestly, while I admire artists...
举例For example / For instance / Including...including one set in the Roman Colosseum
递进What's more / Plus / AlsoPlus, going with friends changes everything
转折While / But / That saidWhile I respect talent, I don't feel connected
反思Looking back / It taught me / It made me realizeIt taught me that repetition is powerful

故事总览 · 五篇完整叙事与关键词

一页通读全部故事 + 重点表达清单。每篇故事后附关键词分析和主题覆盖（按 Part 1 / Part 2&3 分组）。下方的分主题练习有空再看。

Part 1 · 日常问答
  • 形式：考官逐题简短问答，无 Cue Card；每话题约 4 题
  • 题型示例（Art）：Do you like art? / Do you like visiting art galleries? / Do you want to be an artist? / Do you like modern art or traditional art?
  • 答题量：每题 2-4 句，总时长约 4-5 分钟
  • 话题范围：个人日常（习惯、偏好、生活环境），38 个大陆题 + 3 个非大陆题
  • 答题策略：先给明确立场（Yes/No/Sometimes），再给 1-2 句理由或例子展开
  • 语言特点：自然口语、日常词汇、一般现在时为主
  • 故事用法：提取叙事中"我喜欢…/我常去…"式的个人表达，直接用于 Yes 类回答
Part 2 & 3 · 叙事与讨论
  • Part 2 形式：1 张 Cue Card 独白，1 分钟准备 + 1-2 分钟讲述
  • Cue Card 结构：Describe... + You should say:（4 个要点：what/how learned/who benefits/how you feel）
  • Part 3 形式：6 个 follow-up 讨论题，抽象/社会性话题，每题 4-6 句
  • Part 3 题型示例：What kinds of rules do schools have? / Do you think school rules are important? / What is the purpose of punishment?
  • 答题策略：Part 2 覆盖全部要点（开头→主体→结尾）；Part 3 观点 + 理由 + 举例 + 对比
  • 语言特点：叙事短语、评价性语言、复杂句式、过去时（Part 2）/ 一般现在时（Part 3）
  • 故事用法：Part 2 提取经历描述段和叙事弧线；Part 3 提取观点评价句和论证结构

故事一：成都四年

大学时在成都接触艺术，也形成了跟着绿灯方向长时间散步的习惯；散步和在植物中间休息还能直接回答“低花费一天”。天府艺术公园同时覆盖公园和建筑；杭州小旅店窗外的普通街道回答 View；黄河与福州分别覆盖河流和旅行类题目。

覆盖 14 个主题（Part 1: 8 · Part 2&3: 6）
📖 完整故事 · Full Story story

I'm really into art, especially painting and sculpture. For me, painting is fascinating because you can see someone's inner world through their lines and colors—everyone's palette is completely different. I used to visit the Chengdu Art Museum on weekends; it's become my go-to place for unwinding. Last time, I tried three VR experiences, including one set in the Roman Colosseum and another on the Titanic. It was incredibly immersive. Sculpture, for me, carries the weight of history—it reminds me that incredibly skilled people actually existed in those eras. What I love most is how museums bring history to life. As a kid, history felt like just memorizing dates and names, but growing up I realized it's about real people and their stories, which changed everything.

中文翻译 ▶

我很喜欢艺术，尤其是绘画和雕塑。绘画迷人的地方在于你能透过线条和色彩看到一个人的内心世界——每个人的调色板都完全不同。我大学时周末常去成都美术馆，它已经成了我放松的首选去处。上次体验了三个VR项目，包括设定在罗马斗兽场和泰坦尼克号的。沉浸感极强。雕塑对我来说承载着历史的重量——它提醒我那些时代确实存在过技艺非凡的人。我最喜欢的是博物馆让历史活起来的方式。小时候觉得历史就是背日期和人名，长大后意识到历史是关于真实的人和他们的故事，这改变了一切。

When I felt stressed in my first two years at university, I would sometimes walk for two or three hours. I would simply follow the green lights and see where they took me. After a while, the traffic noise fades into a soft background hum, and the walk helps me clear my head after a long day. I do not need a destination; walking gives my thoughts room to settle.

中文翻译 ▶

大学前两年压力很大时，我有时会一口气走两三个小时。我就跟着绿灯走，看看它会把我带到哪里。走了一会儿，车流声会淡成柔和的背景嗡鸣，散步能帮我在漫长的一天后清空脑子。我不需要目的地；走路会让思绪慢慢安定下来。

My favorite low-cost day is equally simple. I walk for a long time, then sit in a park surrounded by plants. If the weather is nice, I may even doze off for a while in the park. It costs nothing, but I feel rested afterwards. The best part is the quiet time outdoors, not saving money.

中文翻译 ▶

我最喜欢的低花费一天也很简单：走很久，再坐在被植物包围的公园里。天气好时，我甚至会在公园里打个盹。完全不花钱，但之后会觉得很放松。最好的部分是那段安静的户外时光，而不是省下了多少钱。

One important river I have visited is the Yellow River. It has supported Chinese civilization, farming, and daily life for a very long time. What I remember personally is the clean wet sand: if I pressed it hard, it became firm, but if I touched it gently, it felt soft. That made the river feel like a real place rather than only a name from history books.

中文翻译 ▶

我去过的一条重要河流是黄河。它长期支持着中华文明、农业和日常生活。我个人记得最清楚的是干净的湿沙：用力按时会变硬，轻轻摸时又很软。这让黄河对我而言不只是历史书里的名字，而是一个真实去过的地方。

One park I particularly like is Tianfu Art Park. It has lakes, green open spaces, and art buildings, so people can walk around the lakes, rest on the grass, take photos, and visit exhibitions. I like that nature, architecture, and art exist in the same place without needing separate stories.

中文翻译 ▶

我特别喜欢的一个公园是天府艺术公园。那里有湖、开阔绿地和美术馆建筑，人们可以沿湖散步、在草地休息、拍照和看展。自然、建筑和艺术都在同一个地方，因此不需要为这些题目再背几套故事。

I am currently staying in a hotel in Hangzhou. From the window, I can see an ordinary street and several buildings, with cars and people passing by. I have not lived there long enough to notice long-term changes, so I mainly see small daily changes in traffic and weather.

中文翻译 ▶

我目前住在杭州的一家旅店。从窗外能看到一条普通街道和几栋楼，车辆和行人会经过。我住的时间还不够长，看不出长期变化，因此主要看到车流和天气每天的小变化。

I like many kinds of food. One strong memory is shrimp balls covered in a tasty sauce at a University of Sheffield event in the Ritz-Carlton. I also enjoy food from other cultures, especially Thai food. I avoid food that is too oily or extremely spicy, because heavy flavours can cover the taste of the ingredients.

中文翻译 ▶

我喜欢很多种食物。一段鲜明记忆是在丽思卡尔顿参加谢菲尔德大学活动时，吃到裹着美味酱汁的虾球。我也喜欢其他文化的食物，尤其是泰餐。我不喜欢过于油腻或特别辣的食物，因为太重的味道会盖住食材本身。

I once took a family trip to Fuzhou, a coastal city in southern China. As someone from the dry north, the humid air, green mountains and sea felt completely new to me. My favorite photo shows clouds resting halfway up the mountains, with the sea behind them. We also had fresh seafood by the sea. That trip made me want to see more places where mountains meet the coast.

中文翻译 ▶

我去过福州的家庭旅行，它是中国南方的一座沿海城市。作为在干燥北方长大的人，湿润的空气、绿色的山和大海都让我觉得很新鲜。我最喜欢的一张照片里，云停在半山腰，身后就是大海。我们还吃了在海边吃到的新鲜海鲜。那次旅行让我想去看更多山海相连的地方。

▶ ⭐ 核心原型（优先记忆） (10个原型)

▶ 堂哥辞职学法律 克服困难成功的人

I'd like to talk about my cousin, who is someone I deeply admire for his sheer determination. He used to work at a bank — a stable, well-paying job that most people would consider ideal. However, he always felt unfulfilled and secretly harbored a passion for law.

About five years ago, he made the bold decision to resign from the bank and devote himself entirely to preparing for the national judicial examination. This exam is notoriously difficult, with a pass rate of barely ten percent. He spent nearly two years studying on his own, often from dawn until midnight, without any formal classroom instruction. There were moments when he doubted himself, especially when close friends questioned whether he was making a reckless mistake.

But he persevered against all odds and passed the exam on his second attempt. Today, he's not only a licensed lawyer but also manages a team at a law firm. His journey taught me that success isn't about having the easiest path — it's about having the courage to pursue what truly matters to you, even when the odds are stacked against you.

我想谈谈我的堂哥，他是我非常敬佩的人，因为他的纯粹毅力。他以前在银行工作——一份稳定、高薪的工作，大多数人都会觉得是理想选择。然而，他总觉得不满足，内心深处一直怀有对法律的热情。

大约五年前，他做出了一个大胆的决定：从银行辞职，全身心投入备战国家司法考试。这个考试以难度著称，通过率仅百分之十左右。他花了将近两年时间自学，经常从清晨学到深夜，没有任何正式的课堂指导。有时候他会自我怀疑，尤其是亲密的朋友质疑他是否在做一个鲁莽的错误决定时。

但他排除万难坚持了下来，第二次参加考试时通过了。如今，他不仅是一名执业律师，还在律所管理一个团队。他的经历让我明白，成功不在于走最轻松的路——而在于有勇气追求真正重要的事，即使困难重重。

可覆盖主题：克服困难成功的人
▶ 贝壳形巧克力 Gifts / 礼物

I cannot clearly remember the most recent gift, but one gift I remember well is a box of shell-shaped chocolates from my childhood. I later bought the same kind again, but it did not taste the same as it did when I was a child.

我记不清最近一次收到的礼物，但很记得小时候收到过一盒贝壳形巧克力。后来我又买过同一种，但再也没有小时候吃到的味道。

可覆盖主题：Gifts / 礼物
▶ 半夜骑共享单车被狗追 自行车/摩托车/汽车旅行

I'd like to talk about a night-time bike ride I took. I was riding a shared bike from Taikoo Li back to my school in the suburbs. It was already midnight, and the navigation app directed me through a long-abandoned residential area.

The streetlights were all off. The buildings had been empty for a long time. Halfway through, a fierce dog started chasing me, barking aggressively. There was not a single person around, only the occasional car passing by. Every time something passed, or when there was complete silence, I thought I was going to die.

I eventually made it back to school safely. After that experience, all I could think about was gratitude for living in a peaceful country. That night ride taught me more about fear and gratitude than any comfortable daytime trip ever could.

我想说一次深夜骑行的经历。我当时从太古里骑共享单车回郊区的学校。已经半夜了，导航把我导进了一片荒废很久的住宅区。

路灯都不开。那些楼空了很久。半路突然有只狗追着我叫。周围一个人也没有，偶尔有车经过。每次有东西经过，或者完全没有任何东西经过的时候，我都以为自己要死了。

我拼命骑。最后终于回到了学校。到了那一刻，满脑子都是感恩和平国家。这次骑行让我记住的是那种原始的恐惧，以及安全到达后强烈的庆幸感。

可覆盖主题：自行车/摩托车/汽车旅行
▶ 蔡徐坤Prada粉色三角香水广告 名人广告

I'd like to talk about Cai Xukun's advertisement for Prada. It was for a pink triangle-shaped perfume, and honestly, I only found out about that perfume because of him.

I saw the ad on social media. The visual was striking — a bright pink bottle with a triangular design, and the celebrity endorsing it with that signature style. The celebrity effect was so strong that the product became instantly recognisable. Before seeing the ad, I had no idea this fragrance existed. After seeing it, I could immediately picture the bottle and associate it with the brand.

What made this ad memorable was how effectively it connected a celebrity's image to a product. It was not about the scent itself — it was about the star power making a product unforgettable. That said, I am aware that celebrity endorsements can be misleading, so I would still research independently before buying.

我想说的是蔡徐坤的Prada广告。那是一款粉色三角形香水，说实话，我就是因为他才知道那款香水的。

我在社交媒体上看到了这条广告。画面很醒目——粉色三角形瓶身，加上名人以标志性风格代言。名人效应太强了，产品立刻变得辨识度极高。在看广告之前，我完全不知道这款香水的存在。看了之后，我立刻就能想象出瓶身并把它和品牌联系起来。

这条广告让人印象深刻的地方在于它如何有效地把名人形象和产品联系在一起。重点不是香味本身——而是明星光环让产品令人难忘。不过我也知道名人代言可能有误导性，所以买之前我还是会自己做研究。

可覆盖主题：名人广告
▶ Rapper朋友音乐会帮忙化妆 不享受的音乐活动

I'd like to talk about a music event I attended. A rapper friend asked me to do his makeup for a concert he was organizing, with various guest performers.

I ended up doing makeup not just for him but for all the guest performers, so I was backstage helping out and watching the show. The music was loud rap, and honestly I'm not particularly fond of noisy rap. Plus, I had to stand the entire time, which was exhausting.

I have to say, I equally dislike any event that requires standing for a long time. It is not about the music — it is about physical discomfort. I was happy to help a friend, but I would not choose to attend that kind of event on my own.

我想说一次音乐活动的经历。一个说唱的朋友托我去给他化妆，他自己开了场音乐会，还有各种嘉宾。

结果我不仅给他化了妆，还给其他嘉宾也都化了。所以我是在后台帮忙，然后顺便看演出。音乐是很大声的说唱，说实话我并不是特别喜欢聒噪的rap。而且全程都得站着，太累了。

我得说，我平等地不喜欢任何需要一直站着的活动。这不是音乐的问题——是身体不舒服。我很开心能帮朋友，但我不会自己选择去参加那种活动。

可覆盖主题：不享受的音乐活动
▶ 没有发小 发小 / Childhood friend

To be honest, I do not really have a childhood friend. When I was young, I did not have many close friends. I would play with different groups of kids, but I kept moving between different circles, so I never stayed in one group long enough to form a lasting friendship.

It is not something I feel bad about — it is just how things were. I was always meeting new people and then naturally drifting apart. The pattern continued as I grew up, and I have become comfortable with it.

So if the topic asks about a lifelong friend, my honest answer is I do not have one, and that is okay. I value the friendships I have now, even if they started more recently.

说实话，我没有发小。小时候我没什么好朋友，都是跟不同的人一起玩，然后不断地换圈子，从来没有长期待在同一个圈子并建立持久友谊的经历。

这并不是让我难过的事——只是情况如此。我总是在认识新的人然后自然疏远。这个模式一直延续到我长大，我已经习惯了。

所以如果题目问的是从小到大的朋友，我的真实回答是我没有，这也没关系。我珍惜现在的友谊，即使它们开始得比较晚。

可覆盖主题：发小 / Childhood friend
▶ 给年轻语文老师建议 给别人建议 / Giving advice

A memorable occasion was when I gave advice to a young Chinese literature teacher. I felt that classes should be more engaging, especially subjects like literature — if the teacher just lectures in a monologue, students get tired. I suggested that the teacher could have students read aloud more often, or call on students to answer questions, so that everyone feels more involved. When students have more interaction, the classroom becomes more vivid. The teacher actually listened. In the next class there was much more interaction, and I could feel the atmosphere change. What I learned from this is that sometimes a small adjustment can completely change the atmosphere.

我曾给一位年轻的语文老师提过改进课堂活动的建议。我觉得课程应该更有趣，尤其是语文这种课——如果只是默默地自说自话地讲课，同学们会感到疲惫。

我建议老师可以多让学生朗读，或者多挑同学回答问题，这样大家的参与感更强。当同学们有更多互动时，课堂会更生动。

老师真的听了这个建议。下一节课多了很多互动，我能感觉到气氛变了。我从中学到的是有时候一个小的调整就能完全改变氛围。

可覆盖主题：给别人建议 / Giving advice
▶ 学医同学找工作 想从事医疗行业的人

I'd like to talk about a classmate who studied medicine. She chose this path very seriously, but finding a job in medicine is actually quite difficult — the competition is incredibly fierce.

As for whether she wants to continue in this field or whether she can — it depends. The reality is that medical careers require years of additional training and specialization, and the job market is oversaturated in many areas.

What I admire about her is that she went into medicine with genuine dedication, not just for the prestige. She knew it would be hard, but the intensity of the competition was still a surprise. Whether she ends up practicing or pivots to a related field, I respect her commitment to healthcare.

我想说的是一个学医的同学。她很认真地选择了这条路，但学医找工作其实并不容易，竞争太激烈了。

至于她最终能不能从事这行——it depends。就业市场很严峻，很多毕业生竞争有限的岗位。所以即使她努力学习拿到了学位，结果也不是确定的。

我觉得她的情况很有意思的一点是选择一条专业道路并不总能直接通向对应的职业。有时候你为之努力的领域比预想的更复杂，必须保持灵活。

可覆盖主题：想从事医疗行业的人
▶ 姑姑家 喜欢拜访但不想住的家

The home I'd like to talk about is my aunt's house. I love visiting her because she is gentle and caring, almost like a mother to me. Whenever I visit, she makes me feel completely at home, and staying with her is genuinely happy.

However, I would not want to live there long-term. My aunt is incredibly kind and gives so much of herself to the family. She constantly takes on burdens for everyone, and over time I realised that even if I tried to share the load, it would not change the essential problem. Watching someone I love sacrifice so much, continuously and quietly, made me feel overwhelmed. I felt a kind of helplessness that made me want to step away rather than witness it every day.

So while I treasure every visit, I realised I am not someone who can watch a loved one give themselves away like that for the long term. It is not about the house itself — it is about the emotional weight of seeing a kind person pour herself out for others.

我想说的是我姑姑的家。我很喜欢去拜访她，因为她很温柔、很会照顾人，像妈妈一样。每次去她都让我感觉像在自己家一样，住在一起真的很幸福。

但我不想长期住在那里。姑姑太善良了，为家庭付出了太多。她不断承受着各种重担，后来我意识到就算我分担也改变不了本质问题。看着自己爱的人如此不断地消耗自己、默默付出，让我感到很崩溃。那种无力感让我想离开，不愿意每天见证这样的场景。

所以我珍惜每次拜访，但我意识到自己没法长期看着亲人这样奉献自己。这不是房子的问题，而是看到善良的人不断为别人倾注自己的情感重量。

可覆盖主题：喜欢拜访但不想住的家
▶ 做蛋糕 收到特殊蛋糕 / Special cake

I haven't actually received a special cake, but I once made a special cake for my younger brother. This year, his summer holiday started quite late. On the day he came home from Shandong for his summer holiday, I bought the ingredients and made a Basque cheesecake for him.

It was my first time making one, but it came out surprisingly well. The top was dark and slightly burnt, while the middle was soft and creamy, almost like the ones sold in cake shops. My mother thought it was a little too sweet, but I liked it, and my brother was very grateful.

What made it special was that I made it myself to welcome him home, and it turned out perfectly on my first try.

我其实没有收到过特殊蛋糕，但我曾经为弟弟做过一个特别的蛋糕。今年他的暑假放得比较晚。他放暑假从山东回家的当天，我买了食材，给他做了一个巴斯克蛋糕。

那是我第一次做这种蛋糕，但成品意外地非常成功。表面颜色深、略带焦香，中间柔软绵密，和蛋糕店卖的味道差不多。妈妈觉得有点太甜，但我很喜欢，弟弟也非常感谢我。

它特别的地方，是我亲手做它来欢迎弟弟回家，并且第一次尝试就做得很完美。

可覆盖主题：收到特殊蛋糕 / Special cake

▶ 生活日常与环境 (7个原型)

▶ 成都周末/大学艺术生活 A person you enjoy spending time with / Art / Cinema / City / Films / Friend / History / Museum / Place to visit / TV / Travel

I'm really into art, especially painting and sculpture. For me, painting is fascinating because you can see someone's inner world through their lines and colors—everyone's palette is completely different. I used to visit the Chengdu Art Museum on weekends; it's become my go-to place for unwinding. Last time, I tried three VR experiences, including one set in the Roman Colosseum and another on the Titanic. It was incredibly immersive. Sculpture, for me, carries the weight of history—it reminds me that incredibly skilled people actually existed in those eras. What I love most is how museums bring history to life. As a kid, history felt like just memorizing dates and names, but growing up I realized it's about real people and their stories, which changed everything.

我很喜欢艺术，尤其是绘画和雕塑。绘画迷人的地方在于你能透过线条和色彩看到一个人的内心世界——每个人的调色板都完全不同。我大学时周末常去成都美术馆，它已经成了我放松的首选去处。上次体验了三个VR项目，包括设定在罗马斗兽场和泰坦尼克号的。沉浸感极强。雕塑对我来说承载着历史的重量——它提醒我那些时代确实存在过技艺非凡的人。我最喜欢的是博物馆让历史活起来的方式。小时候觉得历史就是背日期和人名，长大后意识到历史是关于真实的人和他们的故事，这改变了一切。

可覆盖主题：Art / History / Museum / Friend / A person you enjoy spending time with / Travel / City / Place to visit
▶ 跟着绿灯散步 Apps / Low-cost day / Parks / Public transport / Quiet Place / Technology / Transport / Walking / Websites

When I felt stressed in my first two years at university, I would sometimes walk for two or three hours. I would simply follow the green lights and see where they took me. After a while, the traffic noise fades into a soft background hum, and the walk helps me clear my head after a long day. I do not need a destination; walking gives my thoughts room to settle.

大学前两年压力很大时，我有时会一口气走两三个小时。我就跟着绿灯走，看看它会把我带到哪里。走了一会儿，车流声会淡成柔和的背景嗡鸣，散步能帮我在漫长的一天后清空脑子。我不需要目的地；走路会让思绪慢慢安定下来。

可覆盖主题：Walking
▶ 低花费一天/公园休息 Walking / Parks / Quiet Place / Low-cost day / Art / History / Museum / Food / Favorite food

My favorite low-cost day is equally simple. I walk for a long time, then sit in a park surrounded by plants. If the weather is nice, I may even doze off for a while in the park. It costs nothing, but I feel rested afterwards. The best part is the quiet time outdoors, not saving money.

我最喜欢的低花费一天也很简单：走很久，再坐在被植物包围的公园里。天气好时，我甚至会在公园里打个盹。完全不花钱，但之后会觉得很放松。最好的部分是那段安静的户外时光，而不是省下了多少钱。

可覆盖主题：Walking / Parks / Quiet Place / Low-cost day / Art / History / Museum / Food / Favorite food
▶ 黄河/河流体验 River / Important river / Friend / A person you enjoy spending time with / Travel / City / Place to visit

One important river I have visited is the Yellow River. It has supported Chinese civilization, farming, and daily life for a very long time. What I remember personally is the clean wet sand: if I pressed it hard, it became firm, but if I touched it gently, it felt soft. That made the river feel like a real place rather than only a name from history books.

我去过的一条重要河流是黄河。它长期支持着中华文明、农业和日常生活。我个人记得最清楚的是干净的湿沙：用力按时会变硬，轻轻摸时又很软。这让黄河对我而言不只是历史书里的名字，而是一个真实去过的地方。

▶ 电影《欢迎来龙餐馆》 A person you enjoy spending time with / Apps / Art / Cinema / Favorite food / Films / Food / Friend / History / Museum / TV / Technology / Websites

The most memorable film I have watched recently is “Welcome to Dragon Restaurant”. It follows a Chinese man who helps run a restaurant in a small country in the Middle East. At first, he sees himself as an outsider to the war. The restaurant survives partly because of help from a local friend and an American soldier, but both of them are later killed. When an officer asks him, “Do you still remember that this war has nothing to do with you?”, he can no longer pretend to be only a spectator.

What shocked me most was that every small chance of hope is destroyed by violence. Even a child is misled into thinking that becoming a human bomb is heroic. The film does not give the audience an easy happy ending. Instead, it makes us feel that no one is completely outside a human tragedy.

最近最让我记得住的电影是《欢迎来龙餐馆》。它讲的是一个中国人在中东一个小国参与经营餐馆。起初，他觉得自己只是战争之外的人。餐馆能维持，一部分靠一位当地朋友和一名美国士兵的帮助，但两人后来都死了。当一位军官问他：“你还记得你和这场战争没有关系吗？”时，他再也不能假装自己只是看客。

最震撼我的是，每一点可能的希望都会被暴力毁掉。甚至有一个孩子被蒙蔽，以为成为人肉炸弹是英雄行为。电影没有给观众一个轻松的大团圆，而是让我们感到，没有人能完全置身于人类的苦难之外。

可覆盖主题：Art / History / Museum / Food / Favorite food / Friend / A person you enjoy spending time with / Websites / Apps / Technology / Films / TV / Cinema

I became more serious about the environment after visiting Baima Fairy Cave in Shanxi. It is a natural cave with rock formations that took thousands of years to form. Even though it was hot outside, I needed a jacket inside. The cave was beautiful, but I saw plastic bottles and food wrappers among the rocks. It made me think that small everyday choices can protect a place or damage it. My grandmother has taught me the same thing: she reuses bags and uses rice-washing water to water her plants.

She composts kitchen waste and uses no chemical pesticides. What moved me most is how she extends her care to the small creatures around her—leaving shallow dishes of water for stray cats and birds in summer. She always reminds me: nature doesn't need our management — it needs our respect. Individual actions create the cultural foundation for broader change.

奶奶也是一个爱护自然的人——她经营菜地近十五年，与自然和谐共处。她把厨余垃圾堆肥，不用化学农药。最让我感动的是她把关爱延伸到周围的小动物身上——夏天放浅碟子给流浪猫和鸟类饮水。她总是提醒我：自然不需要我们的管理——它需要的是我们的尊重。个人行为为更大范围的变革奠定了文化基础。

I use WeChat and Xiaohongshu daily—keeping in touch with friends, checking recommendations, and following IELTS accounts. But I try not to scroll mindlessly for hours. I watch videos on Bilibili and practice IELTS with BBC Learning English. Recently, with AI’s help, I made my own IELTS study website. Its functions and layout fit the way I study, so I use it a lot while preparing. For apps and websites, it is not really an either-or choice: a website can be added to a phone’s home screen and opened just like an app. Apps are often handier because phones are portable and the design fits a small screen. I do not wear a watch because I dislike anything tight around my wrist. I usually check the exact time on a screen, so to me a watch is more of an accessory than a tool. I type a lot because typing is a main way to express myself online. When ideas arrive quickly, I can cut, paste, and reorder my sentences until they make sense. I hardly handwrite now, though it may help with a second round of memory.

每天用微信和小红书——和朋友保持联系、查推荐、关注雅思账号。但尽量不无脑刷几个小时。在B站看视频，用BBC Learning English练雅思。最近，在 AI 的帮助下，我做了自己的雅思学习网站。功能和排列方式更贴合我的学习方式，所以备考时我经常使用。至于 App 和网站，并不真的是二选一：网站也能加到手机主屏幕上，像 App 一样随时打开。App 常常更方便，是因为手机便携、设计也适合小屏幕。我不戴手表，是因为不喜欢手腕上有紧的东西。我通常看屏幕上已经显示好的准确时间，所以对我来说手表更像装饰，而不是工具。我经常打字，因为打字是网络时代重要的表达方式。想法来得快时，我可以剪切、粘贴并调整句子顺序，直到表达清楚。现在我几乎不手写，不过手写可能有助于第二次记忆。

▶ 童年发现《图解经济学》 Favorite food / Food / 雅思口语通用

When I was a child, I stumbled upon a book called "Illustrated Economics" in my parents' bookshelf. I didn't even know what economics meant back then, but it completely rewired how I see the world. The book taught me that economics isn't about calculating limited resources; it's a discipline of imagination. This concept of "having versus having more" rather than "having versus having nothing" raised my baseline for how I use time and energy. Before that framework, every moment felt like a draining choice between doing something and doing nothing. But once I understood opportunity cost, each moment became a choice between creating value and creating even more value—both options lead to growth, and either way, I win. It was like upgrading the operating system of my decision-making at age eight. My grandmother is passionate about growing vegetables on her balcony—tomatoes, green onions, and fresh herbs like cilantro. It keeps her physically active. What she loves most is the satisfaction of nurturing something from seed to harvest—a sense of self-sufficiency. The process itself is therapeutic and stress-relieving.

小时候我在父母书架上偶然发现了一本叫《图解经济学》的书。那时候我甚至不知道经济学是什么意思，但它彻底重构了我看世界的方式。这本书告诉我经济学不是计算有限资源，而是想象力的学科。"有与有更多"而非"有与没有"的概念，提高了我使用时间和精力的基准线。在那个框架之前，每一刻都像在做某事和什么都不做之间的消耗性选择。但一旦理解了机会成本，每一刻都变成了在创造价值和创造更多价值之间的选择——两条路都通向成长，不管怎样我都赢。这就像在我八岁时升级了决策的操作系统。我奶奶热衷于种菜——番茄、小葱和香菜等新鲜香草。这让她保持身体活跃。她最爱的是从种子到收获的培育满足感——自给自足的满足感。过程本身也疗愈和解压。

We prefer physical shops because trying clothes on once is easier than dealing with online returns.

When I felt stressed in my first two years at university, I would sometimes walk for two or three hours. I would simply follow the green lights and see where they took me. After a while, the traffic noise fades into a soft background hum, and the walk helps me clear my head after a long day. I do not need a destination; walking gives my thoughts room to settle.

My favorite low-cost day is equally simple. I walk for a long time, then sit in a park surrounded by plants. If the weather is nice, I may even doze off for a while in the park. It costs nothing, but I feel rested afterwards. The best part is the quiet time outdoors, not saving money.

One park I particularly like is Tianfu Art Park. It has lakes, green open spaces, and art buildings, so people can walk around the lakes, rest on the grass, take photos, and visit exhibitions. I like that nature, architecture, and art exist in the same place without needing separate stories.

I am currently staying in a hotel in Hangzhou. From the window, I can see an ordinary street and several buildings, with cars and people passing by. I have not lived there long enough to notice long-term changes, so I mainly see small daily changes in traffic and weather.

I like many kinds of food. One strong memory is shrimp balls covered in a tasty sauce at a University of Sheffield event in the Ritz-Carlton. I also enjoy food from other cultures, especially Thai food. I avoid food that is too oily or extremely spicy, because heavy flavours can cover the taste of the ingredients.

Part 1Art / 艺术

Q
Do you like art?
I'm really into art, especially painting and sculpture. For me, painting is fascinating because you can see someone's inner world through their lines and colors—everyone's palette is completely different. I used to visit the Chengdu Art Museum on weekends; it's become my go-to place for unwinding.
我很喜欢艺术，尤其是绘画和雕塑。对我来说，绘画之所以迷人，是因为你可以通过线条和色彩看到一个人的内心世界——每个人的色彩调性都完全不同。我经常周末去成都美术馆，那里已经成了我放松身心的首选去处。
Q
Do you like visiting art galleries?
Absolutely. I love the atmosphere—the gardens around the museum are beautifully designed, so it's a great spot to grab a coffee or do some work. Last time I visited, I tried three VR experiences, including one set in the Roman Colosseum and another on the Titanic. It was incredibly immersive.
当然喜欢。我很喜欢那里的氛围——美术馆周围的园林设计得很美，所以也是个喝咖啡或做点事情的好地方。上次去的时候，我体验了三个VR项目，其中一个是罗马斗兽场，另一个是泰坦尼克号。沉浸感非常强。
Q
Do you want to be an artist?
Honestly, while I deeply admire artists, I don't see myself becoming one. My strengths lie more in logical thinking and communication. But I definitely want to keep art as a important hobby.
说实话，虽然我很钦佩艺术家，但我不觉得自己会成为其中一员。我的优势更多在于逻辑思维和沟通。但我肯定想把艺术保持为一个有意义的爱好。
Q
Modern or traditional art?
I appreciate both. Traditional art grounds me in history, while modern art like VR installations pushes creative boundaries. They each offer something unique.
两者我都欣赏。传统艺术让我扎根于历史，而现代艺术比如VR装置则推动创意边界。它们各自提供独特的东西。
Part 1History / 历史
▶
Q
Do you like history?
Yes, I find history fascinating, especially when it's connected to real objects. Sculpture, for instance, carries the weight of history—it reminds me that incredibly skilled people actually existed in those eras. It's both awe-inspiring and a bit unsettling.
是的，我觉得历史很迷人，尤其是和实物相关的时候。比如雕塑，它承载着历史的重量——它提醒我，那些技艺精湛的人真实地在那些时代存在过。这既令人敬畏，又有些让人不安。
Q
Have you ever been to historical museums?
Yes, several times. What I love most is how museums bring history to life. The VR experience at the Chengdu Art Museum actually let me "walk through" the Roman Colosseum—it felt like I'd traveled back in time.
去过好几次。我最喜欢的是博物馆让历史活起来的方式。成都美术馆的VR体验让我"走进"了罗马斗兽场——感觉就像穿越回了那个时代。
Q
When was the last time you read about history?
It was actually through that VR experience. The Titanic story was told from an underwater archaeology view, which made it feel incredibly real and moving.
其实就是通过那次VR体验。泰坦尼克号的故事是从水下考古的角度讲述的，这让它感觉非常真实而动人。
Q
Did you like history when you were young?
Not particularly—it felt like just memorizing dates and names. But as I grew older, I realized history is about real people and their stories, which changed everything.
不太喜欢——感觉就是在背日期和人名。但长大后我意识到历史是关于真实的人和他们的故事，这改变了一切。

Q
Do you like morning or evening?
I definitely prefer evenings. After a long day, I love stepping out for a walk—just following wherever the green lights lead me. The traffic noise gradually fades into background music, and it becomes this peaceful time for thinking.
我更喜欢晚上。漫长的一天后，我喜欢出去走走——就跟着绿灯走，走到哪算哪。车流声逐渐淡化为背景音乐，变成思考的宁静时光。
Q
What do you usually do in the evening?

Q
What did you do in the evening when you were little?
Mostly homework and watching TV with my family. My evenings were pretty structured back then—nothing like the freedom I have now.

Q

最大的区别是选择权。小时候我的晚上由父母安排。现在我可以选择散步、去美术馆或见朋友——感觉自由多了。
Part 2&3安静的地方
▶
Cue Card
Describe a quiet place you like to go
描述一个你喜欢去的安静的地方
Answer
The place I go to find quiet is actually not a specific location—it's the act of walking itself. I just step out of my door and follow the green lights, going wherever the street takes me. What's amazing is that even though there's traffic all around, the traffic noise gradually fades into a soft background hum, like the whole city becomes white noise for my thoughts. I usually go in the evening, after a long day of studying. I feel completely at peace—it's like the world feels so big that my small worries fade away. Sometimes I walk for an hour without even noticing where I've ended up. What makes it special is that it costs nothing, requires no planning, and yet it's the most effective way I've found to clear my mind.
我去寻找安静的地方其实不是一个具体的地点——而是走路本身。我就出门，跟着绿灯走，走到哪算哪。令人惊叹的是，尽管周围都是车流，噪音会逐渐溶解成一种背景嗡嗡声，就像整个城市变成了我思考的白噪音。我通常在晚上去，漫长的一天学习之后。我感觉完全平静——就像世界的庞大稀释了我所有的小烦恼。有时候我走了一个小时都没注意到自己走到了哪里。让它特别的是，它不花钱、不需要计划，却是我找到的最有效的清理思绪的方式。
Part 3
Why do some people like noise as background?
I think some people find silence uncomfortable—it can feel too empty or isolating. Background noise like music or café chatter gives them a sense of being surrounded by life without the pressure of interaction.
我觉得有些人觉得沉默不舒服——可能感觉太空虚或孤立。背景噪音比如音乐或咖啡馆的闲聊让他们有被生活环绕的感觉，又没有互动的压力。
Part 3
Do you think people in cities have enough access to quiet spaces?
Honestly, I don't think so. Urban planning prioritizes efficiency over tranquility. Most green spaces are either too crowded or too far from residential areas. What's needed is more pocket parks and pedestrian zones where people can actually escape the noise without traveling miles.
说实话，我觉得不够。城市规划优先考虑效率而非宁静。大多数绿地要么太拥挤，要么离居民区太远。需要的是更多口袋公园和步行区，让人们不用跑很远就能真正逃离噪音。

I eventually went to a park and sat among the plants. The weather was warm and quiet, and I even nodded off there for a while. Later, I took another slow walk through the streets before going home. The whole day cost nothing, but it was incredibly fulfilling. What made it special was the quiet time outdoors and the feeling that I had properly rested.
我想讲一个在成都度过的低花费一天。一天结束后，我就跟着绿灯走，街道把我带到哪里就走到哪里，走很久。后来去了一个公园，坐在植物中间。天气温暖又安静，我甚至在那里打了个盹。之后又慢慢沿街散步才回家。整天没有花钱，但非常充实。让这一天特别的是安静的户外时光，以及真正休息下来的感觉。

How does technology affect leisure time?
Technology has made entertainment more accessible, but it can also trap people indoors. I think the key is balance—using technology to discover things to do, but still going out and experiencing the real world.
科技让娱乐更容易获取，但也可能把人困在室内。我觉得关键在于平衡——用科技去发现可做的事情，但仍然要走出去体验真实世界。
Part 3
Why do some people prefer expensive activities over free ones?

Part 2&3重要河流/湖泊
▶
Cue Card
Describe an important river/lake in your country
描述你国家的一条重要河流或湖泊
Answer
I'd like to talk about the Yellow River, one of the most important rivers in China. It is often described as a birthplace of Chinese civilization, and it has supported farming and daily life in northern China for a very long time. So its importance is both cultural and practical.

I have been to the riverbank myself, and the detail I remember best is the surprisingly clean sand. It felt unusual under my hands and feet: if I pressed it hard, it became firm, but if I touched it gently, it felt soft. A large part of the wet riverbank behaved almost like a non-Newtonian fluid, so walking and playing on it was great fun.

That personal experience made the river feel more real to me. It is not only a famous name from history books; it is a river that shaped the country and still creates vivid memories for people today.
我想讲黄河——中国最重要的河流之一。它常被称为中华文明的重要发源地，也长期支持着中国北方的农业和日常生活，因此它既有文化意义，也有实际作用。

我亲自去过黄河边，印象最深的是那里意外地很干净的沙子。手摸或脚踩时感觉很特别：用力压，它就会变硬；轻轻碰，它又是软的。河岸大片湿沙的表现很像非牛顿流体，所以在上面走和玩特别有趣。

这段亲身经历让我觉得黄河不再只是历史书里的一个著名名字。它既是塑造了这个国家的河流，也仍在给今天的人留下鲜活记忆。
Part 3
Are rivers and lakes important to a country?
Absolutely. They support agriculture, transport, and tourism. But beyond the practical benefits, they're also deeply tied to a country's cultural identity.
当然。它们支撑农业、交通和旅游。但除了实际利益之外，它们也和一个国家的文化认同紧密相关。
Part 3
How can we balance tourism development with protecting natural waterways?
It's a delicate balance. Tourism brings revenue but often damages ecosystems through pollution and overuse. I think the key is controlled access—limiting visitor numbers, banning motorized boats, and investing the tourism income back into conservation rather than just infrastructure.
这是个微妙的平衡。旅游带来收入，但往往通过污染和过度使用破坏生态系统。我觉得关键在于控制准入——限制游客数量、禁止机动船只，并将旅游收入重新投入保护而非仅仅基础设施建设。
Part 2&3想有空时去旅游的地方
▶
Cue Card
Describe a place you would like to visit in your free time
描述一个你在空闲时间想去的地方
Answer
A place I'd like to visit again is Fuzhou, a coastal city in southern China. I went there with my parents and another family when I was younger. Since I'm from Shanxi in the north, the weather, food, and even the way people spoke felt completely different.

What I remember most is the scenery. The air was so humid that the sky and the sea seemed to become one. Clouds rested halfway up the green mountains, almost wrapping around them. I also loved the fresh seafood and the old wooden buildings.

If I had enough free time, I would go back and experience the city more slowly. I have already been there once, so it would not be about collecting a new destination. I want to return to a place that left a strong impression on me.
我有空时想再去的地方是中国南方沿海城市福州。小时候我和父母以及另一家人一起去过。因为我是北方山西人，那里的天气、食物，甚至人们说话的方式都让我觉得完全不同。

我印象最深的是风景。空气非常潮湿，天空和大海像是融在了一起。云停在青山的半山腰，像绕着山一样。我也很喜欢新鲜的海鲜和当地的老木建筑。

如果有足够的空闲时间，我想再去一次，慢慢感受这座城市。我已经去过，所以不是为了收集一个新目的地，而是想重回一个曾给我留下深刻印象的地方。
Part 3
Do you think a gap period in life is important?
Yes, definitely. Taking a break between stages—whether between school and work, or between jobs—gives you time to step back and see the bigger picture. It's not wasted time; it's an investment in self-understanding.
是的，绝对重要。在人生阶段之间休息一下——不管是毕业和工作之间，还是两份工作之间——让你有时间退后一步看到更大的画面。这不是浪费时间，而是对自我理解的投入。
Part 3
Do you think virtual tourism could ever replace physical travel?
Virtual tourism offers accessibility—people with mobility issues or limited budgets can experience famous sites. But it cannot replicate the serendipity of real travel: the unexpected café, the wrong turn that leads somewhere beautiful, the conversation with a stranger. Travel is as much about the unplanned moments as the planned ones.
虚拟旅游提供了可及性——行动不便或预算有限的人可以体验著名景点。但它无法复制真实旅行中的偶然性：意外的咖啡馆、走错路却到达美丽地方、与陌生人的交谈。旅行既关乎计划内的时刻，也同样关乎计划外的时刻。
Part 1Walking / 散步
▶

the traffic noise fades into a soft background hum — 车流声淡成柔和的背景嗡鸣

walking gives my thoughts room to settle — 走路让思绪安定下来

Q
Do you like walking?
Absolutely. Walking is practically my favorite way to unwind after a long day. When I was living in Chengdu, I often strolled through the old streets near my apartment, just following the green lights wherever they take me. It's when I do my best thinking.
当然喜欢。散步几乎是我一天结束后最爱的放松方式。在成都读大学时，我经常在公寓附近的老街上漫步，就是跟着绿灯走，走到哪算哪。那是我思考效率最高的时候。
Q
Where do you usually go for a walk?
I do not usually choose a destination. I start from where I am and follow whichever direction has a green light. That small rule lets the walk develop naturally and takes me onto streets I might not otherwise choose.

Q
What do you think about while walking?
Sometimes I think about whatever is currently on my mind, and sometimes I simply notice the streets around me. The rhythm of walking helps my thoughts settle into a clearer order.
有时我会想最近正在关注的事情，有时只是观察周围街道。走路的节奏会让脑中的想法慢慢形成更清楚的顺序。
Part 1Parks / 公园
▶
Q
Do you like going to parks?
Yes. One park I particularly like is Tianfu Art Park in Chengdu. It has lakes, green open spaces, and several art buildings, so I can walk, sit down, and enjoy both nature and architecture in one place.
喜欢。我特别喜欢成都的天府艺术公园。那里有湖、开阔绿地和几座美术馆建筑，所以我可以在同一个地方散步、坐着休息，同时感受自然和建筑。
Q
What do people usually do in parks in your city?
At Tianfu Art Park, people usually walk around the lakes, rest on the grass, take photos, and visit exhibitions. Some people come mainly for the buildings, while others simply want a calm outdoor space.
在天府艺术公园，人们通常会沿湖散步、在草地休息、拍照和看展。有些人主要为建筑而来，也有人只是想找一个安静的户外空间。
Q
Do you think parks are important for children?
Definitely. Parks give children room to move freely and explore. An art park can offer something extra, because children can notice unusual buildings and artworks as well as plants and water.
当然。公园给孩子们自由活动和探索的空间。艺术公园还能多提供一层体验，因为孩子除了植物和水，也会注意到特别的建筑和艺术作品。
Part 1View / 景色
▶
Q
What can you see from the window of your room?
I'm currently staying in a hotel in Hangzhou. From the window, I can see an ordinary street and several buildings, just like the view from any normal room facing a road. There are cars and people passing by, so it feels simple but full of everyday life.
我目前住在杭州的一家旅店。从窗外能看到一条普通街道和几栋楼，就像任何正常临街房间的景色一样。车辆和行人来来往往，所以它很普通，但也很有日常生活感。
Q
Has the view changed over the years?
I have not lived in this hotel for long enough to notice a major change. The view is quite ordinary, so small daily changes, such as different traffic or weather, are more noticeable than changes to the buildings.
我在这家旅店住的时间还不够长，没有看到什么重大变化。这里的景色很普通，所以比起楼房变化，每天车流或天气的小变化反而更明显。
Q
Would you prefer to live in a place with a better view?
I think the view matters less than the overall living environment. A great view is nice, but if the neighborhood lacks convenience or the apartment is poorly designed, it wouldn't be worth it. That said, having natural light and something pleasant to look at does affect my mood day to day.
我觉得景色不如整体居住环境重要。好景色是不错，但如果社区不方便或公寓设计差，就不值得。不过有自然光和好看的风景确实会影响我每天的心情。
Part 1Scenery / 风景
▶
Q
What is the natural scenery like around your city?
Shanxi has a different kind of beauty — the mountains there are less dramatic than famous tourist spots but deeply familiar. What I value most is how the landscape changes with the seasons, from bare winter hills to lush summer greenery. It taught me that you don't need spectacular scenery to feel connected to nature.
山西有一种不同的美——那里的山不如著名景点壮观，但深深熟悉。我最欣赏的是风景随季节变化，从冬天光秃秃的山丘到夏天郁郁葱葱的绿色。这让我明白，你不需要壮观的景色就能感受到与自然的连接。
Q
Do you prefer mountain scenery or coastal scenery?
Mountains, without a doubt. Maybe it's because I grew up surrounded by them. There's something grounding about being enclosed by peaks that the sea just can't match. The sea feels infinite, but mountains feel like they're holding you in place.
绝对是山。也许是因为从小在山边长大。被群山环抱有一种让你安定的感觉，这是大海给不了的。大海让你觉得无限，但山让你觉得被稳稳地托住。
Q
Is there any scenery you'd like to see in the future?
I'd love to see the northern lights in person. Photos and videos cannot fully reproduce the experience of colourful light moving across a dark sky. Star Walk 2 has made me more curious about what we can actually see above us.
我很想亲眼看到极光。照片和视频无法完整还原彩色光芒在夜空中移动的体验。Star Walk 2 也让我对头顶真正能看到的天空现象更好奇。
Part 1Food / 食物
▶
Q
What kind of food do you like?
I like many kinds of food, but one of my favourites is shrimp balls covered in a tasty sauce. The best one I remember was served at the Ritz-Carlton during a University of Sheffield event. I also enjoy food from other countries, especially Thai food.
我喜欢很多种食物，其中最喜欢的之一是裹着美味酱汁的虾球。我印象中最好吃的一次，是在丽思卡尔顿参加谢菲尔德大学活动时吃到的。我也喜欢外国菜，尤其喜欢泰餐。
Q
Is there any food you don't like?
I do not like food that is too oily or extremely spicy. Heavy flavours can cover up the taste of the ingredients, and eating food that is too spicy all the time is not very healthy.
我不喜欢过于油腻或特别辣的食物。太重的味道会盖住食材本身的味道，而且长期吃得太辣也不太健康。
Q
Do you think it's important to try food from other cultures?
Definitely. I have tried Thai, Japanese, and Western food, and Thai food is my favourite. Food does more than satisfy hunger: it reflects a place's geography, climate, and way of life. It can even show common preferences and personality in a culture.
当然。我吃过泰餐、日料和西餐，最喜欢泰餐。食物不只是满足饥饿：它也反映一个地方的地理、气候和生活方式，甚至能展现一种文化中人们普遍的偏好和性格倾向。
Part 2&3推荐旅行过的地方
▶
Cue Card
Describe a place you have traveled to that you would recommend to others.
You should say:
- Where it is
- How you traveled there
- What you did there
- And explain why you would recommend it
描述一个你去过并想推荐给别人的地方。你应该说：它在哪里 / 你怎么去的 / 你在那里做了什么 / 并解释为什么你会推荐它
Answer
I would recommend Fuzhou, a coastal city in southern China. I went there with my parents and another family. Since I grew up in dry northern China, the humid weather, green landscape, food, and local speech all felt fresh to me.

The strongest memory is the scenery. The sky and the sea seemed to become one, and clouds rested halfway up the mountains as if they were wrapping around them. We also visited an old area with traditional wooden buildings and had very fresh seafood by the sea.

I would recommend Fuzhou because it offers nature, local architecture, and food in one trip. It feels clearly different from northern China, so the journey gives you a real sense of entering another environment without leaving the country.
我会推荐中国南方的沿海城市福州。我和父母以及另一家人一起去过。因为我在干燥的中国北方长大，那里的湿润天气、绿色景观、食物和当地说话方式都让我觉得很新鲜。

最深刻的记忆是风景。天空和大海像融在一起，云停在半山腰，像绕着山一样。我们还去了有传统木建筑的老街区，也在海边吃了非常新鲜的海鲜。

我推荐福州，因为一次旅行就能体验自然、当地建筑和食物。它与中国北方明显不同，所以即使没有出国，也会真切感到自己进入了另一种环境。
Part 3
Why do you think people enjoy traveling to natural places?
I think it comes down to escaping the overstimulation of city life. We're constantly bombarded with notifications and screens, and nature offers a kind of silence that resets your mental bandwidth. There's also something humbling about standing in front of a mountain — it reminds you how small your daily worries actually are.
我觉得归根结底是逃离城市生活的过度刺激。我们不断被通知和屏幕轰炸，而大自然提供了一种能重置你精神带宽的安静。站在山面前还有一种让人谦卑的感觉——它提醒你，你日常的烦恼其实有多渺小。
Part 3
What makes a travel recommendation truly valuable?
A real recommendation comes from personal experience and emotional connection, not just a list of sights. When someone shares how a place made them feel—the unexpected café they found, the conversation with a local—that's when you know it's real and worth considering.
真正有价值的推荐来自个人体验和情感连接，而非仅仅是景点列表。当有人分享一个地方让他们感受如何——他们发现的意外咖啡馆、与当地人交谈——你就知道这是真实的，值得考虑。
Part 2&3去过且喜欢的城市

Cue Card
Describe a city you have visited that you really liked.

描述一个你去过并且非常喜欢的城市。你应该说：这座城市在哪里 / 你什么时候去的 / 你在那里做了什么 / 并解释为什么你喜欢它
Answer
A few years ago, I visited Fuzhou with my family. It is a coastal city in southern China, and it felt very different from the dry north where I grew up. What I remember most is the view: clouds resting halfway up the mountains, with the sea behind them. I took a photo there and it is still my favorite one. We also had fresh seafood by the sea. I would like to go back because it was green, humid, and relaxing.
几年前，我和家人去了福州。它是中国南方的一座沿海城市，和我长大的干燥北方很不一样。我最记得的是景色：云停在半山腰，身后就是大海。我在那里拍了一张照片，到现在还是我最喜欢的一张。我们还吃了在海边吃到的新鲜海鲜。我想再去，因为那里很绿、很湿润，也很放松。
Part 3
Do you think big cities are becoming too similar to each other?
Sometimes. Chain stores can make cities look similar, but local scenery and food still matter. In Fuzhou, the sea, green mountains, old wooden buildings, and seafood gave the city its own character. Cities should protect the things that make them different.
有时候会。连锁店会让城市看起来相似，但当地的景色和食物仍然很重要。福州的大海、青山、老木建筑和海鲜，让它有自己的性格。城市应该保护那些让它与众不同的东西。
Part 3
What factors make a city livable versus just visitable?
A visitable city has attractions; a livable city has community, affordable housing, and reliable public services. I've visited cities with stunning landmarks but terrible daily life. The real test is whether ordinary residents—not just tourists—can build a decent life there.
一个值得参观的城市有景点；一个宜居的城市有社区、负担得起的住房和可靠的公共服务。我参观过有令人惊叹地标但日常生活很糟糕的城市。真正的考验是普通居民——不仅仅是游客——能否在那里过上体面的生活。
📝阅读建议：核心内容，建议反复练习说。先理解故事脉络，再尝试用自己的话复述。

故事二：身边的人与事

身边的人和真实经历——语言培训班的朋友 Anti、《欢迎来龙餐馆》、表哥自学法律、菲律宾志愿者外出活动、郭晶晶，以及我做志愿者时顺便看过的一场足球赛。同一份熟悉素材覆盖朋友、语言学习、电影、运动员、运动队和现场比赛等相关话题。

覆盖 17 个主题：Dream & Ambition / Films & Cinemas / Sports Programs / Sports team / 在成功公司工作的人 / 组织快乐活动 / 交通拥堵 / 收到特殊蛋糕 / 语言学习 / 保护环境的法律（含想颁布的环保法律） / 克服困难成功的人 / 朋友自学 / 商业上很成功的人 / 改变重要想法 / 长期追求/目标 / 擅长学习和说语言的人 / 看过的现场比赛
完整故事 ▶

One friend I really enjoy spending time with is Anti. We met at an English tutoring class, and we got along almost immediately. She studies art and design, so she has a very creative eye. She often hums while she is drawing, and she can turn a simple idea into something beautiful. She is also better at planning than I am. When I want to go out instead of studying, she says, “Fine, but let's come back in thirty minutes and finish the next thing.”

中文翻译 ▶

我很喜欢和朋友 Anti 一起待着。我们在英语补习班认识，而且几乎马上就合得来。她学艺术和设计，所以很有创意。她常常一边画画一边哼歌，还能把一个简单的想法变成好看的作品。她也比我擅长规划。我想出去玩、不想学习时，她会说：“可以，但三十分钟后回来把下一件事完成。”

I once organized a small cross-cultural outing for four foreign volunteers. We walked through nearby streets, tried fried shrimp and other snacks, and talked about local food and culture. It was simple, but everyone enjoyed the food and felt included. Mr Liu later helped me settle the group expenses, and the four volunteers came over to shake his hand and thank him.

中文翻译 ▶

我曾为四位外国志愿者组织过一次小型跨文化外出。我们在附近街上逛，吃炸虾等小吃，也聊当地食物和文化。活动很简单，但大家都吃得开心，也有参与感。后来刘老师帮我结清集体费用，四位志愿者还主动过来和他握手道谢。

The most memorable film I have watched recently is “Welcome to Dragon Restaurant”. It follows a Chinese man who helps run a restaurant in a small country in the Middle East. At first, he sees himself as an outsider to the war. The restaurant survives partly because of help from a local friend and an American soldier, but both of them are later killed. When an officer asks him, “Do you still remember that this war has nothing to do with you?”, he can no longer pretend to be only a spectator.

What shocked me most was that every small chance of hope is destroyed by violence. Even a child is misled into thinking that becoming a human bomb is heroic. The film does not give the audience an easy happy ending. Instead, it makes us feel that no one is completely outside a human tragedy.

中文翻译 ▶

最近最让我记得住的电影是《欢迎来龙餐馆》。它讲的是一个中国人在中东一个小国参与经营餐馆。起初，他觉得自己只是战争之外的人。餐馆能维持，一部分靠一位当地朋友和一名美国士兵的帮助，但两人后来都死了。当一位军官问他：“你还记得你和这场战争没有关系吗？”时，他再也不能假装自己只是看客。

最震撼我的是，每一点可能的希望都会被暴力毁掉。甚至有一个孩子被蒙蔽，以为成为人肉炸弹是英雄行为。电影没有给观众一个轻松的大团圆，而是让我们感到，没有人能完全置身于人类的苦难之外。

One childhood memory is a traffic jam that lasted nearly two hours. What made it unforgettable was that we got out and went to a nearby KFC, which felt like a strange adventure to me as a child. Another food memory is a Basque cheesecake I made on the day my younger brother came home from Shandong for his summer holiday. It was my first time making one, and it turned out very well. I made it myself to welcome him home.

中文翻译 ▶

童年记忆里有一次堵车，持续了将近两个小时。让它难忘的是我们下车去了附近的肯德基，对小时候的我来说像一场奇怪的冒险。另一段食物记忆，是弟弟放暑假从山东回家的当天，我给他做了巴斯克蛋糕。那是我第一次做这种蛋糕，成品却很好。我亲手做它来欢迎弟弟回家。

While preparing for IELTS, I started breaking articles into useful phrase chunks instead of memorizing isolated words. I treat the chunks like Lego pieces and combine them when I speak. While using AI, I also noticed the power of meaningful context and repeated exposure: some words became familiar almost without trying. The strongest reason to learn is the desire to express yourself in a field or relationship that truly matters to you.

中文翻译 ▶

备考雅思时，我不再背零散单词，而是开始把文章拆成实用的完整语块。我把它们当作乐高积木，开口时再进行组合。使用 AI 的过程中，我也感受到有意义的语境和反复接触的力量：有些词几乎不用刻意背就熟悉了。最强的学习动力，是在真正在意的领域或关系里产生表达自己的渴望。

I became more serious about the environment after visiting Baima Fairy Cave in Shanxi. It is a natural cave with rock formations that took thousands of years to form. Even though it was hot outside, I needed a jacket inside. The cave was beautiful, but I saw plastic bottles and food wrappers among the rocks. It made me think that small everyday choices can protect a place or damage it. My grandmother has taught me the same thing: she reuses bags and uses rice-washing water to water her plants.

中文翻译 ▶

去过山西白马仙洞后，我开始更认真地看待环境问题。那里是天然洞穴，岩石形成了几千年。外面很热，洞里却要穿外套。洞穴很美，但我看到塑料瓶和食品包装散落在岩石之间。这让我觉得，日常的小选择既能保护一个地方，也能伤害它。我奶奶也一直这样教我：她重复使用袋子，还会用淘米水浇植物。

My long-term dream is to build a platform that helps people turn ideas into reality. People could find suitable partners, collaborate and receive support from a wider network. My idea of perfect work is to keep improving that platform and work every day for a dream I genuinely believe in.

中文翻译 ▶

我的长期梦想是搭建一个帮助人们把想法真正变成现实的平台。人们可以找到合适的伙伴、展开协作，并获得更大网络的支持。我心目中的完美工作，就是不断改进这个平台，每天为自己真正相信的梦想工作。

One book that influenced me is Illustrated Economics. I found it on my parents' bookshelf when I was young. The pictures made difficult ideas easier to follow, and the book introduced me to opportunity cost. It showed me that reading can give me a new way to understand everyday choices, even when I do not understand every page at first.

中文翻译 ▶

一本影响过我的书是《图解经济学》。小时候我在父母的书架上发现了它，图画让困难概念更容易理解，这本书也让我第一次接触机会成本。它让我看到，即使一开始没有读懂每一页，阅读仍能给我一种理解日常选择的新方式。

Part 1Dream and Ambition / 梦想与志向
▶
Q
What was your childhood dream?
When I was young, I dreamed of building a platform where people could find the right partners and turn their ideas into reality. With collaboration and support from a wider network, I hoped more people could create the lives they truly wanted.
小时候我梦想搭建一个平台，让人们能够找到合适的伙伴，把想法真正变成现实。我希望通过协作和更大范围的网络支持，让更多人创造自己真正想要的生活。
Q
What is your dream job?
My dream job is closely connected to that childhood idea. I would like to build and run a platform that helps people make their ideas happen. Instead of working toward someone else's goal every day, I would be working toward a dream I genuinely believe in.
我的理想工作和童年的想法紧密相连。我想搭建并运营一个帮助人们实现想法的平台。我每天不是在替别人完成一个与我无关的目标，而是在为自己真正相信的梦想奔波。
Q
Are you an ambitious person?
I'd say so, but in a quiet way. I'm not chasing money or status—I want to create something important that helps people connect and collaborate.
算是吧，但是以一种安静的方式。我不追求金钱或地位——我想创造有意义的东西，帮助人们连接和合作。
Q
Do you stick to your dreams?
Generally, yes, although the exact form may change. I may take detours, but the central dream is still the same: helping ideas grow through collaboration and become part of real life.
通常会坚持，不过具体形式可能变化。我也许会走一些弯路，但核心梦想一直没变：让想法通过协作成长，并真正进入现实生活。
Part 2&3在成功公司工作的人

Cue Card
Describe a person who works in a successful company
描述一个在成功公司工作的人
Answer
I'd like to talk about my grandfather, who ran his own business. What impressed me was not only the business itself, but the way he worked with people. He treated his workers like family, and even after the business closed, some of them still came back to visit him. To me, that shows real integrity and long-term trust.
我想说说我外公，他经营自己的生意。让我佩服的不只是生意本身，还有他和人相处的方式。他把员工当家人一样对待，哪怕生意结束后，也有一些员工还会回来探望他。对我来说，这体现了真正的正直和长期信任。
Part 3
Should companies donate money to help society?
Absolutely. Successful companies have a responsibility to give back to the communities that support them. It's not just about charity—it also builds trust and goodwill.
当然。成功的公司有责任回馈支持它们的社区。这不仅仅是慈善——它也建立信任和好感。
Part 3
What personal qualities matter most for career success in your opinion?
Beyond technical skills, I believe integrity and the ability to treat people well are important. A career is long, and people remember how you made them feel. My grandfather's former workers still visiting him proves that.
除了技术能力，我觉得正直和善待他人的能力很重要。职业生涯很长，人们会记得你如何对待他们。外公以前的员工至今还会来探望他，就说明了这一点。
Part 2&3组织快乐活动
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you organized a happy event successfully
描述一次你成功组织了一场欢乐活动的经历
Answer
I'd like to talk about a small cross-cultural outing I organized when four foreign volunteers from the Philippines came to a local school. I really wanted to go out, so I invited all four of them and took them around the nearby streets. We tried fried shrimp and Shanghai-style chicken strips, and I introduced some local food and culture to them.

I also asked Mr. Liu to cover part of the cost. I worked out the bill carefully and told him which part was mine, which part was my treat, and which part could be reimbursed. In the end, he gave me fifty yuan. When we sat down together, I told my Filipino friends, “Mr. Liu paid for all of us.” They immediately walked over, shook his hand, and thanked him. I quietly told him what I had said, and although he acted casual, I think he was secretly pleased.

It was not a large or formal event, but everyone enjoyed the food and felt included. I was happy that I had brought people from different cultures together in such a simple way.
我想讲一次我组织的小型跨文化外出活动。当时有四位来自菲律宾的外国志愿者来到当地一所学校，我很想出去玩，就邀请他们四个人一起到附近街上逛。我们吃了炸虾和上海鸡柳，我也向他们介绍了当地食物和文化。

我还找刘老师报销了一部分费用。我认真算清楚哪部分是我自己的、哪部分是我请客、哪部分可以报销，最后他给了我五十元。大家坐下后，我告诉菲律宾朋友：“刘老师为我们所有人买了单。”他们马上走过去和他握手致谢。我悄悄告诉他自己说了什么，虽然他装得很随意，但我觉得他心里其实挺开心。

这不是大型或正式活动，但每个人都吃得开心，也有参与感。我很高兴自己用这么简单的方式让来自不同文化的人聚到了一起。
Part 3
Do people need others' help when organizing things?
I think it depends on the scale. For small things, you can manage alone, but for bigger events, teamwork is essential. Also, involving others often makes the experience more important.
我觉得取决于规模。小事可以自己搞定，但大型活动团队合作是必须的。而且让他人参与通常让体验更有意义。
Part 3
What role does celebration play in building relationships?
Celebrations create shared emotional anchors. When people experience joy together, it strengthens bonds in ways daily interactions cannot. The memory of a well-organized event becomes a reference point—'remember when we...'—that keeps relationships alive across distance and time.
庆祝活动创造了共同的情感锚点。当人们一起经历快乐时，它以日常互动无法做到的方式加强纽带。一个精心组织的活动的记忆成为一个参照点——'还记得那次我们...'——让关系跨越距离和时间保持鲜活。

Do you prefer watching films at home or in the cinema?
I prefer the cinema. There's something about the big screen and the shared experience—you're sitting in the dark with strangers, all feeling the same emotions. It's hard to replicate that at home.
我更喜欢电影院。大银幕和共同体验有种特别的感觉——你和陌生人坐在黑暗中，感受着同样的情感。这在家里很难复制。

Not as often as I'd like—maybe once or twice a month. But when I do, I like to really immerse myself, not just have something on in the background.
没有希望的那么频繁——大概每月一两次。但看的时候，我喜欢真正沉浸其中，而不是只是放着当背景。

Part 2&3交通拥堵
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you were stuck in a traffic jam
描述一次你被困在交通堵塞中的经历
Answer
I remember a traffic jam from when I was a kid, going to my aunt's house. It was the most memorable one I've ever experienced—we were stuck for nearly two hours. What made it unforgettable was that we actually got out of the car and went to a nearby KFC to eat while waiting. For a child, that was incredibly exciting—getting to eat fast food because of a traffic jam felt like a strange adventure. I also desperately needed the bathroom, which added to the drama. Looking back, it's a funny memory, but at the time it was pretty stressful. I think traffic jams are a major problem in big cities, and developing public transport is one of the best solutions.
我记得小时候去姑姑家时的一次堵车。那是我经历过的最难忘的一次——堵了将近两个小时。让它难忘的是我们竟然下车去附近的肯德基吃了顿饭。对小孩来说，这太刺激了——因为堵车而吃到快餐，感觉像一场奇怪的冒险。我当时还急需要上厕所，更加戏剧化。回想起来这是个搞笑的记忆，但当时其实挺痛苦的。我觉得堵车是大城市的主要问题，发展公共交通是最好的解决方案之一。
Part 3
How can we solve traffic jam problems?
I think improving public transport is key—especially underground systems that bypass road traffic. Also, encouraging remote work and flexible hours could reduce peak-time congestion.
我觉得改善公共交通是关键——尤其是能绕开路面交通的地铁系统。另外，鼓励远程办公和弹性工作时间也能减少高峰时段拥堵。
Part 3
How do you think autonomous vehicles will change urban traffic?
They could dramatically reduce congestion by optimizing routes and eliminating human error. But I worry about the transition period—when both human-driven and autonomous cars share the road. The benefits won't be immediate; it'll take years of integration and infrastructure upgrades.
它们可以通过优化路线和消除人为错误来大幅减少拥堵。但我担心过渡期——当人工驾驶和自动驾驶汽车共享道路时。好处不会立竿见影；需要多年的整合和基础设施升级。
Part 2&3收到特殊蛋糕
▶
Cue Card
Describe a special cake you received from others
描述一个别人送给你的特别蛋糕
Answer
I haven't actually received a special cake, but I once made a special cake for my younger brother. This year, his summer holiday started quite late. On the day he came home from Shandong for his summer holiday, I bought the ingredients and made a Basque cheesecake for him.

It was my first time making one, but it came out surprisingly well. The top was dark and slightly burnt, while the middle was soft and creamy, almost like the ones sold in cake shops. My mother thought it was a little too sweet, but I liked it, and my brother was very grateful.

What made it special was that I made it myself to welcome him home, and it turned out perfectly on my first try.
我其实没有收到过特殊蛋糕，但我曾经为弟弟做过一个特别的蛋糕。今年他的暑假放得比较晚。他放暑假从山东回家的当天，我买了食材，给他做了一个巴斯克蛋糕。

那是我第一次做这种蛋糕，但成品意外地非常成功。表面颜色深、略带焦香，中间柔软绵密，和蛋糕店卖的味道差不多。妈妈觉得有点太甜，但我很喜欢，弟弟也非常感谢我。

它特别的地方，是我亲手做它来欢迎弟弟回家，并且第一次尝试就做得很完美。
Part 3
Is it good to communicate when eating with family?
Absolutely. Mealtime is one of the few moments when everyone puts down their phones and actually talks. It strengthens family bonds and creates a space for honest conversation.
当然。吃饭时间是为数不多的所有人都放下手机真正交谈的时刻。它增强家庭纽带，也为真诚对话创造了空间。
Part 3
How has food culture changed with globalization?
Globalization has made ingredients accessible but often at the cost of authenticity. You can find 'Italian' pizza in any city, but it's usually adapted to local tastes. The paradox is that while we have more variety than ever, truly traditional flavors are becoming harder to find.
全球化让食材变得容易获取，但往往以牺牲正宗性为代价。你可以在任何城市找到'意大利'披萨，但它通常被改良以适应当地口味。悖论是，虽然我们拥有前所未有的多样性，但真正传统的味道却越来越难找到。
Part 2&3语言学习
▶
Cue Card
Describe a thing you did to learn another language
描述一件你为了学习另一门语言而做过的事
Answer
I'd like to talk about what I have been doing while preparing for IELTS. Instead of memorizing isolated words, I started breaking articles into useful phrase chunks. I treat those chunks like Lego pieces: once I know several complete pieces, I can combine them and speak more naturally.

I also noticed the power of environment and repetition while using AI. Because I kept seeing and using certain words in meaningful conversations, I became familiar with them almost without trying.

This method made language feel less like a list to memorize and more like something I could build with. It has helped me move from knowing words to actually getting sentences out.
我想讲自己备考雅思时采用的方法。我不再背零散单词，而是开始把文章拆成实用的完整语块。我把语块当成乐高积木：掌握几块完整的表达后，就能把它们组合起来，更自然地说出口。

在使用 AI 的过程中，我也感受到了环境和重复的力量。因为我不断在有意义的交流中看到并使用某些词，几乎不用刻意背就逐渐熟悉了它们。

这种方法让语言不再像一张需要硬背的清单，而像可以亲手搭建的东西。它帮助我从“认识词”走向真正把句子说出来。
Part 3
What's the best way to learn a language?
A good method combines meaningful context, useful phrase chunks, and repeated exposure. Music can help patterns stay in memory, and real articles show exactly how phrases work. Most importantly, people should find something they truly want that requires the language—using AI technology, making foreign friends, or talking to someone they deeply admire. The desire to express yourself creates a reason to keep learning and using more.
好的方法会结合有意义的语境、实用语块和反复接触。音乐能让语言模式更容易留在记忆里，真实文章则会展示语块到底怎么用。最重要的是，找到一个自己真正在意、而且必须用这门语言才能完成的领域——比如使用 AI 技术、结交外国朋友，或与自己非常欣赏的人交流。表达自己的渴望会推动人持续学习并使用更多语言。
Part 3
Do you think language learning apps can replace traditional methods?
Good apps and websites are extremely helpful. A well-designed tool plans around memory cycles and small learning details that users may not think about themselves. When everything you need has already been considered and placed in the right order, it feels as if a thoughtful partner is supporting your learning. Real conversation is still necessary, but good tools can carry a large part of the preparation.
好的 App 和网站非常有帮助。设计良好的工具会考虑记忆周期以及学习中的各种小细节，这些往往是使用者自己顾不到的。当你发现自己需要的东西都有人提前想好并按恰当顺序设计好时，会觉得像有一个细心的伙伴在托住你的学习。真实交流仍然必要，但好工具能承担很大一部分准备工作。

语块积木 · 直接拿去说

plastic bottles and food wrappers among the rocks — 塑料瓶和包装纸散落在岩石之间

Answer
I'd like to talk about waste sorting regulations in China. The law requires residents to separate their garbage into categories like recyclable, hazardous, and food waste. I think this is a positive step because I personally care deeply about the environment—I always choose public transport over driving, specifically to reduce my carbon footprint. The law first came into effect in Shanghai and then expanded to other cities. I think it's important because individual actions, when multiplied across millions of people, can make a real difference. However, enforcement and education are still challenges—many people find the rules confusing. I think schools should teach children about environmental responsibility from a young age, so it becomes a habit rather than an obligation.
我想说说中国的垃圾分类法规。这个法律要求居民将垃圾分为可回收、有害和厨余等类别。我认为这是积极的一步，因为我个人非常关心环境——我总是选择公共交通而不是开车，专门为了减少碳足迹。这个法律首先在上海实施，然后扩展到其他城市。我觉得它很重要，因为个人行为在数百万人中累积起来，能产生真正的改变。但执行和教育仍是挑战——很多人觉得规则令人困惑。我觉得学校应该从小教孩子环境责任，这样它会变成习惯而非义务。
Part 3
What kinds of rules do schools in China have?
Schools have various rules—uniforms, attendance, no phones in class. I think school rules are important because they teach discipline and respect, but they should also encourage critical thinking rather than blind obedience.
学校有各种规定——校服、考勤、课堂不能用手机。我觉得校规很重要，因为它们教纪律和尊重，但也应该鼓励批判性思维而不是盲目服从。
Part 3
Why do some environmental laws fail to achieve their goals?
Often because enforcement is weak and penalties are too low to deter violators. Another issue is lack of public awareness—people don't understand why the law matters. Effective environmental protection requires both strict enforcement and education, so citizens become partners rather than obstacles.
通常是因为执法不力且处罚太低，不足以威慑违规者。另一个问题是公众意识缺乏——人们不理解为什么这项法律重要。有效的环境保护需要严格执法和教育并重，这样公民才能成为合作伙伴而非障碍。
