如果必须选，我会选现场。那次志愿经历让我感受到，人群和共同的现场气氛本身就是活动的一部分。屏幕也许能把动作拍得更清楚，却无法完整还原这种感受。
Part 2&3克服困难成功的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person you know who has achieved success after overcoming difficulties. You should say: who this person is, what difficulties they faced, how they overcame them, and explain why you feel their success is important.
描述一个你认识的人，他在克服困难后取得了成功。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 他面临了什么困难 / 他是如何克服的 / 并解释为什么你觉得他的成功是有意义的
Answer
I'd like to talk about my cousin, who is someone I deeply admire for his sheer determination. He used to work at a bank — a stable, well-paying job that most people would consider ideal. However, he always felt unfulfilled and secretly harbored a passion for law.

About five years ago, he made the bold decision to resign from the bank and devote himself entirely to preparing for the national judicial examination. This exam is notoriously difficult, with a pass rate of barely ten percent. He spent nearly two years studying on his own, often from dawn until midnight, without any formal classroom instruction. There were moments when he doubted himself, especially when close friends questioned whether he was making a reckless mistake.

But he persevered against all odds and passed the exam on his second attempt. Today, he's not only a licensed lawyer but also manages a team at a law firm. His journey taught me that success isn't about having the easiest path — it's about having the courage to pursue what truly matters to you, even when the odds are stacked against you.
我想谈谈我的堂哥，他是我非常敬佩的人，因为他的纯粹毅力。他以前在银行工作——一份稳定、高薪的工作，大多数人都会觉得是理想选择。然而，他总觉得不满足，内心深处一直怀有对法律的热情。

大约五年前，他做出了一个大胆的决定：从银行辞职，全身心投入备战国家司法考试。这个考试以难度著称，通过率仅百分之十左右。他花了将近两年时间自学，经常从清晨学到深夜，没有任何正式的课堂指导。有时候他会自我怀疑，尤其是亲密的朋友质疑他是否在做一个鲁莽的错误决定时。

但他排除万难坚持了下来，第二次参加考试时通过了。如今，他不仅是一名执业律师，还在律所管理一个团队。他的经历让我明白，成功不在于走最轻松的路——而在于有勇气追求真正重要的事，即使困难重重。
Part 3
What qualities do people need to overcome difficulties?
I think resilience is the most important quality — the ability to keep going when things get tough. Additionally, having a clear sense of purpose helps people stay focused on their goals. Self-discipline also plays a vital role, as overcoming challenges often requires consistent effort over a long period.
我认为韧性是最关键的品质——在困境中继续前行的能力。此外，拥有清晰的目标感能帮助人们保持专注。自律同样至关重要，因为克服挑战往往需要长期持续的努力。
Part 3
What can society do to better support people facing major setbacks?
Society should move beyond celebrating individual resilience and address systemic barriers. This means affordable mental health services, job retraining programs, and financial safety nets. Resilience shouldn't be a prerequisite for survival; it should be a bonus in a system that already protects its most vulnerable members.
社会应该超越颂扬个人韧性，去解决系统性障碍。这意味着负担得起的心理健康服务、职业再培训项目和财务安全网。韧性不应该是生存的前提；它应该是在一个已经保护最脆弱成员的系统中的额外奖励。
Part 2&3朋友自学
▶
Cue Card
Describe something that a friend of yours taught themselves to do. You should say: who this friend is, what they learned, how they learned it, and explain how you felt about their achievement.
描述一件你的朋友自学学会的事情。你应该说：这个朋友是谁 / 他学了什么 / 他是怎么学的 / 并解释你对他这个成就的感受
Answer
I don't have a friend with exactly this experience, but my cousin once succeeded in teaching himself law. He left a stable bank job and prepared for China's national legal examination on his own.

He learned through books, online materials, and past exam papers. He did not take formal classes, and he passed on his second attempt. Later, he became a lawyer and a team manager.

I was proud of him because self-directed learning completely changed his career. His story showed me that learning by yourself requires a clear goal, self-discipline, and the courage to continue when the result is uncertain.
我没有这样的朋友，不过我表哥有一次自学成功的经历。他离开了稳定的银行工作，靠自己准备中国的国家法律职业资格考试。

他用书、网络资料和历年试题学习，没有参加正式课程，并在第二次考试时通过了。后来他成为律师，还负责管理一个团队。

我为他感到骄傲，因为自主学习彻底改变了他的职业。他的经历让我看到，自学需要清晰目标、自律，以及在结果不确定时继续坚持的勇气。
Part 3
What are the advantages of self-learning compared to formal education?
Self-learning offers impressive flexibility — you can learn at your own pace and focus on areas most relevant to your goals. It also develops self-motivation and problem-solving skills. However, formal education provides structured guidance and recognized qualifications, which can be equally valuable depending on one's career path.
自学具有显著的灵活性——你可以按照自己的节奏学习，专注于与目标最相关的领域。它还培养了自驱力和解决问题的能力。不过，正规教育提供系统化的指导和受认可的学历，根据职业发展方向不同，这些同样有其价值。
Part 3
What motivates people to teach themselves new skills in adulthood?
Often it's a combination of necessity and curiosity. Job loss, career transitions, or simply realizing there's more to life than their current routine. What's inspiring is that adult learners bring purpose and focus that younger students sometimes lack—they know exactly why they're learning, which makes the process more efficient and important.
通常这是必要性和好奇心的结合。失业、职业转换，或者只是意识到生活中有比他们当前日常更多的东西。令人鼓舞的是，成年学习者带来了目标和专注，这是年轻学生有时缺乏的——他们确切地知道为什么学习，这使过程更高效和有意义。
Part 2&3商业上很成功的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person you know who is successful in business. You should say: who this person is, what business they run, how they became successful, and explain what you can learn from them.
描述一个你认识在商业上成功的人。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 他经营什么生意 / 他是如何成功的 / 并解释你能从他身上学到什么
Answer
I'd like to talk about my maternal grandfather, who used to run his own company and employ many people. I do not remember every business detail, but I know the company supported a large team and was successful for many years.

What impressed me most was not the size of the business, but the way he treated his workers. He respected them and treated them almost like family. Even after the company closed, some former employees still came back to visit my grandparents.

To me, that is strong evidence of real business success. Profit matters, but the trust people keep after the business is over says even more. I learned from him that treating employees well is not separate from success; it is part of what makes success last.
我想讲我的外公，他以前经营自己的公司，有很多员工。我不记得所有商业细节，但我知道公司支撑着一个不小的团队，并且成功经营了很多年。

最让我印象深刻的不是生意规模，而是他对待员工的方式。他尊重员工，几乎把他们当作家人。即使公司后来关了，一些以前的员工仍然会回来探望我的外祖父母。

对我来说，这是真正商业成功的有力证明。利润当然重要，但生意结束后人们依然保留的信任更能说明问题。我从他身上学到，善待员工不是成功以外的事，而是让成功长久的一部分。
Part 3
What do you think makes a person successful in business?
I believe a combination of vision and execution is essential. Successful entrepreneurs can anticipate trends and adapt quickly. Additionally, interpersonal skills matter enormously — building trust with clients, partners, and employees is often what sustains a business long-term. A bit of timing and luck also play a role, of course.
我认为远见与执行力的结合是不可或缺的。成功的企业家能够预判趋势并快速适应。此外，人际交往能力也极为重要——与客户、合作伙伴和员工建立信任往往是企业长期存续的关键。当然，时机和运气也有一定作用。
Part 3
What ethical responsibilities do successful business owners have?
Beyond profit, they should consider their impact on employees, communities, and the environment. A business that exploits workers or pollutes for profit isn't truly successful—it's just externalizing costs onto society. Long-term success requires balancing financial goals with social responsibility.
除了利润，他们应该考虑对员工、社区和环境的影响。一个剥削工人或为利润而污染的企业不是真正的成功——它只是将成本外部化给社会。长期成功需要在财务目标和社会责任之间取得平衡。
Part 2&3改变重要想法
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you changed your opinion about something important. You should say: what the opinion was, why you changed it, when it happened, and explain how you feel about this change.
描述一次你对某件重要事情改变了看法的经历。你应该说：原来的看法是什么 / 为什么改变 / 什么时候发生的 / 并解释你对这个改变的感受
Answer
One important idea I changed was how vocabulary should be learned. I used to treat language as a list of isolated words to memorize. While preparing for IELTS, I found that knowing a word did not mean I could use it when speaking.

I then started breaking articles into useful phrase chunks. I treated them like Lego pieces and practised combining them in different answers. While using AI, I also met the same expressions repeatedly in meaningful conversations, so some of them became familiar almost naturally.

Now I believe context and repeated use matter more than isolated memorization. This change made speaking feel more practical and reduced the pressure of remembering thousands of separate words.
我改变过的一个重要想法，是应该怎样学习词汇。过去我把语言看成需要背诵的一串零散单词。备考雅思时我发现，认识一个词并不代表开口时能用出来。

后来我开始把文章拆成实用的完整语块，把它们当成乐高积木，在不同答案里练习组合。使用 AI 时，我也会在有意义的交流中反复遇到同一些表达，因此有些词几乎自然地熟悉了。

现在我认为，语境和反复使用比孤立背诵更重要。这个变化让口语更实用，也减少了记忆成千上万个零散单词的压力。
Part 3
Why do people sometimes find it hard to change their opinions?
People often resist changing their views because their beliefs are deeply intertwined with their identity and sense of self. Admitting you were wrong can feel like a personal failure. Additionally, confirmation bias leads people to seek information that supports their existing views while dismissing contradictory evidence. It takes real open-mindedness to shift deeply held beliefs.
人们常常抗拒改变观点，因为他们的信念与自我认同感深度交织。承认自己错了会让人感觉像是一种个人失败。此外，确认偏差使人倾向于寻找支持自己现有观点的信息，同时忽视矛盾的证据。要改变根深蒂固的信念，需要真正的开放心态。
Part 3
Why is it difficult for people to admit they were wrong?
Because our beliefs become part of our identity. Admitting we're wrong feels like admitting a personal flaw. But I've learned that changing your mind is actually a sign of strength—it means you're still thinking, still growing, still willing to take part in new evidence rather than cling to comfortable delusions.
因为我们的信念成为我们身份的一部分。承认自己错了感觉像是承认个人缺陷。但我学到，改变想法实际上是力量的标志——这意味着你仍在思考、仍在成长、仍愿意接受新证据，而不是固守舒适的错觉。
Part 2&3长期追求/目标
▶
Cue Card
Describe a long-term goal that you have been working towards. You should say: what the goal is, how long you have been working on it, what you have done to achieve it, and explain why this goal is important to you.
描述一个你一直在努力实现的长期目标。你应该说：这个目标是什么 / 你努力了多久 / 你做了什么来实现它 / 并解释为什么这个目标对你很重要
Answer
A long-term goal of mine is to express myself comfortably in English, not only to pass one exam. IELTS is my current milestone, but the larger goal is to use English naturally when I explore AI tools, talk with foreign friends, or enter a field that genuinely interests me.

I have been changing the way I learn. Instead of memorizing isolated words, I break articles into phrase chunks and practise combining them like Lego pieces. I also use AI and real conversations to meet the same language repeatedly in context.

This matters to me because the desire to communicate can keep learning alive after an exam is over. A score is useful, but being able to understand people and express a real idea is the result I want to keep.
我的一个长期目标是能够自在地用英语表达自己，而不只是通过一次考试。雅思是眼前的阶段目标，但更大的目标，是在探索 AI 工具、和外国朋友交流，或进入自己真正感兴趣的领域时自然使用英语。

我一直在改变学习方式：不再背零散单词，而是把文章拆成语块，像乐高一样练习组合；也通过 AI 和真实交流，在语境中反复接触同样的语言。

这个目标重要，是因为交流的渴望能让学习在考试结束后继续存在。分数有用，但真正理解别人、表达真实想法，才是我希望长期保留的能力。
Part 3
Do you think it's important for young people to have long-term goals?
Absolutely. Long-term goals give young people a sense of direction and help them make important choices rather than drifting aimlessly. However, I also think it's important to remain flexible — goals can evolve as we grow and gain new experiences. The key is to have something to strive towards while staying open to new possibilities that may reshape those aspirations.
当然。长期目标给年轻人一种方向感，帮助他们做出有意义的选择，而不是漫无目的地随波逐流。不过我也认为保持灵活性很重要——目标会随着我们的成长和新经历而演变。关键是要有值得奋斗的方向，同时对可能重塑这些志向的新可能性保持开放。
Part 3
How do people's goals change as they get older?
Younger people often chase external validation—money, status, recognition. As people mature, goals tend to shift inward—toward meaning, relationships, and personal growth. It's not that ambition fades; it just gets redirected from impressing others to really satisfying yourself.
年轻人常常追求外部认可——金钱、地位、名声。随着人们成熟，目标往往向内转移——转向意义、人际关系和个人成长。这不是雄心消退了；它只是从给别人留下印象转向真正满足自己。
Part 2&3擅长学习和说语言的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person you know who is good at learning and speaking languages. You should say: who this person is, what languages they can speak, how they learned them, and explain why you think this person is good at languages.
描述一个你认识的语言学习和口语能力很强的人。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 他会说哪些语言 / 他是怎么学的 / 并解释为什么你觉得他擅长语言
Answer
I'd like to talk about Vianca, a Filipino friend I met during a one-month summer teaching program. She speaks English and very natural Chinese. During that month, she taught me useful English expressions, while I helped her with some Chinese words and pronunciation.

What impressed me most was how quickly she put new words into use. She did not wait until every sentence was perfect. She simply used Chinese to talk with local people and learn more from each conversation. For her, language was a tool for connecting with people, not just a school subject.

I think she is good at languages because she is curious and not afraid of making mistakes. Once, when I felt discouraged about my own English, she told me, “Never look down on yourself.” I still remember that. She showed me that confidence and real communication can make language learning much more natural.
我想讲讲 Vianca，她是我在一次为期一个月的暑期支教活动中认识的菲律宾朋友。她会说英语，中文也很自然。那个月里，她教我实用的英语表达，我帮她纠正一些中文词汇和发音。

最打动我的是，她会很快把新学的词用起来。她不会等到每句话都完美才开口，而是直接用中文和当地人交流，并从每次对话中继续学习。对她来说，语言是连接人的工具，而不只是一门学科。

我觉得她擅长语言，是因为她好奇，而且不怕犯错。有一次我对自己的英语感到泄气，她告诉我：“永远不要看低自己。”我一直记得这句话。她让我看到，自信和真实交流能让语言学习自然得多。
Part 3
Do you think some people are naturally better at learning languages than others?
Some people may learn languages faster, but talent is only one part of it. In my view, curiosity and the courage to use the language matter more. People improve when they keep listening, speaking, and learning from mistakes.
有些人学语言可能更快，但天赋只是一部分。在我看来，好奇心和真正使用语言的勇气更重要。只要持续听、持续说，并从错误中学习，人就会进步。
Part 3
How do children and adults differ in language learning ways?
Children usually learn through play and daily exposure, so they worry less about mistakes. Adults are better at planning and finding useful resources, but they may overthink grammar. A good method combines children's natural use of language with adults' ability to practise in a focused way.
儿童通常通过玩耍和日常接触来学习，所以他们不太担心犯错。成年人更会制定计划、寻找资源，却可能过度纠结语法。好的方法是把孩子自然使用语言的状态，与成年人有针对性的练习能力结合起来。
Part 2&3看过的现场比赛
▶
Cue Card
Describe a live sports match you watched. You should say: what sport it was, where you watched it, who you went with, and explain how you felt about the experience.
描述一场你观看过的现场体育比赛。你应该说：是什么运动 / 在哪里看的 / 和谁一起去的 / 并解释你对这次经历的感受
Answer
I'd like to talk about a football match I saw while helping at the event as a volunteer. I was there mainly to work, but I had time to watch part of the match.

I do not know much about football teams, so I cannot describe the players or the result in detail. Still, I could feel the excitement whenever the crowd reacted together. Watching people become focused on the same moment felt very different from seeing sport on a screen.

What made it memorable was the shared atmosphere of a live event. I only watched it along the way, but it is still the live match I remember most clearly.
我想讲一场自己在活动中做志愿者时看到的足球赛。我主要是去工作，不过中间有时间顺便看了一部分比赛。

我不太了解足球队，所以说不出球员或比赛结果的很多细节。不过每当人群一起做出反应时，我都能感受到那种兴奋。大家同时专注于一个瞬间，和隔着屏幕看体育很不一样。

最让我记住的是现场活动中大家共享的气氛。我只是工作过程中顺便看了看，但它仍是我记得最清楚的一场现场比赛。
Part 3
Why do you think people enjoy watching live sports events?
I think the appeal lies in the shared emotional intensity that simply cannot be replicated through a screen. When you are surrounded by thousands of people all experiencing the same moment — the collective gasp at a near miss, the eruption after a goal — there is a sense of collective identity that is quite powerful. It also provides a rare opportunity to step away from daily routines and fully immerse oneself in the present, alongside people who may have nothing else in common with you except a shared passion.
我认为这种吸引力在于一种共享的情感强度，这是通过屏幕无法复制的。当你被成千上万的人包围着，所有人都在经历同一个瞬间——一次险些进球时集体的倒吸气、进球后的爆发——那种集体认同感非常强大。它还提供了一个难得的机会，让你暂时远离日常琐事，与一群可能除了共同热爱之外毫无交集的人一起完全沉浸在当下。
Part 3
Do you think watching sports at home will replace watching live?
I don't think so. While TV broadcasts offer better camera angles and instant replays, they filter out the human energy that makes live sport genuinely thrilling. At a stadium, you're swept up in collective emotion—strangers hugging when a goal goes in. That can't be replicated on a couch. Live sports create a sense of community that broadcasts simply can't match.
我不这么认为。虽然电视转播提供更好的镜头角度和即时回放，但它们过滤掉了让现场体育真正激动人心的人性能量。在体育场里，你会被集体情绪裹挟——进球时陌生人互相拥抱。这在沙发上无法复制。现场赛事创造了一种转播无法匹敌的社区感。
📝阅读建议：核心内容，建议反复练习说。先理解故事脉络，再尝试用自己的话复述。

故事三：从家到城市

现在暂住杭州小旅店备考雅思，窗外是普通街道与楼宇；相关题目按需调用居住、区域和景色这一个现实场景。日常作息、整洁习惯、天府艺术公园、太古里、食物与动物等则各自用已确认的真实素材回答。

覆盖 24 个主题：Reading、Home/Accommodation、The area you live in、The city you live in、Hometown、Daily routine、Morning time、Tidiness、Building、Shopping、Gifts、Pets and Animals、Cars（Part 1）；喜欢的家但不想住、无聊的地方、高建筑、有趣的建筑、购物场所、花费超预期物品、当地新闻、特殊场合食物、动物故事书、种菜的人、爱护自然的人（Part 2&3）
完整故事 ▶

At the moment, I am staying in a small hotel in Hangzhou while preparing for IELTS. The window looks onto an ordinary street and several buildings. I have only recently arrived, so I am still getting to know the city and the area. For now, I mainly value the convenient transport and daily services around me.

中文翻译 ▶

目前我在杭州备考雅思，暂时住在一家小旅店。窗外是普通的街道和几栋楼。我刚来不久，还在逐渐认识这座城市和周边区域。目前我主要看重附近交通和日常服务的便利。

My routine is flexible: I sleep when I naturally feel tired and wake up without an alarm. Recently, I have focused mainly on IELTS. I care about cleanliness, but I do not care much about strict order. Clean objects can move and settle naturally, because new combinations sometimes give me ideas. However, I deal with dirt and rubbish quickly. When I cook, I often group the ingredients I find and decide what to make by instinct.

中文翻译 ▶

我的作息很灵活：困意自然出现时睡觉，然后不用闹钟自然醒。最近主要专注于雅思。我在意干净，但不太在意严格秩序。干净的物品可以自然流转和放置，因为新的组合有时会给我灵感；不过脏东西和垃圾会及时处理。做饭时，我常把遇到的食材凭感觉分组，再凭直觉决定怎么做。

During my university years, I was fascinated by how Chengdu's architecture is a mix of traditional and modern architecture—each building reflects the city's history and has its own character and stories. The landmark tower at IFS perfectly captures Chengdu's spirit. The Contemporary Art Gallery is a sleek glass-and-steel structure that cleverly blends modern aesthetics—it interacts with natural light and has an industrial yet refined aesthetic, even equipped with rainwater harvesting and solar panels. Taikoo Li is a beautifully designed open-air complex with narrow alleyways and open courtyards, an indie film bookstore. Modern design maximizes land use efficiency and serves as symbols of economic progress, but buildings with cultural and historical significance are what truly preserves heritage while accommodating growth.

中文翻译 ▶

成都的建筑是传统与现代的混合——每栋建筑反映着城市的历史，有自己的性格和故事。IFS的地标塔完美捕捉了成都的精神。当代艺术馆是玻璃钢结构，巧妙融合了现代美学——与自然光互动，有工业却精致的审美，还配了雨水收集和太阳能板。太古里是设计精美的开放式综合体——窄巷和开放庭院、独立书店。现代设计最大化土地利用效率，是经济进步的象征，但有文化和历史意义的建筑才真正在城市发展中保留遗产。

I once bought a snack order. The clerk recommended a higher-end model, and I decided to stretch my budget to nearly 6,000 yuan. Investing in quality pays off—it significantly improved my video projects. The local news was the opening of a new subway line—elderly residents had been advocating for better transport links for over a decade. The practical impact resonates with me—it also helps reduce carbon emissions. During Spring Festival, my family has traditional Sichuan hotpot. What makes it special is the ritual of gathering around the table. The numbing-spicy flavor is something I strongly associate with home. I'm learning to recreate a taste of home overseas. Food is a powerful cultural symbol that reinforces identity.

中文翻译 ▶

我有一次买零食超出了预算。我让同学帮我买零食，但她选了很贵的版本，总价150元，而我一周的零花钱只有100元左右。我只能打电话给爸爸解释。那以后我学会了，请别人帮忙买东西时一定要说得很具体。

When I was a child, I stumbled upon a book called "Illustrated Economics" in my parents' bookshelf. I didn't even know what economics meant back then, but it completely rewired how I see the world. The book taught me that economics isn't about calculating limited resources; it's a discipline of imagination. This concept of "having versus having more" rather than "having versus having nothing" raised my baseline for how I use time and energy. Before that framework, every moment felt like a draining choice between doing something and doing nothing. But once I understood opportunity cost, each moment became a choice between creating value and creating even more value—both options lead to growth, and either way, I win. It was like upgrading the operating system of my decision-making at age eight. My grandmother is passionate about growing vegetables on her balcony—tomatoes, green onions, and fresh herbs like cilantro. It keeps her physically active. What she loves most is the satisfaction of nurturing something from seed to harvest—a sense of self-sufficiency. The process itself is therapeutic and stress-relieving.

中文翻译 ▶

小时候我在父母书架上偶然发现了一本叫《图解经济学》的书。那时候我甚至不知道经济学是什么意思，但它彻底重构了我看世界的方式。这本书告诉我经济学不是计算有限资源，而是想象力的学科。"有与有更多"而非"有与没有"的概念，提高了我使用时间和精力的基准线。在那个框架之前，每一刻都像在做某事和什么都不做之间的消耗性选择。但一旦理解了机会成本，每一刻都变成了在创造价值和创造更多价值之间的选择——两条路都通向成长，不管怎样我都赢。这就像在我八岁时升级了决策的操作系统。我奶奶热衷于种菜——番茄、小葱和香菜等新鲜香草。这让她保持身体活跃。她最爱的是从种子到收获的培育满足感——自给自足的满足感。过程本身也疗愈和解压。

My grandmother is also someone who protects nature—she's been running a vegetable plot for nearly fifteen years, living in harmony with nature. She composts kitchen waste and uses no chemical pesticides. What moved me most is how she extends her care to the small creatures around her—leaving shallow dishes of water for stray cats and birds in summer. She always reminds me: nature doesn't need our management — it needs our respect. Individual actions create the cultural foundation for broader change.

中文翻译 ▶

奶奶也是一个爱护自然的人——她经营菜地近十五年，与自然和谐共处。她把厨余垃圾堆肥，不用化学农药。最让我感动的是她把关爱延伸到周围的小动物身上——夏天放浅碟子给流浪猫和鸟类饮水。她总是提醒我：自然不需要我们的管理——它需要的是我们的尊重。个人行为为更大范围的变革奠定了文化基础。

I learned a painful shopping lesson at boarding school. I asked a classmate to buy some snacks for me, but she chose the expensive versions and the total came to 150 yuan. My weekly allowance was only about 100 yuan, so I had to call my dad, feeling embarrassed. Since then, I have learned to be very specific when I ask someone to buy something for me.

中文翻译 ▶

我在寄宿学校学到过一次很痛的购物教训。我让一个同学帮我买零食，但她选了很贵的版本，总价150元，而我一周的零花钱只有100元左右。我只能尴尬地打电话给爸爸。那以后我学会了，请别人帮忙买东西时一定要说得很具体。

One evening at boarding school, the electricity suddenly went out. We were excited because we thought the evening class would be cancelled. Then the teacher came in with candles. In the end, the light was too dim, so the school sent us back to the dorm early. We tried hard not to look too pleased, but everyone was secretly happy.

中文翻译 ▶

寄宿学校有一天晚上突然停电。我们很高兴，以为晚自习取消了。然后老师带着蜡烛走进来。最后光线太暗，学校怕伤眼睛，就让我们提前回宿舍。我们拼命不让自己看起来太开心，但大家心里都在高兴。

Part 1Home/Accommodation / 住房
▶
Q
Do you live in a house or a flat?
At the moment, I am staying in a hotel in Hangzhou while preparing for IELTS. It is a temporary place rather than my family home, and the room faces an ordinary street and several buildings.
目前我在杭州备考雅思，暂时住在一家旅店。这里不是我的家庭住所，房间窗外就是一条普通街道和几栋楼。
Q
What is your favorite room in your home?

Part 2&3喜欢拜访但不想住的家
▶
Cue Card
Describe a home that you visited but would not like to live in. You should say: where it is, what it looks like, why you visited it, and explain why you would not like to live there.
描述一个你参观过但不想住的房子。你应该说：它在哪里 / 看起来什么样 / 你为什么去参观 / 并解释为什么你不想住在那里
Answer
The home I'd like to talk about is my aunt's house. I love visiting her because she is gentle and caring, almost like a mother to me. Whenever I visit, she makes me feel completely at home, and staying with her is genuinely happy.

However, I would not want to live there long-term. My aunt is incredibly kind and gives so much of herself to the family. She constantly takes on burdens for everyone, and over time I realised that even if I tried to share the load, it would not change the essential problem. Watching someone I love sacrifice so much, continuously and quietly, made me feel overwhelmed. I felt a kind of helplessness that made me want to step away rather than witness it every day.

So while I treasure every visit, I realised I am not someone who can watch a loved one give themselves away like that for the long term. It is not about the house itself — it is about the emotional weight of seeing a kind person pour herself out for others.
我想说的是我姑姑的家。我很喜欢去拜访她，因为她很温柔、很会照顾人，像妈妈一样。每次去她都让我感觉像在自己家一样，住在一起真的很幸福。

但我不想长期住在那里。姑姑太善良了，为家庭付出了太多。她不断承受着各种重担，后来我意识到就算我分担也改变不了本质问题。看着自己爱的人如此不断地消耗自己、默默付出，让我感到很崩溃。那种无力感让我想离开，不愿意每天见证这样的场景。

所以我珍惜每次拜访，但我意识到自己没法长期看着亲人这样奉献自己。这不是房子的问题，而是看到善良的人不断为别人倾注自己的情感重量。
Part 3
What are the differences between living in the city and the countryside?
Living in the city offers greater access to amenities such as healthcare, education, and entertainment, while the countryside provides a slower pace of life and cleaner environment. However, rural areas often lack the infrastructure that young professionals rely on.
城市生活能更好地获取医疗、教育和娱乐等设施，而乡村提供了更慢的生活节奏和更干净的环境。但农村地区往往缺乏年轻专业人士所依赖的基础设施。
Part 3
Do you think people's preferences for homes change as they age?
Absolutely. Young people tend to prefer vibrant urban environments with easy access to social activities, whereas older individuals often value peace and quiet, gravitating towards suburban or rural settings where they can enjoy a slower pace of life.
当然。年轻人倾向于喜欢充满活力的城市环境，方便参加社交活动；而年长者往往更看重安静，倾向于选择郊区或乡村，享受更慢的生活节奏。
Part 2&3无聊的地方
▶
Cue Card
Describe a place that you think is boring. You should say: where it is, when you went there, why you went there, and explain why you think it is boring.
描述一个你觉得无聊的地方。你应该说：它在哪里 / 你什么时候去的 / 你为什么去 / 并解释为什么你觉得它无聊
Answer
To be honest, I am usually not bored. Whenever I feel even slightly restless, I just go outside and walk. Walking and maybe grabbing something to eat along the way — that is enough to make boredom disappear completely.

I often walk around Taikoo Li, where there is a temple nearby that I visit to feel a sense of calm and strength. Or I wander to Tianfu Art Park. These are my regular walking spots.

So I do not really have a boring place to describe. My honest answer is that as long as I can walk and explore, I do not feel bored.
说实话，我通常不无聊。每当稍微感到无聊时，我就直接出去散步。走走、偶尔再买点吃的，就一点也不无聊了。

我经常逛到太古里那边，旁边有个庙，我常去感受宁静与力量感。或者走到天府艺术公园。这都是我常去的散步点。

所以我其实没有哪个无聊的地方可说。我的真实回答是只要能散步和探索，我就不会觉得无聊。
Part 3
Why do some people think museums are boring?
Some people find museums boring because they lack interactive elements or the exhibits aren't presented engagingly. Younger generations, accustomed to digital stimulation, may struggle to connect with static displays and lengthy text panels.
有些人觉得博物馆无聊是因为缺乏互动元素，或者展品呈现方式不够吸引人。习惯了数字刺激的年轻一代可能难以与静态展示和冗长的文字说明产生共鸣。
Part 3
How can public spaces be made more interesting?
Public spaces can be enhanced through creative design and interactive installations, such as public art, community events, and green spaces. Incorporating technology, like augmented reality guides, can also make spaces more engaging for visitors.
公共空间可以通过创意设计和互动装置来提升，比如公共艺术、社区活动和绿地。引入技术手段，如增强现实导览，也能让空间对访客更有吸引力。
Part 2&3喜欢或不喜欢的高建筑
▶
Cue Card
Describe a tall building you like or dislike. You should say: what it is, where it is, what it looks like, and explain why you like or dislike it.
描述一栋你喜欢或不喜欢的高楼。你应该说：它是什么 / 在哪里 / 看起来什么样 / 并解释为什么你喜欢或不喜欢它
Answer
The tall building I'd like to talk about is Chengdu IFS. It is a polished high-rise complex in the city centre with many luxury fashion and perfume brands. Anyone can walk in, test fragrances, collect scented cards, and sometimes receive small samples.

That became a special university memory for me. I kept several perfume cards from L'Artisan Parfumeur for four years, and each card still has its own clear scent. I found that amazing because most perfume cards lose their smell quite quickly.

Because of those cards, IFS became the place where my perfume-card collection began. I like the building not only because it looks refined, but because an ordinary visit gave me a small memory that has lasted for years.
我想讲的高楼是成都 IFS。它是市中心一座精致的高层综合体，里面有许多时尚和香水奢侈品牌。任何人都可以走进去试香、领取香卡，有时还能拿到一些小样。

这成了我大学时期一段很特别的记忆。我把阿蒂仙之香的几张香卡保存了四年，每张卡依然能清楚闻出各自的味道。这让我很震撼，因为普通香卡通常很快就没味道了。

因为这些香卡，IFS 成了我收集香卡这件事开始的地方。我喜欢它，不只是因为建筑精致，也因为一次普通的到访留下了持续多年的小记忆。
Part 3
Why do cities build tall buildings?
Cities build tall buildings primarily to maximize land use efficiency in densely populated areas. They also serve as symbols of economic progress and architectural ambition, helping cities establish their global identity.
城市建高楼主要是为了在人口密集区域最大化土地利用效率。它们也是经济进步和建筑雄心的象征，帮助城市建立全球辨识度。
Part 3
Do you think old buildings should be replaced by new tall buildings?
Not necessarily. Old buildings carry cultural and historical significance that new ones cannot replicate. A balanced way that preserves heritage while accommodating growth would be ideal.
不一定。老建筑承载着新建筑无法复制的历史文化价值。理想的做法是在保留遗产的同时兼顾城市发展的平衡方案。
Part 2&3有趣的建筑
▶
Cue Card
Describe an interesting building you have seen. You should say: what it is, where it is, what it looks like, and explain why you think it is interesting.
描述一栋你见过的有趣建筑。你应该说：它是什么 / 在哪里 / 看起来什么样 / 并解释为什么你觉得它有趣
Answer
The most interesting buildings I have visited are the museums in Tianfu Art Park in Chengdu. They stand beside lakes and green space, and their large curved roofs make the whole area feel carefully designed.

The shapes are modern, but they also feel Chinese. The Tianfu Art Museum was inspired by a hibiscus flower rising from water, while the neighbouring museum uses layered roof curves that resemble mountains and the roofs of traditional western Sichuan homes. To me, they look a little like opening petals or modern tiles spreading out.

I like them because the buildings are part of the park rather than separate from it. I can visit an exhibition, then walk outside and continue enjoying the design beside the water.
我去过最有趣的建筑，是成都天府艺术公园里的几座美术馆。它们位于湖水和绿地旁边，巨大的曲线屋顶让整个区域都显得经过精心设计。

造型很现代，却也有中式感觉。天府美术馆的灵感来自出水芙蓉，相邻美术馆层叠的屋顶曲线则像山峰，也呼应川西传统民居屋面。对我来说，它们有点像展开的花瓣，或向外铺开的现代瓦檐。

我喜欢它们，是因为建筑本身就是公园的一部分，并没有和环境分开。我可以先看展，再走到外面，继续在水边感受建筑设计。
Part 3
How does architecture affect people's mood?
Architecture significantly influences mood through elements like natural light, color schemes, and spatial layout. Well-designed spaces can elevate people's spirits, while poorly designed ones can cause stress and discomfort.
建筑通过自然光、色彩方案和空间布局等元素显著影响人的情绪。设计良好的空间能提升人的精神状态，而设计糟糕的空间则可能导致压力和不适。
Part 3
Should public buildings be beautiful or functional?
Ideally, they should be both. While functionality is essential for public buildings to serve their purpose, beauty enhances the user experience and contributes to civic pride, making the investment worthwhile.
理想情况下两者兼备。功能性对于公共建筑实现其用途至关重要，但美感提升了用户体验并有助于增强市民自豪感，使投资物有所值。

A piece of local news that caught my attention was about Typhoon Dolphin approaching Hangzhou. It was the first typhoon I had ever experienced, so I felt both excited and nervous. After seeing the warnings, I bought a large amount of food because I imagined being alone in a hotel with no supplies and nothing to eat.

In reality, it was much less dramatic than I expected. Food delivery stopped for only about half a day, and there was heavy rain for part of that day. The rest of the time was safe and fairly normal. The city returned to normal very quickly, and the weather was still hot afterwards.

The news interested me because it was my first direct experience of a typhoon warning. It also showed me how easily our imagination can make an unfamiliar event feel more frightening than it really is.
一条吸引我的当地新闻是台风“白海豚”接近杭州。这是我人生中第一次经历台风，所以既兴奋又紧张。看到预警后，我买了大量食物，因为我想象自己会一个人被困在物资不足的酒店里，甚至没有东西吃。

社交媒体让新闻更即时、更易获取，但也降低了可靠性，因为错误信息传播很快。人们现在碎片化地消费新闻，可能为了速度牺牲了深度和背景。

Part 2&3一本有重要影响的书
▶
Cue Card
Describe a book that had a significant impact on you. You should say: what the book is, when you read it, what it is about, and explain why it had such an impact on you.

Answer
I'd like to talk about a book called “Illustrated Economics”. I found it on my parents' bookshelf when I was a child. I did not even know what economics meant then, but the diagrams caught my attention.

The book used simple examples to explain value, choices, and trade-offs. I started to understand that every choice means giving up something else. It made me think more carefully about time, money, and what I really wanted.

Looking back, it was a simple book, but it was exactly what I needed at that age. It made big ideas feel less scary and taught me to ask better questions.
我想说一本叫《图解经济学》的书。小时候我在父母书架上翻到它。当时我甚至不知道经济学是什么意思，但图解吸引了我。

它用简单例子解释价值、选择和取舍。我开始理解每次选择都意味着放弃别的东西。它让我更认真地看待时间、钱，以及自己真正想要什么。

回头看它是一本很基础的书，但它正好是那个年纪的我需要的。它让大概念没那么可怕，也让我学会问更好的问题。

The person I'd like to talk about is my grandmother, who has been passionate about growing vegetables for as long as I can remember. She keeps a small garden on the balcony of her apartment in Chengdu, where she grows tomatoes, green onions, and fresh herbs like coriander. Every morning, she spends at least an hour tending to her plants — watering, pruning, and checking for pests. What I find impressive is how this hobby keeps her physically active and mentally sharp at her age. She often shares her homegrown vegetables with family and neighbors, which has made her quite popular in the community. I think what she loves most is the satisfaction of nurturing something from seed to harvest. As someone who grew up in a city where most food comes from supermarkets, I find her garden both fascinating and inspiring. She's taught me that growing your own food is not only rewarding but also a way to stay connected to nature, even in an urban environment. Her dedication has even inspired me to start a small herb garden of my own.
我想说的是我奶奶，从我记事起她就热衷于种菜。她在成都公寓的阳台上打理着一个小花园，种了番茄、小葱和香菜等新鲜香草。尽管空间有限，她用垂直种植和回收容器等创意技巧打造了令人惊讶的高产迷你菜园。每天早上她至少花一小时照料植物——浇水、修剪、检查虫害。让我觉得了不起的是这个爱好让她在高龄仍保持身体活跃和头脑敏锐。她常把自家种的蔬菜分享给家人和邻居，在社区里很受欢迎。我想她最爱的是从种子到收获那种培育的满足感。在城里长大、习惯了食物来自超市的我，觉得她的菜园既有趣又受启发。她教会我，自己种菜不仅有益，也是在城市环境中与自然保持连接的方式。她的投入甚至激励我也开始种自己的小香草园。

Part 2&3爱护自然的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person you know who cares about protecting nature. You should say: who this person is, what they do to protect nature, how long they have been doing it, and explain why you admire them.
描述一个你认识的人，他关心保护自然。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 他做了什么来保护自然 / 做了多久 / 并解释为什么你钦佩他
Answer
The person I'd like to describe is my grandmother, who has been tending a small vegetable garden on the outskirts of Chengdu for nearly fifteen years. What started as a simple retirement hobby slowly evolved into a real commitment to living in harmony with nature. Every morning, she walks to her plot with a woven basket, composting kitchen scraps along the way rather than throwing them out. She grows seasonal vegetables — tomatoes, cucumbers, leafy greens — entirely without chemical pesticides, relying instead on companion planting and natural pest control methods she learned from older neighbors. What touches me most, though, is how she extends her care to the small creatures around her. She leaves shallow dishes of water for stray cats and birds during Chengdu's sweltering summers, and she once nursed an injured sparrow back to health over the course of a week. When I visit her on weekends, I often help with the watering, and she always reminds me that nature doesn't need our management — it needs our respect. In a city that is rapidly modernizing, her quiet devotion to the land feels like a gentle but powerful form of environmental activism.
我想谈谈我的奶奶，她在成都郊外经营一小块菜地将近十五年了。最初只是退休后的简单爱好，后来逐渐发展成一种与自然和谐共处的真切承诺。每天早上，她提着编织篮走向菜地，沿途把厨余垃圾拿去堆肥而不是丢弃。她种应季蔬菜——番茄、黄瓜、叶菜——完全不用化学农药，而是依靠间作种植和从老邻居那里学来的天然防虫方法。最让我感动的是，她把关爱延伸到了周围的小动物身上。成都闷热的夏天里，她会在菜地边放浅碟子给流浪猫和鸟类饮水，她还曾经花一周时间照料一只受伤的麻雀直到康复。周末我去帮她浇水时，她总是提醒我：自然不需要我们的管理，它需要的是我们的尊重。在一座快速现代化的城市里，她对土地的默默守护，像是一种温柔却有力的环保行动。
Part 3
Do you think individuals can make a real difference in environmental protection?
Absolutely. While government policies and corporate initiatives are essential, I believe individual actions create the cultural foundation for larger change. When someone like my grandmother composts daily or grows food sustainably, she is not just reducing waste — she is influencing everyone around her, including me. Collective environmental awareness often starts with personal habits that ripple outward through families and communities, slowly shifting what society considers normal and acceptable.
当然可以。虽然政府政策和企业倡议至关重要，但我认为个人行为为更大范围的变革奠定了文化基础。当我奶奶每天堆肥、用可持续方式种菜时，她不仅仅是在减少浪费——她还在影响身边的每一个人，包括我。集体环保意识往往从个人习惯开始，像涟漪一样向外扩散到家庭和社区，逐渐改变社会认为正常和可接受的行为标准。
Part 3
How can individuals help environmental protection beyond personal habits?
Individual habits matter, but collective action matters more. People can join community groups, support environmental policies, and use their professional skills—whether in law, media, or technology—to amplify the movement. One person's composting is good; a thousand people pushing for policy change is life-changing.
个人习惯很重要，但集体行动更重要。人们可以加入社区团体、支持环境政策，并利用他们的专业技能——无论是法律、媒体还是技术——来放大运动。一个人的堆肥是好的；一千人推动政策变革则是变革性的。

这一组只保留真实且能复用的数字生活素材：自制雅思网站、Star Walk 2、打字、耳机与音乐、《图解经济学》和近期电影。广告或并非真实考题的内容不再硬套成人物经历。

完整故事 ▶

I use WeChat and Xiaohongshu daily—keeping in touch with friends, checking recommendations, and following IELTS accounts. But I try not to scroll mindlessly for hours. I watch videos on Bilibili and practice IELTS with BBC Learning English. Recently, with AI’s help, I made my own IELTS study website. Its functions and layout fit the way I study, so I use it a lot while preparing. For apps and websites, it is not really an either-or choice: a website can be added to a phone’s home screen and opened just like an app. Apps are often handier because phones are portable and the design fits a small screen. I do not wear a watch because I dislike anything tight around my wrist. I usually check the exact time on a screen, so to me a watch is more of an accessory than a tool. I type a lot because typing is a main way to express myself online. When ideas arrive quickly, I can cut, paste, and reorder my sentences until they make sense. I hardly handwrite now, though it may help with a second round of memory.

中文翻译 ▶

每天用微信和小红书——和朋友保持联系、查推荐、关注雅思账号。但尽量不无脑刷几个小时。在B站看视频，用BBC Learning English练雅思。最近，在 AI 的帮助下，我做了自己的雅思学习网站。功能和排列方式更贴合我的学习方式，所以备考时我经常使用。至于 App 和网站，并不真的是二选一：网站也能加到手机主屏幕上，像 App 一样随时打开。App 常常更方便，是因为手机便携、设计也适合小屏幕。我不戴手表，是因为不喜欢手腕上有紧的东西。我通常看屏幕上已经显示好的准确时间，所以对我来说手表更像装饰，而不是工具。我经常打字，因为打字是网络时代重要的表达方式。想法来得快时，我可以剪切、粘贴并调整句子顺序，直到表达清楚。现在我几乎不手写，不过手写可能有助于第二次记忆。

Science interests me most when I can see an idea clearly. That is why I like Star Walk 2. I can point my phone at the sky and identify stars or planets above me. It makes space feel less distant and easier to understand. The same app also answers questions about apps, science, outer space and stars, so I only need to remember one real example.

中文翻译 ▶

当我能清楚地看见一个概念时，科学最能吸引我。这就是我喜欢 Star Walk 2 的原因。把手机对准天空，就能辨认头顶的星星或行星。它让外太空显得没那么遥远，也更容易理解。同一个真实例子可以回答 App、科学、外太空和星星，不需要再背四套故事。

I choose music according to the state I am in. I may listen to K-pop when I want more energy, but now I choose gentle music such as lo-fi more often because I need calm space to think or rest. I am quiet in public and normally listen with headphones. When I am alone, I may hum softly once in a while, but I do not really sing.

中文翻译 ▶

我会根据当下的状态选择音乐。想要更多能量时可能听 K-pop，不过现在更多会选 lo-fi 这类温和的音乐，因为我需要安静下来思考或休息。我在公共场合很安静，通常会戴耳机听。一个人时偶尔会轻轻哼一下，但并不是真的唱歌。

My clothes have not changed much because my mother has usually made the final decision. She cares mainly about comfort, while I hope to have more freedom to choose what I like after I earn my own money. As a compromise, we normally choose safe, comfortable casual clothes together. We prefer physical shops because trying clothes on once is easier than dealing with online returns.

中文翻译 ▶

我的穿衣风格没有太大变化，因为过去通常由妈妈作最终决定。她主要关注舒适，而我希望以后自己赚钱后能更自由地选择喜欢的衣服。作为妥协，我们一般共同选择安全、舒适的休闲款。我们更喜欢实体店，因为一次试好比处理网购退换更省事。

When I was a child, I found a book called Illustrated Economics. It used pictures and simple examples, so ideas that sounded difficult became much easier to understand. It helped me see that choices are often not between having something and having nothing, but between one useful option and another useful option. That book had an important influence on how I make decisions.

中文翻译 ▶

小时候我看到过一本《图解经济学》。它用图画和简单例子解释概念，所以原本听起来很难的内容变得容易理解。它让我看到，很多选择并不是“拥有”和“一无所有”之间的选择，而是一个有用选项和另一个有用选项之间的选择。这本书对我的决策方式产生了重要影响。

The recent film I remember best is Welcome to the Dragon Restaurant. It follows Chinese people who initially believe a war in a small country has nothing to do with them. After friends from both sides die, that distance disappears. The film repeatedly lets a little hope appear and then shows how easily war destroys it. It made me feel that there are no truly lucky moments in war and that ordinary observers are not separate from human suffering.

我最近最能记住的电影是《欢迎来龙餐馆》。故事里的中国人起初认为，小国家里的战争与自己无关；但来自战争双方的朋友相继死去后，这种旁观距离消失了。电影一次次让一点希望出现，又让人看到战争多么轻易地将它摧毁。它让我感到，战争中没有真正幸运的时刻，普通旁观者也无法与人类的苦难完全分开。

Part 1Music / 音乐
▶
Q
What kind of music do you like?
It depends on the state I am in. When I need to feel calm, think, or take a break, I usually listen to gentle music such as lo-fi beats. If I feel excited, I may put on some K-pop, but these days I listen to calm music much more often.
要看我当下是什么状态。需要平静下来、思考或休息时，我通常会听一些温和的音乐，比如 lo-fi 节拍。兴奋的时候我可能会放 K-pop，不过现在更多时候还是听温和的音乐。
Q
Do you often listen to music?
Pretty much every day. I choose music according to what I need at that moment. Gentle music helps me slow down when I am studying or resting, so it has become a small part of my daily routine.
几乎每天都会。我会根据当下需要来选音乐。学习或休息时，温和的音乐能让我慢下来，所以它已经成了日常生活里的一个小部分。
Q
Do you think music tastes change as people get older?
Yes, I think they can. I used to listen to K-pop more often because I liked the energy. Now I more often need calm space for thinking or resting, so I naturally choose gentler music. It is less about getting older and more about what your life needs at the time.
会，我觉得会变。我以前更常听 K-pop，因为喜欢那种能量。现在我更常需要安静下来思考或休息的空间，所以自然会选更温和的音乐。这与其说是长大，不如说是当下的生活需要什么。
Part 1Singing / 唱歌
▶
Q
Do you like singing?
Not really. I am quite a quiet person, and in public I usually listen with headphones. When I am alone, I may hum softly once in a while, but I do not really sing.
不太喜欢。我是比较安静的人，在公共场合通常会戴耳机听。一个人时我偶尔会轻轻哼一下，但并不是真的会唱歌。
Q
Did you sing much as a child?
A little, mainly in music class at primary school. I did not think much about it then, but I have always been more comfortable listening quietly than singing in front of people.
会一点，主要是在小学音乐课上。当时没想太多，不过我一直更习惯安静地听，而不是在别人面前唱。
Q
Do you think anyone can learn to sing well?
I believe most people can improve significantly with training, but natural talent does play a role. It's like any skill — practice gets you far, but some people start with a head start. That said, singing isn't just about sounding good. It's about emotional expression, and that's something anyone can develop regardless of their vocal range.
我相信大多数人通过训练可以显著改善，但天赋确实有影响。就像任何技能一样——练习能走很远，但有些人起点更高。不过唱歌不只是好听，更是情感表达，这是任何人无论音域如何都可以发展的。
Part 1Social media / 社交媒体
▶
Q
Do you use social media often?
Yes, I use WeChat and Xiaohongshu daily. I mainly use them to stay in touch with friends and look up recommendations. I also follow some IELTS study accounts for tips. But I try not to scroll mindlessly for hours.
是的，我每天都用微信和小红书。主要用来和朋友保持联系、查推荐。我也关注了一些雅思学习账号获取技巧，但我会尽量不无脑刷几个小时。
Q
Has social media changed how people communicate?
Definitely. People share more online but talk less face-to-face. Even among my friends, conversations sometimes happen entirely through memes and stickers. It's convenient, but I feel we're losing the depth of real conversations.
当然。人们在网上分享得更多了，但面对面交流少了。甚至我朋友之间，对话有时候全靠表情包完成。很方便，但我觉得我们在失去真正对话的深度。
Q
Do you think you spend too much time on social media?
Sometimes, yes. I catch myself doomscrolling late at night when I should be sleeping. The infinite feed design makes it hard to stop — there's always one more post. I've started setting screen-time limits on certain apps, which helps but doesn't solve the problem entirely. It requires conscious effort.
有时候是的。我发现自己深夜该睡觉时还在不断刷。无限信息流的设计让人很难停下来——总觉得再看一条就好。我开始给某些App设屏幕时间限制，有帮助但没完全解决问题，还是需要有意识的自律。
Part 1Websites / 网站
▶
Q
What websites do you often visit?
Recently, I visit my own IELTS study website most often. I made it with AI’s help, and its functions and layout fit the way I study, so I use it a lot while preparing. I also use BBC Learning English and the British Council website when I need practice or test information.
最近我最常访问的是我自己的雅思学习网站。我在 AI 的帮助下做了它，功能和排列方式更贴合我的学习方式，所以备考时经常使用。我也会在需要练习或查考试信息时用 BBC Learning English 和英国文化协会的网站。
Q
Do you prefer apps or websites?
It depends, but it is not really an either-or choice now. A website can be added to a phone’s home screen and opened like an app. Traditional apps are often more convenient because phones are portable and the design fits a small screen, rather than because apps are always better than websites.
要看情况，但现在其实不真的是二选一。网站也能加到手机主屏幕上，像 App 一样打开。传统 App 往往更方便，是因为手机很便携、设计也适合小屏幕，而不只是因为 App 总比网站好。
Q
Are there any websites you used to visit but don't anymore?
Yes. When I was a child, I used a simple online games website called 7k7k. I stopped using it because I grew up, and I also got a phone with many more convenient apps. It is a good example of how our browsing habits change with our stage of life.
有。小时候我用过一个叫 7k7k 的小游戏网站。后来不用了，一是因为长大了，二是因为有了手机，上面有更多方便的 App。这很能说明浏览习惯会随着人生阶段变化。
Part 1Watch / 手表
▶
Q
Do you wear a watch?
No, I do not. I dislike anything tight around my wrist. People my age are used to checking the exact time already shown on a screen, so I do not really need a watch.
不戴。我不喜欢手腕上有紧的东西。我们这一代人习惯直接看屏幕上已经显示好的准确时间，所以我并不需要手表。
Q
Are watches still useful?
They can be useful for some people, especially if they want health data or quick notifications. But for me, a watch is more of an accessory than a tool. A phone already gives me the exact time and does much more.
对有些人来说有用，尤其是想看健康数据或快速通知的人。但对我来说，手表更像装饰，而不是工具。手机已经能给我准确时间，也能做更多事情。
Q
Have you ever received a watch as a gift?
No, I have not. It would be a thoughtful gift, but I would probably treat it as a piece of decoration rather than something I wear every day.
没有。它会是一份很有心意的礼物，但我大概会把它当作一件装饰品，而不是每天佩戴的东西。
Part 1Typing / 打字
▶
Q
Do you type a lot every day?
Yes, quite a lot. Typing is one of the main ways people express themselves online. I really want to put my thoughts into words and communicate, so when ideas come quickly, I type quickly too.
挺多的。打字是网络时代主要的表达方式之一。我很想把想法说出来、和人交流，所以想法来得快时，我打字也会很快。
Q
Do you prefer typing or handwriting?
I almost always prefer typing. I can slow down on purpose if I need to, but typing lets me cut, paste, and reorder sentences easily. My thoughts often arrive all at once, so my first version can be a little rushed; changing the order on a screen is much easier.
我几乎总是更喜欢打字。需要时我也可以刻意慢下来，但打字能让我方便地剪切、粘贴并调整句子顺序。我的想法常常一下子同时冒出来，所以初稿有点着急、顺序也乱；在屏幕上调整顺序会容易得多。
Q
Has typing changed the way you write?
Definitely. It makes changing my wording and sentence order immediate. I do not handwrite much now. Handwriting may have one advantage: it can help with a second round of memory, because you slow down and process the information again.
确实。它让我可以立刻改用词和句子顺序。现在我很少手写。手写可能有一个优势：它能帮助第二次记忆，因为你会慢下来，再处理一遍信息。
Part 1Science / 科学
▶
Q
Are you interested in science?
I am interested in some areas of science, especially astronomy. An app called Star Walk 2 shows the real positions of stars around the Earth, which made space feel much more concrete to me.
我对部分科学领域感兴趣，尤其是天文学。一个叫 Star Walk 2 的程序会显示星星在地球周围的真实位置，这让太空对我来说具体了很多。
Q
Did you like science subjects in school?
Not every subject. I found some school science too abstract when it was only in a textbook. I became more interested when I could see an idea working in a real example, such as locating constellations with an app.
不是每一科都喜欢。如果只在课本里，我会觉得有些科学内容太抽象。能在真实例子中看到一个概念如何运作时，比如用程序定位星座，我才会更感兴趣。
Q
Do you think science is important for everyday life?
Yes. Science helps us understand things we cannot easily see. For example, Star Walk 2 uses scientific information to show where stars and planets are, so an ordinary phone can help me understand the sky above me.
重要。科学帮助我们理解平时不容易直接看见的事物。例如 Star Walk 2 利用科学信息显示星星和行星的位置，所以一部普通手机就能帮助我理解头顶的天空。
Part 1Outer space and stars / 外太空与星星
▶
Q
Are you interested in outer space?
Yes, especially after using Star Walk 2. It shows where stars and constellations are in real time, so I can point my phone at the sky and understand what I am looking at.
感兴趣，尤其是在使用 Star Walk 2 之后。它会实时显示星星和星座的位置，所以我可以把手机对准天空，知道自己正在看什么。
Q
Do you like looking at stars?
Yes. What surprised me was learning that the twelve zodiac signs people casually talk about are based on real groups of stars that have been there for a very long time. The app helps me connect those familiar names with the actual sky.
喜欢。让我惊讶的是，人们平时随口聊到的十二星座，其实对应着长期存在于天空中的真实星群。这个程序帮我把熟悉的名字和真正的天空联系起来。
Q
Do you think space exploration is worth the money?
I do, though I understand why some people question it. The immediate benefits aren't always visible, but space research has led to spin-off technologies like GPS, satellite communication, and water purification systems. Plus, the possibility of discovering habitable planets or signs of life could basically change how we see our place in the universe. It's an investment in long-term knowledge.
我觉得值得，虽然理解为什么有人质疑。直接好处不总是可见的，但太空研究带来了GPS、卫星通信和水净化系统等衍生技术。而且，发现宜居行星或生命迹象的可能性可能从根本上改变我们对自己在宇宙中位置的看待。这是对长期知识的投资。
Part 1Headphone / 耳机
▶
Q
Do you use headphones often?
Yes, almost every day. I am quite a quiet person, so in public I usually listen with headphones. They let me listen to music without disturbing other people, and they give me a little personal space.
对，几乎每天都用。我是比较安静的人，所以在公共场合通常会戴耳机听。这样既能听音乐、不打扰别人，也能给自己留一点私人空间。
Q
When do you take off your headphones?
I take them off when I am talking to someone or having a meal with family or friends. I use headphones to stay quiet in public, not to avoid people. It is important to be present in a real conversation.
和人说话，或者和家人朋友吃饭时，我会摘下来。我戴耳机是为了在公共场合保持安静，不是为了躲开别人。真实交流中专心在场很重要。
Q
In what situations should people not wear headphones?
People should not wear them when crossing the street or walking near traffic, because they need to hear warnings. They should also take them off during a conversation, a class, or a meeting. Headphones are useful, but safety and real interaction come first.
人们在过马路或靠近车流时不该戴，因为需要听见警告。谈话、上课或开会时也应该摘下来。耳机有用，但安全和真实交流更重要。

What kind of clothes do you usually wear?
I usually wear safe, comfortable casual clothes. My mother cares most about comfort, while I also want some choice in style, so simple casual pieces are usually our compromise.
我通常穿稳妥、舒适的休闲服。妈妈最关注舒适，我也希望在款式上有些选择，所以简单的休闲款通常是我们的折中。
Q
Who buys clothes for you?
My mother has usually made most clothing decisions. She prefers taking me to physical stores so we can buy the right size once, because returning unsuitable clothes bought online is troublesome.
过去大部分衣服主要由妈妈决定。她更愿意带我去实体店一次买到合适尺码，因为网购不合适后退换比较麻烦。
Q
Has your style changed as you've gotten older?
Not really, because my mother has decided what I wear since I was young. In the future, when I earn my own money, I hope to have more freedom to find out what I genuinely like.
没有太大变化，因为从小主要都是妈妈决定我穿什么。以后自己赚钱后，我希望有更多自由，慢慢发现自己真正喜欢的风格。
Part 2&3Apps / 程序
▶
Cue Card
Describe an app you use often. You should say: what the app is / how long you have used it / what you use it for / and explain why you find it useful.
描述一个你经常使用的App。你应该说：这个App是什么 / 你用了多久 / 你用它做什么 / 并解释为什么你觉得它有用
Answer
I'd like to talk about Star Walk 2, an astronomy app. I started using it because I was curious about stars but could not identify anything in the night sky.

The app uses my location and the direction of my phone to show the real-time positions of stars, planets, and constellations. I can point the screen in any direction and see what is above or even below the horizon.

What I find most useful is that it turns an abstract subject into something I can explore directly. It also showed me that familiar zodiac signs are real groups of stars rather than only names used in casual conversation.
我想讲 Star Walk 2，一个天文程序。我开始用它，是因为我对星星很好奇，却无法辨认夜空中的东西。

它会结合我的位置和手机朝向，显示星星、行星和星座的实时位置。我可以把屏幕朝向任意方向，看到地平线上方、甚至下方有什么。

我觉得它最有用的地方，是把抽象的主题变成我可以直接探索的东西。它也让我知道，熟悉的十二星座是真实星群，并不只是闲聊时使用的名称。
Part 3
What makes an app successful?
I think a successful app needs to be intuitive and genuinely useful. Many apps fail because they're cluttered with unnecessary features. The best ones solve a specific problem simply and elegantly. User experience is everything — if people can't figure out how to use it within the first minute, they'll uninstall it without hesitation.
我觉得一个成功的App需要直观且真正有用。很多App失败是因为堆砌了不必要的功能。最好的App能简洁优雅地解决一个具体问题。用户体验就是一切——如果一分钟内搞不明白怎么用，人们会毫不犹豫地卸载。
Part 3
How do apps influence our daily decision-making?
They shape our choices in ways we don't even notice—recommendation algorithms, notification timing, interface design. The app that suggests a restaurant isn't just helpful; it's curating your reality. Being aware of this influence is the first step toward making really independent decisions.
它们以我们甚至没注意到的方式塑造我们的选择——推荐算法、通知时机、界面设计。推荐餐厅的不仅仅是帮忙；它在策划你的现实。意识到这种影响是做出真正独立决定的第一步。
Part 2&3想拥有的科技产品
▶
Cue Card
Describe a piece of technology you would like to own. You should say: what it is / how you know about it / what you would use it for / and explain why you want to own it.
描述一件你想拥有的科技产品。你应该说：它是什么 / 你怎么知道的 / 你会用它做什么 / 并解释为什么你想拥有它
Answer
I would like a pair of good noise-canceling headphones. I already use ordinary earphones in public because I am quiet and do not want to disturb other people.

A better pair could reduce background noise without forcing me to raise the volume. That would be useful when I study or walk through a busy area.

I do not need a particular brand. I mainly want something comfortable, practical and safe for my hearing.
我想要一副好用的降噪耳机。我在公共场合本来就会使用普通耳机，因为我比较安静，也不想打扰别人。

更好的耳机可以减少背景噪音，而不用逼着我调高音量，学习或走过热闹区域时会很实用。

我不需要特定品牌，主要希望它舒适、实用，而且对听力更安全。
Part 3
Do you think technology has made our lives better or worse?
Both, honestly. Technology has made communication and learning incredibly convenient, but it has also created new problems like screen addiction and reduced attention spans. The key is using technology mindfully rather than letting it control us. It's a tool, not a master.
说实话都有。技术让沟通和学习变得极其便利，但也带来了屏幕成瘾和注意力下降等新问题。关键是有意识地使用技术，而不是被它控制。它是工具，不是主人。
Part 3
Do you think society is too dependent on technology?
In some ways, yes. We've outsourced so many cognitive functions to devices—navigation, memory, calculation. The danger isn't the technology itself but the atrophy of skills we no longer practice. Balance means using tools without letting them replace our own mental capabilities.
在某些方面是的。我们已经把很多认知功能外包给了设备——导航、记忆、计算。危险不在于技术本身，而在于我们不再练习的技能萎缩。平衡意味着使用工具，而不让它们取代我们自己的心智能力。
Part 2&3遇到的科技问题
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time you had a problem with technology. You should say: what the problem was / when it happened / how you solved it / and explain how you felt about it.
描述一次你遇到技术问题的经历。你应该说：问题是什么 / 什么时候发生的 / 你怎么解决的 / 并解释你当时的感受
Answer
A recent technology problem happened while I was building my IELTS learning website with AI. I added a button that should collapse the complete story, but when I clicked it, only the first half disappeared. Several paragraphs were left above the topic cards.

At first, it looked like a button problem. After checking the HTML structure, I found that part of the story had been placed outside the collapsible container. I moved all story paragraphs into the same container and then checked the other stories for the same mistake.

I felt frustrated because the page looked almost correct, which made the bug easy to miss. But solving it taught me to check the structure, not only the visible result.
最近一次技术问题发生在我用 AI 制作雅思学习网站时。我加了一个应该收起完整故事的按钮，但点击后只有前半部分消失，还有几段文章留在主题卡片上方。

起初看起来像按钮有问题。检查 HTML 结构后，我发现一部分故事被放在了可收起容器之外。我把所有故事段落移进同一个容器，也检查了其他故事是否有同类错误。

我当时有些烦，因为页面看起来几乎正确，这让问题很容易被漏掉。不过解决它让我学会了，不仅要看页面结果，还要检查底层结构。
Part 3
Why do people become so dependent on technology?
Because technology has integrated into almost every aspect of modern life, from communication to transportation to entertainment. It offers convenience and efficiency that we've grown to rely on. The dependency becomes a problem when we lose basic skills as a result — like not being able to navigate without GPS.
因为技术已经融入了现代生活几乎方方面面，从沟通到交通到娱乐。它提供的便利和效率让我们越来越依赖。当这种依赖导致我们丧失基本技能时——比如没有GPS就不会认路——问题就出现了。
Part 3
How can we make technology more accessible to older generations?
The key is designing with empathy rather than just efficiency. Larger text, simpler interfaces, patient tutorials. But equally important is intergenerational mentorship—younger family members spending time teaching, not just fixing problems remotely. Technology should connect, not isolate.
关键在于以同理心设计而非仅仅追求效率。更大的文字、更简单的界面、耐心的教程。但同样重要的是代际指导——年轻家庭成员花时间教学，而不是仅仅远程解决问题。技术应该连接，而非孤立。

描述一次电子设备出故障的经历。你应该说：是什么设备 / 什么时候发生的 / 你怎么处理的 / 并解释它对你造成了什么影响
Answer
A recent device problem happened when my phone battery began draining much faster than usual while I was preparing for IELTS. I needed the phone for study apps, online dictionaries and ordinary communication, so it became inconvenient quite quickly.

I first closed background apps and turned on power-saving mode, but the problem continued. I then took the phone to a repair shop and learned that the battery had aged and needed replacing. After the replacement, it worked normally again.

The experience was annoying, but the solution was simple. It reminded me that when one device supports many parts of daily life, even a small fault can interrupt the whole routine.
最近一次电子设备问题，是我备考雅思时手机电池开始比平时掉电快很多。学习 App、在线词典和日常沟通都要用手机，所以很快就变得不方便。

我先关掉后台应用并打开省电模式，但问题依然存在。后来我把手机送去维修，才知道是电池老化，需要更换。换完以后就恢复正常了。

这件事有些烦人，但解决方式并不复杂。它提醒我，当一个设备支撑着日常生活的很多部分时，一个小故障也可能打乱整个作息。
Part 3
How can people reduce their reliance on electronic devices?
Setting boundaries is the most effective way. For example, designating phone-free hours or keeping devices out of the bedroom. interesting in offline activities like exercise or reading also helps. It's about building habits that don't revolve around screens.
设定边界是最有效的方法。比如设定无手机时段，或者不把设备带进卧室。参与运动、阅读等线下活动也有帮助。关键是建立不围绕屏幕的生活习惯。
Part 3
Why do people often choose to replace rather than repair broken devices?
Planned obsolescence and the high cost of repair relative to replacement. Manufacturers make devices hard to fix, and authorized repairs are expensive. But this creates massive electronic waste. Right-to-repair legislation could change this, forcing companies to design for longevity.
计划性淘汰以及相对于更换而言高昂的维修成本。制造商让设备难以修复，授权维修又很贵。但这造成了大量电子垃圾。维修权立法可以改变这一点，迫使公司设计得更耐用。

So rather than describing one particular video, my honest feeling is that the format itself is designed for consumption, not for memory. That is not necessarily a bad thing — sometimes people just need something to fill a quiet moment. But it means I cannot point to one and say it was fascinating in a lasting way.
说实话，网上的短视频太多了，我完全想不起哪个具体的视频。短视频到处都是，你只要一直刷，它们就混在一起了。

我觉得短视频本身就不是用来记忆的。它们只是源源不断地存在，把人融化进去，填满碎片时间。你看了一个又一个，不知不觉一小时就过去了，却一个都记不住。

所以与其说某个视频多有趣，我真实的感受是这种形式本身就是为消费设计的，不是为记忆设计的。这不一定坏事——有时候人就是需要东西填满安静的时刻。但这意味着我没法指出某一个说它有多令人难忘。
Part 3
Do you think online videos are replacing traditional media?
To a large extent, yes. Young people increasingly turn to platforms like Bilibili or YouTube for entertainment and information. Traditional TV still has its audience, but the trend is clearly shifting toward on-demand, user-generated content that viewers can engage with through comments and discussions.
在很大程度上是的。年轻人越来越多地转向B站或YouTube等平台获取娱乐和信息。传统电视仍有观众，但趋势明显在转向点播式、用户生成内容，观众还能通过评论和讨论参与互动。
Part 3
How has short-form video changed how we consume information?
It's fragmented our attention spans and prioritized entertainment over depth. Complex issues get reduced to 60-second takes. But it also democratizes content creation—anyone can share expertise. The challenge is developing the discipline to seek long-form content when the topic deserves it.
它分散了我们的注意力，将娱乐置于深度之上。复杂问题被简化为60秒的说法。但它也实现了内容创作的民主化——任何人都可以分享专业知识。挑战在于培养在话题需要时寻找长篇内容的自律。

对我来说，我也通常用手机打发时间，跟我认识的大多数人一样。不管是短视频、消息还是浏览，手机已经基本取代了电视。手机更个人、更方便——我可以随时选择看什么。

所以我没法具体描述某个电视节目或网络节目。我的真实回答是我的观看习惯已经完全转移到手机上了，我觉得我这个年纪的人很多都是这样。
Part 3
Do documentaries have educational value?
Absolutely. Well-made documentaries can teach viewers about cultures, science, and history in a way that textbooks can't. They combine visual storytelling with factual information, making complex topics accessible and memorable. That's why they're widely used in education.
当然。优秀的纪录片能以教科书无法做到的方式教观众了解文化、科学和历史。它们把视觉叙事和事实信息结合在一起，让复杂的话题变得易懂且令人印象深刻。这就是为什么纪录片在教育中被广泛使用。
Part 3
How has streaming changed the television industry?
It's disrupted the traditional advertising model and shifted power to consumers. People now binge-watch entire seasons, demand global content, and cancel subscriptions easily. This pressure has forced studios to prioritize quality over quantity—a show lives or dies by word of mouth within the first week. The competition is fiercer, but the winners are often more innovative.
它颠覆了传统广告模式，将权力转移给消费者。人们现在可以一次性看完整季、要求全球内容、轻松取消订阅。这种压力迫使工作室优先考虑质量而非数量——一部剧在第一周内就靠口碑决定生死。竞争更激烈，但赢家往往更具创新性。

这条广告让人印象深刻的地方在于它如何有效地把名人形象和产品联系在一起。重点不是香味本身——而是明星光环让产品令人难忘。不过我也知道名人代言可能有误导性，所以买之前我还是会自己做研究。
Part 3
Should celebrities be responsible for the products they advertise?
I believe they should bear some responsibility. When a celebrity endorses a product, their reputation lends credibility to it. If the product turns out to be harmful or misleading, the celebrity's image should also take a hit. It's an ethical obligation, not just a business transaction.
我认为他们应该承担一定责任。当名人代言产品时，他们的声誉为产品背书。如果产品被证明有害或误导，名人的形象也应该受损。这是一种道德义务，不只是商业交易。
Part 3
Why do companies use celebrities in advertisements?
Because celebrities embody aspirational qualities that brands want associated with their products. When consumers see someone they admire using a product, they subconsciously transfer their positive feelings about the celebrity onto the brand. It's emotional association rather than rational evaluation. With influence comes responsibility—the celebrity's reputation becomes the product's credibility.
因为名人体现了品牌希望与其产品关联的令人向往的特质。当消费者看到他们钦佩的人使用某产品时，会潜意识地将对名人的正面感受转移到品牌上。这是情感关联而非理性评估。影响力伴随着责任——名人的声誉变成了产品的可信度。

That said, the first few minutes were uncomfortable. Like most people my age, I'm so accustomed to having my phone within arm's reach that its absence felt almost unnatural. I kept instinctively reaching for my pocket. But slowly, I settled into a state of deep concentration that I rarely achieve in daily life. This experience made me realize how much our phones fragment our attention. Now, I sometimes intentionally put my phone in another room when studying, to recreate that exam-like focus.
我想说雅思考试，这是一种严禁使用手机的场合。我在成都一家语言中心参加模考时亲身体验过。进考场前，我们必须关机并放到外面指定区域。监考员明确说如果发现任何候选人身上有手机，将立即取消考试资格。考试中我反而感到一种奇特的解放感。没有查看通知的诱惑，我能完全专注于阅读和写作。不过最初几分钟确实不太舒服。和大多数同龄人一样，我习惯了手机触手可及，它的缺席几乎让我觉得不自然，我总下意识去摸口袋。但渐渐地，我进入了一种日常生活中很少能达到的深度专注状态。这次经历让我意识到手机有多么碎片化我们的注意力。现在我有时会故意把手机放到另一个房间学习，来重现那种考试般的专注。
Part 3
Should phones be banned in schools?
I think a partial ban makes sense. Phones can be valuable learning tools, but they're also major distractions. Allowing phones during breaks but prohibiting them during class seems like a reasonable compromise that balances benefits and drawbacks.
我觉得部分禁止比较合理。手机可以是很好的学习工具，但也是主要的干扰源。课间允许用但上课禁止，似乎是一个平衡利弊的合理折中方案。
Part 3
Is it becoming harder for people to disconnect from their phones?
Definitely. Phones are now designed to be habit-forming — notifications, infinite scroll, and social feedback loops all exploit our brain's reward system. Many people experience phantom vibrations even when their phone isn't there. Breaking free requires intentional effort, like setting screen-time limits or creating phone-free zones at home. It's a modern challenge that previous generations never faced.
确实如此。手机现在被设计成容易让人上瘾的——通知、无限滚动和社交反馈回路都在利用我们大脑的奖励系统。很多人甚至会在手机不在时感觉到幻震。摆脱这种习惯需要有意识的努力，比如设置屏幕时间限制或在家里设立无手机区域。这是上一代人从未面临的现代挑战。

Do you think live music events will become less popular in the future?
I doubt it. While streaming services have made recorded music more accessible than ever, they can't replace the communal atmosphere of a live event. People crave shared experiences — singing along with a crowd, feeling the energy of the performers. If anything, as digital life becomes more isolated, live events may become even more valued as a way to connect with others in person.

隐私的丧失和不断维持完美形象的压力。每一个行为都被审视。更糟糕的是拟社会关系——粉丝觉得他们亲密地了解名人，这创造了不切实际的期望，甚至可能对名人造成危险。

I eventually made it back to school safely. After that experience, all I could think about was gratitude for living in a peaceful country. That night ride taught me more about fear and gratitude than any comfortable daytime trip ever could.

How has technology changed the way people travel?
Technology has made travel more accessible — online booking, GPS navigation, and translation apps have removed many barriers. But it's also made people less adventurous. When everything is planned and mapped out in advance, there's less room for spontaneous discovery, which is often the most memorable part of traveling.
技术让旅行变得更便利——在线预订、GPS导航和翻译App消除了很多障碍。但也让人们变得不那么有冒险精神。当一切都被提前规划和导航好，留给自发探索的空间就少了，而那往往才是旅行中最难忘的部分。
Part 3
How might transportation habits change in the next decade?
I think we'll see a shift toward micro-mobility and shared transport—electric bikes, scooters, carpooling apps. Urban design will prioritize pedestrians and cyclists over cars. The challenge is infrastructure: building bike lanes and charging stations fast enough to match demand.
我想我们会看到向微型出行和共享交通的转变——电动自行车、滑板车、拼车应用。城市设计将优先考虑行人和骑行者而非汽车。挑战在于基础设施：建设自行车道和充电站的速度要跟上需求。
Part 2&3长时间未收到回复
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time you waited a long time for a reply. You should say: what you were waiting for / how long you waited / what you did while waiting / and explain how you felt about it.
描述一次你等了很久才收到回复的经历。你应该说：你在等什么 / 等了多久 / 等待时做了什么 / 并解释你的感受
Answer
I'd like to talk about a deeply unsettling experience that actually changed how I understand human relationships. A close friend of mine—let me call him my closest friend—suddenly stopped responding to my messages. At first I assumed he was busy, but days turned into weeks, and the silence became deafening. What shocked me wasn't just the rejection—it was realizing that such a small act, merely not responding, could trigger genuine fear in me, someone who prides himself on being rational and stable. I eventually reached out to him directly, and he added me back, only to go silent again. This sent me down a rabbit hole of research. I discovered that human relationships function like neural networks: we depend on consistent feedback loops to maintain connection, just as neurons require stable neurotransmitter release. When feedback breaks, the system panics—not because of logical threat, but because uncertainty itself is a stressor. I suddenly understood the wife ignored by her husband, the child isolated at school, the toddler left unattended by a busy mother. Society runs on reciprocal feedback at every level. Broken feedback loops create the same biological stress as physical danger, yet we have no vocabulary to name this pain because there's no "visible" perpetrator. This experience became the seed of my fascination with how communication systems shape human wellbeing.
我想说我一个朋友突然停止回复我消息的经历。起初我以为他只是忙，但几天变成了几周，沉默变得震耳欲聋。让我震惊的不仅仅是被拒绝——而是意识到如此微小的行为，仅仅是不回复，竟然能在自诩理性和稳定的我身上触发真正的恐惧。我最终直接联系了他，他又加回了我，但再次沉默。这让我开始深入研究。我发现人际关系就像神经网络：我们依赖持续的反馈回路来维持连接，就像神经元需要稳定的神经递质释放。当反馈断裂时，系统会恐慌——不是因为逻辑上的威胁，而是因为不确定性本身就是一种压力源。我突然理解了被丈夫忽视的妻子、在学校被孤立的孩子、被忙碌母亲忽视等待的幼儿。社会在各个层面都依赖互惠反馈。断裂的反馈回路产生的生物压力与物理危险相同，但我们却没有词汇来命名这种痛苦，因为没有"可见"的加害者。这次经历成为我对沟通系统如何塑造人类幸福产生迷恋的种子。
Part 3
Has technology made people more or less patient?
Less patient, I'd say. We've become so accustomed to instant communication that any delay feels unacceptable. Years ago, waiting weeks for a letter was normal. Now, if someone doesn't reply within hours, we start to worry. Technology has raised our expectations for speed to an unrealistic level.
我觉得是更没耐心了。我们太习惯即时通讯了，任何延迟都觉得不可接受。多年前等几周一封信是正常的，现在如果几个小时没收到回复就开始焦虑。技术把我们对速度的期望提高到了不现实的水平。
Part 3
How has instant communication affected our patience?
It's eroded our tolerance for waiting. We expect immediate replies and get anxious when they don't come. But some things inherently require time—creative work, important decisions, important relationships. The skill we need to relearn is distinguishing between urgent and important, and giving important things the time they deserve.
它侵蚀了我们等待的容忍度。我们期待立即回复，如果没有到来就会焦虑。但有些事情本质上需要时间——创造性工作、重要决定、有意义的关系。我们需要重新学习的技能是区分紧急和重要，并给予重要事情应得的时间。
Part 2&3近期观影
▶
Cue Card
Describe a film you watched recently. You should say: what the film was, where you watched it, what it was about, and explain whether you enjoyed it.
描述一部你最近看的电影。你应该说：电影是什么 / 在哪里看的 / 讲了什么 / 并解释你是否喜欢它
Answer
The most memorable film I've seen recently is called "Welcome to Dragon Restaurant." I watched it at a cinema in Hangzhou. It is about a Chinese man who goes to a small country in the Middle East and helps run a restaurant. At first, he sees himself as an outsider to the war between that country and the United States.

The restaurant survives partly because two friends help him. One is his local business partner, and the other is an American soldier. When both of them are later killed, he can no longer believe that the war has nothing to do with him. An officer asks him, “Do you still remember that this war has nothing to do with you?” That question pulls him—and the audience—out of the role of a spectator.

What shocked me most was that every small chance of hope is destroyed by violence. Even a child is misled into thinking that becoming a human bomb is a heroic path. Many films give the audience hope and finally end with everyone safe, but this film does not. It makes each possible escape disappear, one after another.

So I would not say I enjoyed it in a relaxing way, but it is the one film whose story I can still remember clearly. It made me understand that no one is completely outside a human tragedy. We should truly fear and respect war instead of thinking that it has nothing to do with us.
我最近看过、也最难忘的电影叫《欢迎来龙餐馆》。我是在杭州的一家电影院看的。它讲的是一个中国人来到中东一个小国，并参与经营一家餐馆。起初，他觉得自己是那场战争之外的人，因为交战双方是当地国家和美国。

餐馆能经营下去，一部分靠两位朋友的帮助。一位是他的当地合伙人，另一位是美国士兵。后来两人都死了，他再也无法相信战争与自己无关。一位军官问他：“你还记得你和这场战争没有关系吗？”这个问题把他，也把观众，从旁观者的位置拉了出来。

最震撼我的是，每一点可能的希望都会被暴力毁掉。甚至有一个孩子被蒙蔽，以为成为人肉炸弹是一条英雄之路。很多电影会给观众希望，最后让所有人平安团聚，但这部电影没有。它让每一种可能的侥幸一个接一个地消失。

所以我不会说它是一部让人放松、享受的电影，但它是我唯一能清楚记住情节的电影。它让我明白，没有人能完全置身于人类的苦难之外。我们应该真正敬畏战争，而不是觉得它与自己无关。
Part 3
Do you think documentaries can change people's behavior?
I do, though I think the impact is often slow rather than immediate. A well-made documentary plants seeds of awareness that may take root over time. The key, I believe, is emotional engagement over information dumping. When viewers form a personal connection with a story or a character on screen, they are far more likely to reflect on their own behavior and consider change, compared to simply being presented with statistics and warnings that often feel distant and abstract.
我认为可以，不过这种影响通常是渐进的而非立竿见影的。一部优秀的纪录片播下意识的种子，可能在日后生根发芽。我认为关键在于情感参与而非信息灌输。当观众与屏幕上的故事或人物建立个人情感连接时，他们远比仅仅被呈现统计数据和警告——那些往往显得遥远而抽象的东西——时更有可能反思自己的行为并考虑改变。
Part 3
How do film reviews influence audience expectations?
They frame our viewing experience before we even enter the theater. A glowing review raises expectations that the film may not meet; a negative one might discourage us from something we'd actually enjoy. The best approach is to know what you personally value in cinema and let that guide you more than aggregate scores.
它们在我们进入影院之前就框定了我们的观影体验。好评会提高电影可能达不到的期望；差评可能会阻止我们欣赏实际上会喜欢的东西。最好的方法是了解你在电影中个人看重什么，让那比综合评分更指导你。
📝阅读建议：核心内容，建议反复练习说。先理解故事脉络，再尝试用自己的话复述。

故事五：成长之路

这一组以少量真实素材覆盖成长与人物类题目：小时候由散步找到平静，语言班朋友 Anti，表哥自学法律，乡村学校志愿活动中的跨文化外出，以及通过协作平台帮助更多想法落地的长期梦想。

覆盖 27 个主题：教师、人生阶段、童年活动、爱好、感到无聊、讲笑话、镜子、工作或学习、发小、为家人骄傲、给别人建议、微笑的场合、鼓励别人做不愿做的事、乐于助人的人、在团队中工作、擅长做计划的人、发挥想象力、重要决定、近期改变的计划、想从事医疗行业的人、早起经历、机智解决问题的人、别人帮助解决问题、想颁布的新法律、想从事的短期海外工作、喜欢画画的孩子、完美工作
完整故事 ▶

My main hobby is walking without a fixed destination. It began in childhood, when I discovered that going outside could help me calm down and slowly feel better during unhappy moments. Since then, I have enjoyed walking whether I am upset or already happy. I may follow the green lights, sit in a park, or pass through a busy area. Hobbies help us decompress and remember that life is not only about being productive all the time.

中文翻译 ▶

我最主要的爱好是没有固定目的地地散步。这个习惯始于小时候：在一些不开心的时刻，我发现到室外走走能让我恢复平静，心情也慢慢变好。从那以后，无论难过还是本来就很开心，我都喜欢散步。我可能跟着绿灯走、在公园坐一会儿，或者穿过热闹的街区。爱好帮助我们减压，也提醒我们生活并不只是时刻保持高效。

I have recently graduated after four years at university in Chengdu, and I am now preparing for IELTS while staying in Hangzhou. My long-term dream is to build a platform that helps people turn ideas into reality. People could find suitable partners, collaborate, and receive support from a wider network. My perfect work would be to keep developing that platform and work for a dream I genuinely believe in.

Anti is a friend I met at a language class. We got along almost immediately, and we often laugh at the same small details because we have a shared sense of humor. Another important person in my family is my cousin. He left a bank job, studied law by himself and succeeded on his second attempt. His experience shows that people can change the direction of their lives through persistence.

During a volunteer programme at a rural school, I invited four foreign volunteers to go into town. We tried fried shrimp and other snacks, and I showed them some local culture. Afterwards, Mr Liu helped me settle the group expenses. I told the volunteers he had paid for us, and all four came over to shake his hand and thank him. His practical help made the activity easier for everyone.

Part 1Teachers / 教师
▶
Q
Do you have a favorite teacher?
Yes, absolutely. My most memorable teacher was my high school Chinese literature teacher. She had this impressive ability to bring classical texts to life by connecting them to our daily experiences. She is actually one of the reasons I became interested in education myself.
是的，当然。我最难忘的老师是高中的语文老师。她有一种非凡的能力，能把经典文本和我们的日常经历联系起来，让它们活起来。其实她也是我对教育产生兴趣的原因之一。
Q
What makes a good teacher?
I think a good teacher needs genuine passion for their subject and empathy toward students. It's not just about delivering information but about noticing when a student is struggling and offering the right kind of encouragement at the right moment.
我认为好老师需要对所教科目有真正的热情，并对学生有同理心。不仅仅是传递信息，而是要能注意到学生什么时候遇到了困难，并在恰当的时刻给予恰当的鼓励。

我想过，但没有把它确定成职业计划。我才刚毕业，所以更想先探索自己的兴趣，再决定是否选择某一种固定职业。
