Q
Do your friends think you are funny?
Some of them do. Anti and I often laugh at ordinary situations because we have a shared sense of humor. It is less about telling impressive jokes and more about noticing the same funny details.
有些朋友会这样觉得。Anti 和我常常会因为普通情境一起笑，因为我们有相近的笑点。重点不是讲多厉害的笑话，而是我们会注意到同样有趣的细节。
Part 1Mirrors / 镜子
▶
Q
Do you often look at yourself in the mirror?
I would say a reasonable amount. I check before going out and perhaps once more during the day. I am not obsessed with my appearance; I just want to make sure I look clean and presentable.
算是合理的频率吧。出门前照一下，白天可能再看一次。我不算对外貌着迷，只是想确认自己看起来干净、得体。
Q
Do you have a mirror in your room?
Yes, I have a full-length mirror in my bedroom. It is actually quite useful, not just for checking my outfit but also for practicing my speaking. I sometimes rehearse IELTS answers in front of it to watch my facial expressions.
有的，我卧室有一面全身镜。其实挺有用的，不光是看穿搭，还可以练口语。我有时候会对着镜子排练雅思答案，观察自己的面部表情。
Q
Do you think mirrors are important?
In a practical sense, yes, they help us present ourselves properly. But on a deeper level, I think mirrors are also metaphorical. They force you to confront yourself, which can be uncomfortable but necessary for personal growth.
从实用角度说是的，它们帮我们得体地展示自己。但在更深的层面上，我觉得镜子也是隐喻性的。它们迫使你直面自己，这可能让人不舒服，但对个人成长是必要的。
Part 1Work/studies / 工作或学习
▶
Q
What are you studying at the moment?
I recently graduated after four years at university in Chengdu. At the moment, I am preparing for IELTS, so most of my study time goes into English speaking, phrase chunks, and repeated practice.
我刚结束在成都的四年大学生活并毕业。目前我在备考雅思，所以大部分学习时间都用在英语口语、语块和反复练习上。
Q
Why did you choose your undergraduate subject?
I chose my undergraduate subject when I was younger, but after studying it, I realised it did not suit me very well. That experience was still useful because it made me clearer about what I do not want to continue doing.
我年纪更小时选择了本科专业，但真正学习后，我发现它并不太适合自己。这段经历仍然有用，因为它让我更清楚以后不想继续做什么。
Q
What do you plan to do after finishing your studies?
I have not fixed a final career plan yet. My current priority is to finish this stage of IELTS preparation and understand my interests through real projects, such as the learning website I have been building.
我还没有确定最终职业计划。当前优先事项是完成这一阶段的雅思备考，并通过真实项目了解自己的兴趣，比如最近制作的学习网站。
Q
Is there anything you would change about your studies?
If I could change something, I would explore my real interests earlier instead of assuming that one university subject had to decide my whole future. People often understand themselves only after trying something in real life.
如果能改变一点，我会更早探索自己真正的兴趣，而不是以为一个大学专业必须决定整个人生。人往往要真正尝试之后，才会更了解自己。
Part 2&3发小
▶
Cue Card
Describe a friend you have known since childhood. You should say: who this person is, how you first met, what you used to do together, and explain why this friendship has lasted so long.
描述一个你从小认识的朋友。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 你们怎么认识的 / 以前一起做什么 / 并解释为什么这段友谊持续了这么久
Answer
To be honest, I do not really have a childhood friend. When I was young, I did not have many close friends. I would play with different groups of kids, but I kept moving between different circles, so I never stayed in one group long enough to form a lasting friendship.

It is not something I feel bad about — it is just how things were. I was always meeting new people and then naturally drifting apart. The pattern continued as I grew up, and I have become comfortable with it.

So if the topic asks about a lifelong friend, my honest answer is I do not have one, and that is okay. I value the friendships I have now, even if they started more recently.
说实话，我没有发小。小时候我没什么好朋友，都是跟不同的人一起玩，然后不断地换圈子，从来没有长期待在同一个圈子并建立持久友谊的经历。

这并不是让我难过的事——只是情况如此。我总是在认识新的人然后自然疏远。这个模式一直延续到我长大，我已经习惯了。

所以如果题目问的是从小到大的朋友，我的真实回答是我没有，这也没关系。我珍惜现在的友谊，即使它们开始得比较晚。
Part 3
Why do some childhood friendships fade away while others last?
I think it comes down to mutual effort and shared values. Some friendships are based purely on proximity, like going to the same school, and once that circumstance changes, there is nothing holding the relationship together. The ones that last usually involve a deeper emotional connection that transcends physical distance.
我认为这归结于双方的努力和共同的价值观。有些友谊纯粹基于距离近，比如上同一所学校，一旦环境变了就没有什么维系关系了。能持久的那种通常涉及更深层的情感连接，超越了物理距离。
Part 3
Do you think technology has made it easier to keep friendships?
In one sense, yes. Apps like WeChat make it effortless to stay in touch across continents. But I would argue that technology can also create an illusion of closeness. Liking someone's post is not the same as sitting across from them over a bowl of hotpot and having a real conversation.
从某种意义上说是的。像微信这样的应用让跨国保持联系变得毫不费力。但我认为科技也可能制造一种亲密的错觉。给某人的帖子点赞和面对面坐着吃火锅聊天的感觉是完全不同的。
Part 2&3为家人骄傲
▶
Cue Card
Describe a family member you are proud of. You should say: who this person is, what they did, how they achieved it, and explain why you feel proud of them.
描述一个你为之骄傲的家庭成员。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 他做了什么 / 他是如何做到的 / 并解释为什么你感到骄傲
Answer
The family member I am most proud of is my grandfather. He ran his own business, but what makes me proud is the way he treated the people who worked for him. He treated his workers like family. Even after the business closed, some of them still came back to visit. That is why I think success is also about how you treat people, not just money or position.
我最骄傲的家人是外公。他经营自己的生意，但我真正为他骄傲的是他对待员工的方式。他把员工当作家人。哪怕生意结束后，一些员工仍会回来探望。我觉得这说明成功也在于你如何对待别人，而不仅是钱或职位。
Part 3
Do you think young people today are more willing to take career risks than in the past?
I think so. The rise of the gig economy and digital platforms has made career changes more visible and less risky than before. Young people see others succeeding outside traditional paths, which normalizes the idea of switching careers. However, there is also real economic pressure that makes some people more cautious.
我觉得是的。零工经济和数字平台的兴起让职业转变变得更加可见、风险也比起以前更低。年轻人看到别人在传统路径之外成功，这让换赛道变得更加正常化。不过也有真实的经济压力让一些人更谨慎。
Part 3
What qualities are needed to succeed after a career change?
I would say resilience above all, because starting over means being a beginner again and facing potential failure. You also need self-discipline to learn independently, and a clear sense of purpose to keep you going when the novelty wears off.
我会说首先是韧性，因为重新开始意味着又变成初学者并面对可能的失败。你还需要自律来独立学习，以及清晰的目标感，在新鲜感消退后仍然支撑你走下去。
Part 2&3给别人建议
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you gave advice to someone. You should say: who you gave advice to, what the situation was, what advice you gave, and explain how the person reacted.
描述一次你给别人建议的经历。你应该说：你给谁建议 / 当时的情况是什么 / 你给了什么建议 / 并解释对方的反应
Answer
A memorable occasion was when I gave advice to a young Chinese literature teacher. I felt that classes should be more engaging, especially subjects like literature — if the teacher just lectures in a monologue, students get tired. I suggested that the teacher could have students read aloud more often, or call on students to answer questions, so that everyone feels more involved. When students have more interaction, the classroom becomes more vivid. The teacher actually listened. In the next class there was much more interaction, and I could feel the atmosphere change. What I learned from this is that sometimes a small adjustment can completely change the atmosphere.
我曾给一位年轻的语文老师提过改进课堂活动的建议。我觉得课程应该更有趣，尤其是语文这种课——如果只是默默地自说自话地讲课，同学们会感到疲惫。

我建议老师可以多让学生朗读，或者多挑同学回答问题，这样大家的参与感更强。当同学们有更多互动时，课堂会更生动。

老师真的听了这个建议。下一节课多了很多互动，我能感觉到气氛变了。我从中学到的是有时候一个小的调整就能完全改变氛围。
Part 3
Do young people usually take advice from older people?
It really depends on how the advice is delivered. Young people tend to resist being lectured, but they are quite open to stories and experiences shared in a conversational way. I think the most effective advice does not feel like advice at all, it feels like someone walking alongside you rather than pointing the way from above.
这取决于建议是如何传达的。年轻人倾向于抗拒被说教，但他们对以对话方式分享的故事和经验相当开放。我觉得最有效的建议让人感觉不像建议，更像是有人和你并肩行走，而不是从高处指路。
Part 3
Is it better to ask for advice or to figure things out on your own?
I think a combination of both is ideal. Seeking advice helps you avoid obvious mistakes and gain view, but working things out independently builds problem-solving skills and confidence. The wisdom lies in knowing which way suits each situation.
我觉得两者结合最理想。寻求建议帮助你避免明显的错误并获得视角，但独立解决问题能培养你的问题解决能力和信心。智慧在于知道哪种方法适合每种情况。
Part 2&3微笑的场合
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you smiled a lot. You should say: when it happened, who you were with, what happened, and explain why you smiled so much.
描述一次你笑了很多的经历。你应该说：什么时候发生的 / 和谁在一起 / 发生了什么 / 并解释为什么你笑那么多
Answer
One time I smiled a lot was during the volunteer programme at a rural school. After I invited four foreign volunteers into town, I asked Mr Liu to help with the group expenses. I carefully explained my calculation: I had removed what I ate and the part I wanted to treat everyone to, so I only asked him to cover the rest.

He laughed and said that I had probably been the one who wanted the food and had simply persuaded everyone else to join me. The way he described my thinking was so accurate that I could not help laughing too. He then helped pay most of the group cost.

Later, I told the four volunteers that Mr Liu had paid for us. They all came over to shake his hand and thank him. That small cross-cultural scene made everyone smile, because the whole misunderstanding ended in a warm and funny way.
有一次我笑了很久，是在乡村学校志愿活动期间。我邀请四位外国志愿者一起去街上后，请刘老师帮忙处理集体费用。我很认真地解释自己的算法：已经扣掉自己吃的部分，也扣掉了本来想请大家吃的部分，只请他承担剩下的费用。

他笑着说，其实大概就是我自己想吃，然后撺掇大家一起去。他把我的思路说得太准确，我也忍不住笑了。后来他帮忙承担了大部分集体费用。

我又告诉四位志愿者，是刘老师为大家付了钱。他们都主动过来和他握手道谢。这个小小的跨文化场面让大家都笑了，因为整件小误会以一种温暖又好玩的方式结束了。
Part 3
Do you think people smile more or less as they grow older?
That is an interesting question. I think children smile more frequently and spontaneously, while adults might smile less often but more meaningfully. Adults also learn to smile for social reasons, which is different from the pure, unfiltered joy of a child's smile.
这是个有趣的问题。我觉得孩子笑得更频繁、更自发，而成年人可能笑得没那么频繁但更有意义。成年人也学会了出于社交原因微笑，这和孩子纯粹的、不加掩饰的笑容是不同的。
Part 3
What role does humor play in cross-cultural communication?
It's both a bridge and a minefield. Shared laughter creates instant connection, but humor is deeply cultural—what's funny in one context might be offensive in another. The safest form is self-deprecating humor—it shows humility and rarely alienates anyone.
它既是桥梁也是雷区。共同的笑声创造即时连接，但幽默是深深文化性的——在一个语境中有趣的东西在另一个中可能冒犯。最安全的形式是自嘲幽默——它展示谦逊，很少疏远任何人。
Part 2&3鼓励别人做不愿做的事
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you encouraged someone to do something they did not want to do. You should say: who the person was, what they did not want to do, how you encouraged them, and explain the result.
描述一次你鼓励别人做他们不想做的事的经历。你应该说：那个人是谁 / 他不想做什么 / 你怎么鼓励的 / 并解释结果
Answer
During a volunteer programme at a rural school, four foreign volunteers arrived, and I really wanted us to go into town together. They had not planned an outing and were a little unsure, so I encouraged them to come and experience the local area.

I explained that we could try a few simple local snacks and that I could help with communication and introduce some local culture. I kept the plan easy, so it did not feel like a formal trip. In the end, all four agreed to come.

We ate fried shrimp and other snacks, walked around, and enjoyed the time together. The outing later became a small cross-cultural activity. It worked because I did not pressure them; I made the unfamiliar plan feel simple and enjoyable.
在一次乡村学校志愿活动中，学校来了四位外国志愿者，我很想和他们一起去街上。他们原本没有这个计划，也有一点犹豫，所以我鼓励他们一起出去体验当地环境。

我告诉他们，我们可以尝一些简单的当地小吃，我也可以帮忙沟通、介绍当地文化。我把计划说得很轻松，所以它不像一次正式旅行。最后四个人都同意一起去。

我们吃了炸虾等小吃，也一起走了走，大家都很开心。这次外出后来成了一个小型跨文化活动。它之所以成功，是因为我没有强迫他们，而是让一个陌生的计划显得简单又好玩。
Part 3
Why is it sometimes difficult to encourage people?
Because encouragement can easily cross the line into pressure if the person is not ready. People who are afraid or anxious often interpret well-meaning words as demands, so the challenge is finding the right balance between being supportive and respectful of their emotional state.
因为如果对方还没准备好，鼓励很容易越界变成压力。害怕或焦虑的人往往把善意的话语解读为要求，所以挑战在于在支持和尊重他们的情绪状态之间找到合适的平衡。
Part 3
Should parents encourage children to try things they are afraid of?
Yes, but within reason. Children need gentle nudges to expand their comfort zones, but pushing too hard can backfire and create lasting fear. The key is to break the challenge into small, manageable steps so the child can build confidence slowly.
是的，但要适度。孩子需要温和的推动来扩大舒适区，但推得太狠可能适得其反，造成持久的恐惧。关键是将挑战分解成小的、可控的步骤，让孩子逐步建立信心。
Part 2&3乐于助人的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person who is always helpful to others. You should say: who this person is, how they help others, who they help, and explain why you think they are helpful.
描述一个总是乐于助人的人。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 他怎么帮助别人 / 帮助了谁 / 并解释为什么你觉得他乐于助人
Answer
The person I would mention is Mr Liu, whom I knew during a volunteer programme at a rural school. One day, I invited four foreign volunteers to go into town with me. I showed them some local culture and we bought food together, but I then had to work out which expenses should be covered by the school.

When I explained the situation to Mr Liu, he listened to my rather complicated calculation and helped cover most of the group expenses. Later, I told the four volunteers that he had paid for us, and they all came over to shake his hand and thank him.

I remember this because his help was practical and immediate. He did not make the situation feel embarrassing; he simply made the activity easier for everyone.
我想说的是刘老师，我在乡村学校参加志愿活动时认识了他。有一天，我邀请四位外国志愿者和我一起去街上。我带他们了解当地文化，也一起买了食物，但后来需要弄清楚哪些费用应该由学校承担。

我向刘老师解释情况后，他听完我有些复杂的计算，帮忙承担了大部分集体费用。后来我告诉四位志愿者是他为大家付了钱，他们都主动过来和他握手道谢。

我记得这件事，是因为他的帮助很实际也很及时。他没有让这件事变得尴尬，而是直接让整个活动对所有人都更顺利。
Part 3
Do you think people are less willing to help others than in the past?
It is hard to say. In big cities, the fast pace of life can make people seem more self-absorbed. But I also see a lot of online communities where strangers help each other freely, sharing knowledge and resources. So perhaps the form of helping has changed rather than disappeared.
这很难说。在大城市，快节奏的生活让人觉得更自我。但我也看到很多在线社区里陌生人免费互相帮助，分享知识和资源。所以也许帮助的形式变了，而不是消失了。
Part 3
Should helping others be taught as a skill or is it innate?
It's both. Some people have natural empathy, but helpfulness can absolutely be developed. What's teachable is recognizing when help is actually needed versus when it might be intrusive. The most helpful people I know combine real care with practical judgment—they don't just want to help; they know how to help effectively.
两者都是。有些人天生有同理心，但乐于助人绝对可以培养。可教的是识别什么时候真正需要帮助，什么时候可能是侵扰。我认识的最乐于助人的人将真诚关怀与实用判断结合——他们不只是想帮忙；他们知道如何有效帮忙。
Part 2&3在团队中工作
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you worked in a team. You should say: what the team project was, what your role was, how the team worked together, and explain whether the experience was positive or negative.
描述一次你在团队中工作的经历。你应该说：团队项目是什么 / 你的角色是什么 / 团队如何合作 / 并解释这次经历是积极的还是消极的
Answer
A team experience I remember clearly was the cross-cultural outing with four foreign volunteers at a rural school. I suggested going into town, helped everyone choose food, and introduced some local culture. The volunteers joined in, while Mr Liu later helped with the group expenses.

We did not have formal roles, but everyone contributed in a practical way. What made the experience positive was that people from different backgrounds felt included. It showed me that a team does not always need a complicated structure; it needs clear communication and people willing to help.
我记得很清楚的一次团队经历，是在乡村学校和四位外国志愿者一起进行的跨文化外出。我提议到街上走走，帮大家选择食物，也介绍了一些当地文化。志愿者们都参与进来，刘老师后来还帮忙处理了集体费用。

我们没有正式分工，但每个人都以实际方式作出了贡献。这次经历积极的地方，是不同背景的人都感到自己参与其中。它让我看到，团队不一定需要复杂结构，更需要清楚的沟通和愿意帮忙的人。
Part 3
What are the advantages and disadvantages of working in a team?
The main advantage is synergy, the combined effort of a team can achieve what no individual could alone. The downside is that coordination costs time, and personality conflicts can derail the entire project if not managed well. Good leadership is usually the deciding factor.
主要优势是协同效应，团队的整体努力可以实现个人无法单独完成的成果。缺点是协调需要花费时间，如果管理不好，性格冲突可能让整个项目脱轨。好的领导力通常是决定性因素。
Part 3
What makes a good team leader?
A good team leader needs to listen actively, make decisions decisively but fairly, and keep the team's morale high even under pressure. I also think the best leaders are those who give credit rather than taking it for themselves, because that builds trust over time.
一个好的团队领导需要积极倾听，果断而公平地做决定，即使在压力下也要保持团队士气。我也认为最好的领导者是那些把功劳归于团队而不是揽在自己身上的人，因为这样才能逐渐建立信任。
Part 2&3擅长做计划的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person you know who is good at making plans. You should say: who this person is, how they plan things, what kinds of things they plan, and explain why you think they are good at planning.
描述一个你认识的擅长做计划的人。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 他怎么做计划 / 通常计划什么 / 并解释为什么你觉得他擅长做计划
Answer
A person I know who plans well is my cousin who taught himself law. After leaving his bank job, he had to study independently while preparing for a difficult examination. He broke the goal into stages, kept studying after the first unsuccessful attempt, and passed on his second try.

I think he is good at planning because he turns a large goal into actions he can repeat. His plan was not perfect from the beginning, but he adjusted it instead of giving up.
我认识的一个擅长计划的人，是自学法律的表哥。离开银行工作后，他要一边独立学习，一边准备一场很难的考试。他把目标分成不同阶段，第一次没有成功后继续学习，第二次终于通过。

我觉得他擅长计划，是因为他会把大目标变成可以反复执行的行动。他的计划并非一开始就完美，但他会调整，而不是放弃。
Part 3
Do you think it is important to make plans?
Yes, but I also think over-planning can be a problem. Plans give you direction and reduce anxiety, but if you cling to them too tightly, you miss out on unexpected opportunities. The best way is to plan enough to feel prepared but leave room for spontaneity.
是的，但我也认为过度计划会有问题。计划给你方向感并减少焦虑，但如果你太执着于计划，就会错过意外的机会。最好的方法是计划到觉得准备充分，但留出自发的空间。
Part 3
Do you think people who plan everything are less spontaneous?
Sometimes, yes. People who over-rely on plans can struggle when things don't go as expected — they feel anxious and try to force the plan rather than adapt. But my friend is different because he plans as a framework, not a script. He leaves pockets of flexibility where spontaneity can happen naturally. I think the key is planning the structure but leaving the details open.
有时候是的。过度依赖计划的人在事情不如预期时会感到焦虑——他们试图强行执行计划而不是适应变化。但我的朋友不同，因为他的计划是框架而非剧本。他留出了灵活的口袋，让即兴发挥可以自然发生。我觉得关键是规划结构但把细节留白。
Part 2&3发挥想象力
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you used your imagination. You should say: when it was, what you imagined, what you did with the idea, and explain how it made you feel.
描述一次你运用想象力的经历。你应该说：什么时候 / 你想象了什么 / 你用这个想法做了什么 / 并解释你的感受
Answer
When I was a child, I imagined building a platform that could help people find partners and turn ideas into reality. The main idea was not a game or one fixed activity. I wanted people with different abilities to meet, cooperate and receive support from a wider network.

At that age, I could not build it, so it stayed in my imagination. However, the central idea has remained with me. Now I think of it as both a long-term dream and my idea of perfect work. I can begin with small real projects, observe what helps people cooperate, and gradually move the idea closer to reality.

It makes me feel hopeful because an imagined possibility can slowly become a practical direction.
小时候，我想象搭建一个帮助人们找到伙伴、把想法真正变成现实的平台。它的重点不是游戏，也不是某一种固定活动，而是让拥有不同能力的人相遇、合作，并获得更大网络的支持。

那时我当然没有能力把它做出来，所以它一直停留在想象中。但核心想法一直没有消失。现在我把它同时看作长期梦想和心目中的完美工作。我可以从小型真实项目开始，观察什么能帮助人们合作，再逐渐让这个想法靠近现实。

它让我感到有希望，因为想象中的可能性可以慢慢变成实际方向。
Part 3
Do you think schools should encourage imagination more?
Absolutely. In many education systems, including China's, there is a heavy emphasis on standardized testing and correct answers, which can squeeze out imaginative thinking. Schools should create space for open-ended projects where there is no single right answer, because that is closer to how real-world problems actually work.
绝对应该。在包括中国在内的许多教育体系中，标准化考试和正确答案被过分强调，这可能挤压想象力的空间。学校应该为开放式项目创造空间，因为那更接近真实世界问题的运作方式。
Part 3
Can imagination be taught, or is it innate?
I believe everyone is born with imaginative capacity, but it can be nurtured or suppressed depending on the environment. It is less about teaching imagination from scratch and more about removing the barriers that block it, things like fear of being wrong or too much structure.
我相信每个人天生都有想象的能力，但环境可以培养它也可以压制它。与其说是从零教起，不如说是移除阻碍想象力的障碍，比如害怕犯错或过度结构化。
Part 2&3重要决定
▶
Cue Card
Describe an important decision you made. You should say: what the decision was, when you made it, why you made it, and explain how it affected your life.
描述一个你做出的重要决定。你应该说：决定是什么 / 什么时候做的 / 为什么做这个决定 / 并解释它如何影响了你的生活
Answer
An important recent decision was to use the period after graduation to focus on IELTS. I had just finished four years of university and moved to Hangzhou, so I needed to decide what deserved my attention first.

Instead of treating preparation as simple word memorisation, I began organising my real stories, building phrase chunks, and making my own IELTS website with AI. The website let me arrange topics in a way that matched how I remember information.

This decision affected my daily life because IELTS became my main focus. It also helped me discover a learning method that fits the way I think, which may remain useful after the test.
最近一个重要决定，是把毕业后的这段时间集中用来备考雅思。我刚结束四年大学生活并来到杭州，需要决定眼下最值得投入精力的事情。

我没有把备考只当作背单词，而是开始整理真实故事、建立语块，并在 AI 帮助下制作自己的雅思网站。网站让我能按照更符合自己记忆方式的结构排列主题。

这个决定改变了日常生活，因为雅思成了当前主要关注点；它也让我发现了一种适合自己思考方式的学习方法，考试结束后可能仍然有用。
Part 3
What factors should people consider when making important decisions?
I think people should consider both practical and emotional factors. Practically, you need to assess finances, timeline, and feasibility. Emotionally, you need to ask whether the decision aligns with your core values and whether you can live with the regret of not trying.
我认为人们应该同时考虑实际和情感因素。实际层面，你需要评估财务、时间线和可行性。情感层面，你需要问这个决定是否符合你的核心价值观，以及你是否能承受不尝试的遗憾。
Part 3
Do you think it is harder to make decisions now than in the past?
In some ways yes, because we have too many options. In the past, career paths were more linear — you studied one thing and did it for life. Now, the possibilities are endless, which is liberating but also paralyzing. Social media makes it worse by showing us all the paths we didn't take. I think feeling tired from making too many choices is a real modern phenomenon.
在某种程度上是的，因为我们有太多选择。过去职业路径更加线性——你学一样东西就做一辈子。现在可能性是无限的，这既解放也令人瘫痪。社交媒体让情况更糟，因为它向我们展示了所有没有选择的路。我认为决策疲劳是真实的现代现象。
Part 3
Do you think young people today make decisions more independently?
In some ways yes, because access to information allows young people to research options thoroughly before consulting anyone. But I also think the abundance of choices can actually make decision-making harder, leading to analysis paralysis where people delay choosing altogether.
在某些方面是的，因为获取信息的便利让年轻人在咨询任何人之前就能充分研究选项。但我也认为选择的丰富反而可能让决策变得更难，导致分析瘫痪，人们干脆拖延不做选择。
Part 2&3近期改变的计划
▶
Cue Card
Describe a plan you changed recently. You should say: what the original plan was, why you changed it, what the new plan is, and explain how you feel about the change.
描述一个你最近改变了的计划。你应该说：原来的计划是什么 / 为什么改变 / 新计划是什么 / 并解释你对改变的感受
Answer
Recently, I changed the way I prepare for IELTS speaking. At first, I was trying to remember separate answers and isolated words for many topics. The amount of material kept growing, and I realised that too many separate stories created unnecessary memory pressure.

My new plan is to use fewer real stories for several related topics and to extract longer reusable phrase chunks from each answer. I treat them like Lego pieces, so I can combine familiar parts naturally instead of rebuilding every sentence from zero.

I feel much better about this change because the material is now easier to review and more closely connected to my real life. It has also taught me that changing a plan can be a way of making it more realistic, not a sign of failure.
最近，我改变了准备雅思口语的方法。起初，我试图为很多话题分别记答案和零散词汇。材料越来越多，我发现太多彼此分离的故事会制造不必要的记忆压力。

现在的新计划，是用更少的真实故事覆盖几个相关话题，并从答案中提取更长、可重复使用的语块。我把它们当作乐高积木，这样就能自然组合熟悉的部分，而不用每次从零重建整句话。

我很喜欢这个变化，因为现在的材料更容易复习，也和真实生活联系得更紧密。它也让我明白，改变计划可以是让计划变得更现实，而不是失败的表现。
Part 3
Why do people sometimes need to change their plans?
Plans are based on assumptions about the future, and when reality does not match those assumptions, adjustment becomes necessary. Sometimes new information emerges, sometimes circumstances beyond our control intervene, and sometimes we simply underestimate how long something will take.
计划是基于对未来的假设，当现实与这些假设不符时，调整就变得必要。有时新信息出现，有时超出我们控制的情况发生，有时我们只是低估了某件事需要的时间。
Part 3
How can people better handle unexpected changes to their plans?
By building flexibility into their mindset from the start. If you view plans as intentions rather than contracts, changes feel less like failures. Also, having a Plan B ready reduces panic. The most adaptable people I know expect disruption and see it as an opportunity rather than a catastrophe.
通过从一开始就在心态中建立灵活性。如果你将计划视为意图而非合同，变化就不太像失败。另外，准备好B计划减少恐慌。我认识的最适应力强的人预料到干扰，并将其视为机会而非灾难。
Part 2&3想从事医疗行业的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person you know who wants to work in the medical field. You should say: who this person is, what they want to do, why they chose this field, and explain how you feel about their choice.
描述一个你认识的想在医疗领域工作的人。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 他想做什么 / 为什么选择这个领域 / 并解释你对他选择的感受
Answer
I'd like to talk about a classmate who studied medicine. She chose this path very seriously, but finding a job in medicine is actually quite difficult — the competition is incredibly fierce.

As for whether she wants to continue in this field or whether she can — it depends. The reality is that medical careers require years of additional training and specialization, and the job market is oversaturated in many areas.

What I admire about her is that she went into medicine with genuine dedication, not just for the prestige. She knew it would be hard, but the intensity of the competition was still a surprise. Whether she ends up practicing or pivots to a related field, I respect her commitment to healthcare.
我想说的是一个学医的同学。她很认真地选择了这条路，但学医找工作其实并不容易，竞争太激烈了。

至于她最终能不能从事这行——it depends。就业市场很严峻，很多毕业生竞争有限的岗位。所以即使她努力学习拿到了学位，结果也不是确定的。

我觉得她的情况很有意思的一点是选择一条专业道路并不总能直接通向对应的职业。有时候你为之努力的领域比预想的更复杂，必须保持灵活。
Part 3
Why do some people choose difficult careers like medicine?
I think it comes down to a combination of calling and capability. Some people feel a real vocation to help others, and medicine offers the most direct way to do that. Others are drawn by the intellectual challenge, the human body is endlessly complex, and some personalities thrive on that kind of problem-solving.
我认为这归结于使命感和能力的结合。有些人真正感受到帮助他人的使命感，而医学提供了最直接的途径。另一些人被智力挑战所吸引，人体无比复杂，某些性格的人正是在那种问题解决中如鱼得水。
Part 3
Do you think medical professionals are valued enough in society?
This is a complex issue. During health crises, medical professionals are rightly celebrated as heroes, but in ordinary times their working conditions and compensation do not always reflect their importance. There is often a gap between societal appreciation and practical support.
这是个复杂的问题。在健康危机期间，医疗专业人员理所当然地被誉为英雄，但在平时他们的工作条件和薪酬并不总能反映他们的重要性。社会赞誉和实际支持之间常常存在差距。
Part 2&3早起经历
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when you got up early. You should say: when it was, why you got up early, what you did, and explain how you felt about it.
描述一次你早起的日子。你应该说：什么时候 / 为什么早起 / 你做了什么 / 并解释你的感受
Answer
One day I woke up early naturally, without setting an alarm. I did not have a special event to attend; my body simply felt rested. I ate whatever food was available and started working on my IELTS materials while the surroundings were still quiet.

I liked the fresh feeling of that morning, but I would not force myself to repeat it every day. I prefer to sleep when tiredness comes naturally. For me, waking up early feels good when it happens after enough rest, not when it is created by pressure.
有一天我没有定闹钟，却自然早醒了。那天没有必须参加的特殊活动，只是身体已经休息够了。我随意吃了些现有的食物，趁周围还很安静时开始整理雅思材料。

我很喜欢那个早晨清新的感觉，但不会强迫自己每天复制。我更愿意在困意自然出现时睡觉。对我来说，早起只有在充分休息后自然发生时才舒服，而不是靠压力制造出来。
Part 3
Do you think it is better to get up early or stay up late?
I think it depends on your biological rhythm. Some people are naturally more productive in the morning, while others do their best thinking at night. the key is to be consistent, forcing yourself into a schedule that fights your natural clock usually backfires.
我觉得取决于你的生物节律。有些人天生早上效率更高，另一些人晚上思维最活跃。关键是规律，强迫自己进入一个和自然生物钟对抗的日程通常会适得其反。
Part 3
Why do some people find it hard to get up early?
Modern lifestyles are a big factor. Late-night screen time disrupts sleep quality, and irregular schedules confuse the body's internal clock. Also, if there is no compelling reason to get up early, the motivation simply is not there.
现代生活方式是一个大因素。睡前看屏幕会影响睡眠质量，不规律的作息会打乱身体的生物钟。另外，如果没有一个足够 interesting 的早起理由，动力根本就不存在。
Part 2&3机智解决问题的人
▶
Cue Card
Describe a person who solved a problem in a clever way. You should say: who the person was, what the problem was, how they solved it, and explain why you think it was clever.
描述一个用聪明方式解决问题的人。你应该说：这个人是谁 / 问题是什么 / 他怎么解决的 / 并解释为什么你觉得很聪明
Answer
I would talk about Mr Liu during our cross-cultural outing. I had invited four foreign volunteers to go into town, but afterwards the small group bill became awkward. I showed him my calculation and explained which part was mine, which part was my treat, and which part belonged to the group.

He opened the calculator, asked how I had worked it out, laughed at my way of thinking, and then gave me fifty yuan. The clever part was that he solved the practical problem while keeping the mood light. No one felt blamed or embarrassed, and the activity ended happily.
我想讲跨文化外出活动中的刘老师。我邀请四位外国志愿者一起去街上，但结束后那笔不大的集体费用有点尴尬。我把计算拿给他，解释哪部分是我的、哪部分是我请客、哪部分属于集体。

他打开计算器，问我怎么算的，听完笑了笑，然后给了我五十元。聪明的地方在于，他解决了实际问题，同时让气氛保持轻松。没有人被责怪或感到尴尬，活动也愉快地结束了。
Part 3
What kinds of problems require creative solutions?
Problems that involve both practical details and people's feelings often need creative solutions. A good answer cannot only be mathematically correct; it should also keep communication comfortable for everyone involved.
同时涉及实际细节和他人感受的问题，往往需要创造性的解决方式。好的答案不能只在计算上正确，也应该让所有相关人的沟通保持舒服。
Part 3
Can creative problem-solving be taught?
I believe it can be nurtured through exposure to diverse situations and by encouraging people to reframe problems rather than just solving them. Case studies, role plays, and real-world projects are all effective ways to develop this kind of flexible thinking.
我相信它可以通过接触多样化情境以及鼓励人们重新定义问题而非仅仅是解决问题来培养。案例研究、角色扮演和真实项目都是培养这种灵活思维的有效方式。
Part 2&3别人帮助解决问题
▶
Cue Card
Describe a time when someone helped you solve a problem. You should say: who helped you, what the problem was, how they helped you, and explain how you felt about it.
描述一次别人帮你解决问题的经历。你应该说：谁帮了你 / 问题是什么 / 他怎么帮的 / 并解释你的感受
Answer
During a volunteer programme at a rural school, I once invited four foreign volunteers to go into town. We bought food and I introduced some local culture, but afterwards I was unsure how to divide the personal and group expenses.

I took my calculation to Mr Liu and explained that I had already removed my own food and part of what I wanted to treat the group to. He listened, found the calculation amusing, and then helped me settle the group expenses. That immediately removed the awkward part of the activity.

I felt relieved and grateful. The moment became even more memorable when the four volunteers came over to shake his hand and thank him. It showed me that practical help can solve a problem without making it feel heavy.
在一次乡村学校志愿活动中，我邀请四位外国志愿者一起去街上。我们买了食物，我也介绍了一些当地文化，但结束后我不太确定个人费用和集体费用应该怎么分。

我把计算结果拿给刘老师，解释说自己已经扣除了个人吃的东西，也扣掉了本来想请大家吃的部分。他听完觉得我的算法有点好笑，然后帮我结清了集体费用。活动里尴尬的那一部分立刻就解决了。

我感到轻松也很感谢他。后来四位志愿者主动过来和他握手致谢，让这一幕更有记忆点。它让我发现，实际的帮助可以解决问题，又不会让事情显得很沉重。
Part 3
Do you think it is better to solve problems alone or ask for help?
I think it depends on the nature of the problem. For problems that require personal reflection or creative insight, working alone can be more productive. But when you are stuck in a blind spot, as I was with my writing, an outside view is invaluable and can save you very large amounts of time.
我觉得取决于问题的性质。对于需要个人反思或创造性洞察的问题，独自工作可能更有效。但当你陷入盲点时，就像我写作那样，外部视角是无价的，可以为你节省大量时间。
Part 3
What skills are needed to help others solve problems?
First, active listening, because you need to understand the problem before offering a solution. Second, practical judgment, so the help actually fits the situation. Empathy also matters, because the way help is offered can make people feel supported rather than embarrassed.
首先是积极倾听，因为给出解决方案前要先理解问题。其次是实际判断力，确保帮助真的适合当时的情况。同理心也很重要，因为提供帮助的方式会决定对方感到被支持，还是感到尴尬。
Part 2&3想颁布的新法律
▶
Cue Card
Describe a new law you would like to see introduced. You should say: what the law would be, who it would affect, how it would work, and explain why you think it is necessary.
描述一项你想看到实施的新法律。你应该说：法律会是什么 / 会影响谁 / 如何运作 / 并解释为什么你觉得有必要
Answer
If I could introduce a new law, it would give stronger protection to natural sites such as caves, forests and scenic areas. Visitors who leave rubbish or damage natural formations would receive a clear fine, while the sites would also need enough bins, signs and staff.

I thought about this after visiting Baima Fairy Cave. The natural rock formations had taken a very long time to develop, but I still saw plastic bottles and food wrappers among them. A small careless action can damage a place that cannot simply be replaced.

The law should affect both visitors and site managers. Visitors need clear responsibility, but managers also need to make good behaviour easy. Its purpose would be to protect places that take nature far longer to create than people take to damage.
如果我能制定一部新法律，它会对洞穴、森林和景区等自然地点提供更严格的保护。游客乱扔垃圾或破坏自然结构时，应受到明确罚款；景区也必须提供足够的垃圾桶、提示牌和管理人员。

我是在去过白马仙洞后想到这件事的。天然岩石经过很长时间才形成，但我仍然在其中看到塑料瓶和食品包装。一个很小的粗心行为，就可能破坏无法简单替换的地方。

这部法律应同时约束游客和景区管理者。游客需要承担明确责任，管理者也要让文明行为更容易做到。它的目的，是保护那些大自然创造起来远比人类破坏起来更慢的地方。
Part 3
Do you think laws can keep up with technological change?
This is one of the fundamental challenges of modern governance. Technology evolves at a pace that outstrips the process of making laws, which is deliberately slow and deliberative. I think the solution is not faster laws but more principles-based regulation that can adapt to new technologies without needing to be rewritten constantly.
这是现代治理面临的基本挑战之一。技术发展的速度超越了立法过程，而后者刻意是缓慢和审慎的。我认为解决方案不是更快的法律，而是更多基于原则的监管，能够适应新技术而不需要不断重写。
Part 3
Should young people have a say in making laws that affect them?
Absolutely. Laws affecting digital natives should not be written exclusively by people who did not grow up with the internet. Young people bring a lived understanding of how technology actually works in daily life, which is something that theory alone cannot replace.
当然。影响数字原住民的法律不应该完全由没有在互联网时代长大的人来制定。年轻人带来了对技术如何在日常生活中实际运作的切身理解，这是纯理论知识无法替代的。
Part 2&3想从事的短期海外工作
▶
Cue Card
Describe a short-term job abroad you would like to do. You should say: what the job would be, where you would do it, how long it would last, and explain why you would like to do it.
描述一份你想做的海外短期工作。你应该说：工作是什么 / 在哪里做 / 持续多久 / 并解释为什么你想做
Answer
I have only just graduated from university, so I have never worked abroad and I do not have a detailed plan yet. If I had the chance, I would try a short project-assistant role in an English-speaking country for one or two months. I would prefer a small international team where the work involved real communication and cooperation.

The title of the job is not the main point for me. I would treat it as a short test of a different working environment. It would give me a reason to use English every day, learn how people from different backgrounds work together, and see whether living abroad suits me. Because it would be short, I could learn from the experience without pretending that I already knew my long-term career direction.
我才刚大学毕业，所以没有在海外工作过，也还没有详细计划。如果有机会，我愿意在一个英语国家尝试一两个月的短期项目助理工作。我更希望加入一个小型国际团队，工作内容需要真实沟通和合作。

对我来说，职位名称并不是重点。我会把它当作对不同工作环境的一次短期体验。它能让我每天不得不用英语，了解不同背景的人如何合作，也看看自己是否适合海外生活。因为时间不长，我可以从中学习，又不用假装自己已经确定了长期职业方向。
Part 3
What are the benefits of working abroad?
Working abroad forces you to adapt to a different culture and work environment, which builds strength after setbacks and the ability to work with people from other cultures. It also broadens your professional network across borders, which is increasingly valuable in a globalized economy. The main challenge, of course, is being away from your support system.
在国外工作迫使你适应不同的文化和工作环境，这培养了韧性和跨文化能力。它还让你跨越国界拓展职业人脉，这在全球化经济中越来越有价值。当然主要挑战是远离你的支持系统。
Part 3
Do you think short-term international experiences are valuable for young people?
Yes, I think they are incredibly valuable because they offer a short period of cultural immersion without the long-term commitment of relocation. Short-term experiences are often more accessible and can serve as a stepping stone that helps young people decide whether they want to pursue longer international opportunities.
是的，我认为它们非常有价值，因为它们提供了一种浓缩的文化沉浸体验，而不需要长期迁移的承诺。短期经历通常更容易获得，可以作为一块跳板，帮助年轻人决定是否要追求更长期的国际机会。
Part 2&3喜欢画画的孩子
▶
Cue Card
Describe a child you know who likes drawing or painting. You should say: who the child is, what they like to draw, how they developed this interest, and explain why you think they enjoy it.
描述一个你认识的喜欢画画的孩子。你应该说：这个孩子是谁 / 喜欢画什么 / 怎么发展出这个兴趣的 / 并解释为什么你觉得他喜欢画画
Answer
I do not know a real child who loves drawing, so the only one I can clearly think of is a girl in the animated series Littlest Pet Shop, which I watched as a child. She seemed to enjoy turning ideas into pictures and designs, and drawing felt like a natural part of her daily life.

I remember her because she briefly made me want to draw as well. I liked the programme so much that I asked my mother to buy me a drawing board and some canvases. However, after they arrived, I hardly drew anything at all. I knew I was not good at it, and I was strangely unwilling to make a bad mark and ruin a clean canvas.

That contrast is why the character stayed in my memory. For her, drawing looked free and enjoyable; for me, the fear of spoiling the canvas stopped me before I started.
我现实中没有认识的、特别喜欢画画的孩子，所以唯一能清楚想到的是动画片《至Q宠物屋》里的一个女孩。我小时候看过这部动画，她很喜欢把想法变成图画和设计，画画就像她日常生活里很自然的一部分。

我记得她，是因为她一度让我也想学画画。我太喜欢那部动画了，于是让妈妈给我买画板和画布。但东西买回来后，我几乎什么也没画。我知道自己不擅长，而且又很舍不得在干净的画布上留下不好看的痕迹。

这种反差反而让我一直记得那个角色。对她来说，画画自由又好玩；对我来说，害怕破坏画布让我还没开始就停下了。
Part 3
Do you think art education is important for children's development?
I consider it essential, though it is often undervalued in systems that put first test scores. Art education develops capacities that other subjects cannot easily replicate — the ability to understand space and shapes, emotional expression, and the ability to tolerate ambiguity and explore multiple solutions to a single problem. When children draw or paint, they are not just making pictures; they are learning to observe the world closely and translate their perceptions into something communicable, which is a basic cognitive and life skill.
我认为它至关重要，尽管在以考试分数为优先的体系中它常被低估。艺术教育培养的是其他学科难以替代的能力——空间推理、情感表达，以及对模糊性的容忍和探索单一问题多种解决方案的能力。当孩子画画时，他们不仅仅是在制作图像；他们是在学习仔细观察世界，并将自己的感知转化为可传达的东西，这是一种基本的认知能力和生活技能。
Part 3
Should children be encouraged to pursue art as a career?
I think they should be encouraged to explore art without pressure, but whether it becomes a career should be their own decision. The reality is that art careers are financially uncertain, and parents' concerns are valid. However, discouraging children entirely from art can stifle a skill that's valuable in many fields — design, communication, problem-solving. The best way is to let art enrich their development while helping them understand the real situation.
我认为应该鼓励他们无压力地探索艺术，但是否以此为职业应该是他们自己的决定。现实是艺术职业在经济上不确定，家长的担忧是合理的。但完全阻止孩子接触艺术可能会压制一项在许多领域都有价值的技能——设计、沟通、解决问题。最好的方法是让艺术丰富他们的发展，同时帮助他们了解现实情况。
Part 2&3完美工作
▶
Cue Card
Describe what you think would be the perfect job for you. You should say: what the job would be, what skills it requires, why you think it would be perfect, and explain how you plan to achieve it.
描述你心目中完美的工作。你应该说：工作是什么 / 需要什么技能 / 为什么觉得它完美 / 并解释你计划如何实现
Answer
My perfect job is really the working form of my dream. I want to build a platform that helps people turn their ideas into reality. On it, people could find suitable partners, work together, and receive support from a wider network. The aim would be simple: to help more good ideas become real projects and, in the process, create better lives.

This work would require me to understand people, organize ideas clearly, connect the right partners, and keep learning while solving real problems. It would not be a fixed office role with the same task every day. I would be building the platform, supporting collaboration, and improving it through actual use.

It feels perfect to me because I would be working for a dream I genuinely believe in. I can start with small projects, learn what truly helps people cooperate, and gradually build a wider network around them.
我心目中的完美工作，其实就是让我的梦想成为每天所做的事。我想搭建一个帮助人们把想法真正变成现实的平台。人们可以在上面找到合适的伙伴、共同协作，并获得更大范围网络的支持。目标很简单：让更多好的想法成为真实项目，并在这个过程中创造更美好的生活。

这份工作需要我理解人、清楚地整理想法、连接合适的伙伴，并且在解决真实问题的过程中不断学习。它不会是一份每天重复同一任务的固定办公室工作。我会建设平台、支持协作，再根据真实使用不断改进它。

它之所以完美，是因为我每天都在为自己真正相信的梦想工作。我可以先从小项目开始，了解什么真的能帮助人们合作，再逐渐围绕它们建立更大的网络。
Part 3
What qualities do you think are most important for a fulfilling career?
For me, the key qualities are a real sense of purpose, room to grow, and enough freedom to make decisions. A fulfilling career should let people see why their work matters. It should also keep them learning instead of making every day feel exactly the same.
对我来说，关键是真正的目标感、成长空间，以及足够的自主决定权。一份令人满足的工作应该让人看到自己的工作为什么有意义，也应该让人持续学习，而不是每天都完全一样。
Part 3
Do you think job satisfaction is more important than salary?
It depends on a person's situation. If basic needs are not covered, salary naturally comes first. After that, job satisfaction matters more, because people spend a large part of their lives working. Ideally, a job should provide both a stable life and a sense of meaning.
这取决于一个人的现实情况。如果基本生活还没有保障，薪水自然更重要。在此之后，工作满意度会更重要，因为人一生中有很大一部分时间都在工作。理想情况下，一份工作应该既提供稳定生活，也带来意义感。

6.5分技巧

📝阅读建议：5分钟浏览，理解差异即可。考前可快速复习对照表。

从 6 分到 6.5 分的词汇升级对照、关键提升动作、详细对比案例与提升路径。

6 分和 7 分的核心差异不在"词汇难度"，而在精确度、句型多样性和因果链完整度。 以下对比基于 331 组 6/7 分范文的文本统计。
五大提升维度
维度6分特征7分特征提升策略
词汇精确度 good / bad / interesting / very / really impressive / negative / fascinating / truly / really 用更精确的同义词替换泛用词，但不必追求"大词"
句型多样性 I like... because... and... so... which 从句 / Although 让步 / Not only...but also / 分词结构 每个回答至少使用 2 种不同句型结构
因果链完整度 给出原因但不展开后果 原因→条件→结果→影响 完整链条 在 because 后加 If...then 或 which means... 补充后果
连接词分层 also / and / but / so On top of that / While / That said / Since 按逻辑层选词：立场→因果→举例→让步→递进
细节具体化 "I visit galleries" "I often visit local galleries—it's become my go-to activity for unwinding" 加入频率、地点、感受、比喻等细节

词汇升级对照表（8组核心对照）

6分表达6.5分表达
I like artI'm really into art
It was funIt was incredibly fulfilling
I was surprisedWhat surprised me was...
It's importantIt carries the weight of...
I learned thatIt taught me that...
The cake was niceWhat made it special was the story behind it
I go walkingI follow the green lights
I think it's goodI personally care deeply about

词汇升级对照表

6分表达7分升级主题说明
really enjoy quite passionate about Art 从口语化"很享受"升级为更精确的情感表达
a great way to relax my go-to activity for unwinding Art/Evening 从泛泛的"好方法"升级为个人化、具象的表达
I think In my opinion / In my view 通用 从口语化"我觉得"升级为更正式的观点表达
very important important / significant 通用 形容词精确化
big significant 通用 模糊量词→精确形容词
because since 通用 因果连接词正式化
but however / that said 通用 转折词升级，增加让步层次
really truly / really 通用 程度副词精确化
people individuals 通用 名词正式化
kids children 通用 口语→书面
good excellent / impressive 通用 泛用形容词→精确评价
interesting fascinating / captivating 通用 情感强度升级
a lot of many / loads of 通用 量词正式化或口语高级化
helps me relax helps me switch off / unwind 通用 动词搭配升级
I don't really connect with I don't feel a strong connection to Art 否定表达扩展，更完整
find them quite boring find them quite repetitive / slow-paced Films/Sports 模糊评价→精确特征描述
I'd rather do something I prefer activities that are more 通用 从口语省略到完整从句
good way to deal with practical way to addressing 交通 动词搭配正式化
Another good way Another practical way 交通 形容词精确化

5个关键提升动作

  1. 加具体细节：不说"I like art"，说"I'm really into painting because you can see someone's inner world through their colors"
  2. 用What强调句：不说"I was surprised that..."，说"What surprised me was that..."
  3. 加反思收尾：每段结尾加"It taught me that..."或"It made me realize that..."
  4. 用对比结构："not just X, but Y" / "while X, I don't Y"
  5. 加感官与情感词：interesting, devastating, awe-inspiring, fulfilling

详细对比案例

案例 1：Art — Yes - Passionate Do you like art?
Band 6.0
Yes, I really enjoy art—it's a great way to express emotions and ideas without using words. I especially love visiting art galleries on weekends; it helps me relax and see the world from different views. Even though I'm not good at drawing myself, I still value the creativity and effort behind every piece.
Band 7.0
Absolutely, I'm quite passionate about art because it allows people to express complex emotions and thoughts in ways that words sometimes can't. On weekends, I often visit local galleries—it's become my go-to activity for unwinding and gaining fresh views on life. Although I'm not skilled at drawing or painting myself, I deeply admire the imagination and hard work artists put into their creations.

具体升级点：

  • Yes, I really enjoy → Absolutely, I'm quite passionate about（开场词升级+情感精确化）
  • a great way → allows people to...in ways that...（从泛评到机制描述）
  • helps me relax → my go-to activity for unwinding（个人化+搭配升级）
  • not good at drawing → not skilled at drawing or painting（扩展+精确化）
  • value → deeply admire（动词强度升级）
案例 2：Sports programs — Yes Do you like watching sports programs?
Band 6.0
Yes, I really enjoy sports programs. I especially like watching live football matches because the atmosphere is so intense and exciting. They also help me keep up with my favorite teams and players. Sometimes, I even watch highlights with my friends—it's a fun way to spend time together.
Band 7.0
Absolutely, I'm quite fond of sports programs. Live football matches are my favorite—they create such an electric atmosphere that you can't help but get caught up in the excitement. I also rely on sports coverage to stay informed about my favorite teams and athletes. And on a more social note, watching match highlights with friends has become a bit of a ritual for us; it's not just about the sport, but about sharing reactions and opinions in real time.

具体升级点：

  • really enjoy → quite fond of（搭配多样化）
  • the atmosphere is so intense → create such an electric atmosphere that...（从平铺到so...that结构）
  • help me keep up → rely on...to stay informed（动词搭配升级）
  • a fun way to spend time → a bit of a ritual for us; not just about...but about...（概念升级+not only...but also变体）
  • 新增 in real time 增加细节精确度
案例 3：交通拥堵 — Public Transport How can we solve traffic jams?
Band 6.0
I think improving public transportation is the best way to reduce traffic jams. If buses and subways are easy to use, not too expensive, and always on time, more people will take them instead of driving. For example, cities like Tokyo and Singapore have very good public transport systems.
Band 7.0
In my opinion, enhancing public transportation is the most effective long-term solution to traffic congestion. When public transit is convenient, affordable, and reliable—like frequent subway services or express buses—people are far more likely to leave their cars at home. Take Tokyo or Singapore as examples: despite being densely populated, their well-well-connected and efficient public transport networks keep road traffic surprisingly manageable.

具体升级点：

  • improving → enhancing（动词正式化）
  • best way → most effective long-term solution（概念精确化）
  • easy to use, not too expensive → convenient, affordable, and reliable（三词并列升级）
  • more people will take them → people are far more likely to leave their cars at home（从正面到反面，因果更完整）
  • very good → well-well-connected and efficient（形容词精确化）
  • 新增 despite being densely populated 让步从句
案例 4：安静的地方 — University Library Describe a quiet place
Band 6.0
The quietest place I like is the top floor of my university library. It's almost completely silent there, which is perfect for studying. I've known about it since my first year. Now, I go almost every weekday to work on assignments or prepare for exams.
Band 7.0
My go-to quiet place is the top floor of my university library—it's so silent you can almost hear a pin drop. I discovered it in my first year as a student, and it quickly became my sanctuary for deep work. I head there almost every weekday to tackle assignments or study for exams, and the peaceful atmosphere always helps me stay focused, calm, and surprisingly productive.

具体升级点：

  • The quietest place I like → My go-to quiet place（个人化表达）
  • almost completely silent → so silent you can almost hear a pin drop（夸张修辞增加生动性）
  • I've known about it → I discovered it（动词精确化）
  • perfect for studying → my sanctuary for deep work（概念升华）
  • work on → tackle（动词升级）
  • 新增 and the peaceful atmosphere always helps me...focused, calm, and surprisingly productive（三词并列+感受扩展）

提升路径总结

1
第一步：替换泛用词
把 good / bad / very / really / a lot of 替换为更精确的同义词
2
第二步：增加句型种类
在回答中加入 which 从句、Although 让步、Not only...but also 等结构
3
第三步：完善因果链
在 because 后补充 If...then 条件句或 which means... 后果句
4
第四步：分层使用连接词
按立场→因果→举例→让步→递进的逻辑层选择连接词
5
第五步：增加细节具体化
加入频率、地点、个人感受和比喻，让回答更有画面感
未找到匹配的内容，试试其他关键词
5篇故事 × 106个主题 × 331组思路 × 目标6.5分
